title: Designing and piloting a hybrid Micro-PBL activity for teaching velocity and acceleration in Year 9 STEM
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper reports the design and pilot implementation of a 50-minute hybrid Micro Project-Based Learning (Micro-PBL) STEM outreach activity developed to support Year 9 students’ perceived understanding of velocity, acceleration, and unit conversion through a combination of hands-on construction and digital simulation. Delivered as part of a STEM outreach initiative at Edith Cowan University, the activity engaged 36 students across two workshop sessions. Students constructed LEGO F1 mini cars, measured distance and time, calculated average velocity and acceleration under a uniform acceleration assumption, and performed unit conversions. Data were subsequently entered into a custom-built Streamlit application that simulated races, generated descriptive statistics, and visualised motion using velocity-time and distance-time graphs. This pilot pedagogical design study explored the feasibility of integrating physical experimentation, digital simulation, graphical visualisation, and gamification within a single 50-minute learning cycle. Data sources included classroom observations, student surveys, and qualitative feedback. Survey results indicated high levels of enjoyment (M = 4.38, SD = 0.65), willingness to recommend the activity to others (M = 4.44, SD = 0.75), and positive perceptions of the simulation’s support for visualising motion (M = 4.12, SD = 0.88). Observations and qualitative feedback indicated strong engagement during both the hands-on and simulation phases. Confidence in calculating velocity and acceleration was comparatively lower (M = 3.68, SD = 1.07), while students reported that the visualisations supported their interpretation of motion concepts. The findings provide preliminary evidence that hybrid Micro-PBL approaches can support student engagement and perceived conceptual understanding in secondary STEM education. The activity offers a practical model for STEM outreach and classroom innovation while identifying directions for future research on learning outcomes and cognitive load.</jats:p>

title: INTELLIGENT INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR SUPPORTING THE ACCELERATION OF INTERNATIONAL INNOVATIVE BUSINESS PROJECTS

items.abstract: <jats:p>The concept of intelligent acceleration – is substantiated as a process of reducing the time lag between environmental changes, their intelligent interpretation, decision-making and the implementation of managerial actions. A “data → intelligent analytics → scenarios → decisions → action → feedback” loop and a five-level architecture-comprising the Data Layer, Intelligence Layer, Scenario Layer, Decision Layer and Acceleration  Layer – are proposed. Areas of application for Big Data, artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, digital platforms and optimization technologies are identified. The synergistic interaction of systemic risks is taken into account. The scientific novelty lies in the systemic presentation of intelligent information technologies as a unified, adaptive mechanism for the economic acceleration of international innovation projects; this mechanism ensures a reduction in the management lag and enhances adaptability, decision quality and resource utilization efficiency. The proposed approach can be utilized to design the digital architecture of international innovation projects, develop intelligent decision support systems, assess systemic risks and optimize resources. A promising avenue for future research is the development of an integrated economic -mathematical model of intelligent acceleration that accounts for the speed of the innovation cycle, resource efficiency, adaptability and aggregate systemic risk.</jats:p>

<jats:p>
                    Magnetised plasma configurations in fusion devices are unavoidably subject to magnetic perturbations. Most notably, magnetic perturbations are intentionally applied in tokamaks to suppress edge localised modes (ELMs). However, despite growing confidence in the method, a complete understanding of the process involving all relevant mechanisms is yet to be gained. In this work, we present an integral kinetic plasma response model in the large-aspect-ratio limit capable of appropriately resolving finite Larmor radius effects of ions. Benchmarking against a prior differential model based on a finite Larmor expansion to second order demonstrates the necessity of the integral model due to unphysical modes in the solution of the former. Further, we investigate the isotope dependence of the linear plasma response in both approaches. We find that for identical plasma parameters, the linear response shows no significant variation between hydrogen and deuterium. Scanning the shielding current as a function of plasma rotation gives qualitatively different predictions for the ion resonance. While the finite Larmor radius expansion produces a narrow feature near the fluid resonance condition, the integral model reveals a substantially broader effective kinetic ion resonance shifted towards the condition where the

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In order to prepare for possible future operation of JT–60SA with tungsten plasma facing components, a H–mode scenario of JT–60SA at high power and high current is considered as reference in order to investigate the tungsten transport behavior and assess the amount of electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) which is predicted to be required in order to avoid central accumulation of tungsten. The modeling is performed with the ASTRA transport code in combination with the TGLF-SAT2 quasi–linear turbulent transport model and with neoclassical transport of impurities computed by the drift-kinetic solver NEO and the FACIT model. The impact of argon as additional seeded impurity is also considered, not only in the core behavior but also on the possibility of achieving tungsten screening in the pedestal region. The main result is that these H–mode conditions in JT–60SA achieve a so far largely unexplored domain of parameters, in which a reactor–like very low collisionality is combined with high rotation levels. In contrast to the usual domain of operation of present medium size tokamaks, where tungsten neoclassical transport is in the plateau to Pfirsch–Schlüter regime, in the predicted JT–60SA conditions toroidal rotation has a beneficial effect in increasing the strength of the temperature screening, enabling operation without any strong central tungsten accumulation and, in the most unfavorable conditions of high tungsten concentration and low rotation, requiring only 2 MW of central ECRH power to avoid locally negative electron heat fluxes in the center. Within the limited predictive capabilities of the present modeling approach for pedestal parameters, a sufficiently large and realistic domain of parameters in terms of argon concentration and plasma rotation, as well as of relative density and temperature logarithmic gradients, can also be expected to lead to the dominance of tungsten temperature screening in the JT–60SA pedestal.</jats:p>

title: Memory-dependent operating windows for photonic teleportation from a laser-driven spin–photon interface

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Generating entangled photons from a laser-driven spin provides a promising resource for quantum communication, but their usefulness can depend on how the surrounding nuclear environment evolves during photon generation. We investigate a spin–photon interface driven by finite laser pulses while retaining nuclear-spin dynamics across successive emission cycles. Measurements on the intermediate photons produce conditional endpoint states, whose entanglement, Bell correlations, teleportation fidelity, and expected detection rates are evaluated. By comparing dynamically evolving, frozen-field, and reset nuclear environments, we find that simplified noise models can predict different operating windows for useful teleportation. In particular, the frozen-field approximation may overestimate performance under the conditions studied. Optical branching, imperfect feedforward, and nuclear-register size further constrain these windows. The results establish a task-oriented framework for evaluating photonic resources while highlighting the need for accurate environmental modeling and device-specific calibration.</jats:p>

title: Standing wave interference pattern impact on generation dynamics in sigma-cavity lasers

affiliation.name: Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences
Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences
Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>A sigma-cavity laser configuration, consisting of ring and linear sections, is known to provide stable single-frequency (SF) generation. However, using an Er-doped fiber laser as an example we demonstrate that in addition to typical stable SF generation self-sweeping can occur even with moderate isolation of ∼37 dB provided in the ring section by a standard circulator. We demonstrate that the generation regime—SF stabilization, self-sweeping, or multi-frequency operation—can be controlled by introducing additional losses in the laser cavity. Depending on the specific point of the cavity where the losses are introduced, the sweeping rate can either increase or decrease with attenuation variation. The observed regimes are explained in terms of an extremely weak counter-propagating wave forming gain dynamic population grating in the ring section of the cavity. The results provide new insights into mode dynamics in sigma-cavity fiber lasers. They can be of use both for the task of mode-hopping suppression required for stable SF operation and for the task of controlling the self-sweeping rate for applications requiring wavelength tuning.</jats:p>

title: Effect of diode laser (532 nm) and Helium – Neon laser (632.8 nm) on the Activity of White Blood Cell

items.abstract: <jats:p>It is widely recognized that low-level laser irradiation affects immune system cells in various ways, one of which is enhancing the phagocytic activity of the treated cells. This study has been established to shed light on the possible effect of laser irradiation on phagocytic activity of W.B.Cs. Fresh blood samples have been obtained from 50 healthy adults volunteers for phagocytosis assay. The activity of W.B.C for whole blood have been measured at (5, 15, 30, 60, 90 and 120) min before and after exposure to laser He-Ne laser (632.8nm), Diode laser (532nm) irradiation. The present study revealed a significant increase in the mean activity of phagocytosis after exposure to 632.8 nm and 532nm, this activity further increased by increasing exposure time. The laser irradiation by 532 nm has been much more efficient; 30 minutes irradiation with 532 nm reached comparable and produced even better effects on the improvement of blood activity than the 60 min irradiation with 632.8 nm at significant level (P<0.05). The W.B. Cs count has been significantly increased by using 632.8 nm and 532 nm irradiation compared with non-irradiated group. (P<0.05). In conclusion, the current study suggests that low level laser can increase the phagocytic activity of W.B. Cs, and this increase is proportional to increasing the exposure time.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>During the operation of the tokamak device, the high heat load released by the core plasma instability events severely affects the structure and performance of tungsten-based divertor materials. For the expected Type I ELMs in future long-pulse steady-state fusion devices, the coaxial gun discharge plasma parameters are designed to simulate the characteristics of low-medium energy density. Under constant initial conditions (discharge frequency, gas-prefilled), the total accumulated heat flux is kept constant by varying the energy density and the number of pulses. By combining the plasma-material interaction process, the temperature evolution of tungsten (W) target under different heat loads and its damage effects are comparatively studied. The results show that when the total energy is fixed, the thermal deposition time scale and the instantaneous temperature gradient lead to different types of damage, including roughening, grain loss, blistering, crack networks, and cracking accompanied by melting. Low-energy-density multi-pulse impacts cause slow heat deposition and small temperature gradients, increasing surface roughness via cyclic thermal stress. High-energy-density impacts involving only a few pulses cause rapid heat deposition and steep temperature gradients, inducing high thermal stresses that lead to blistering and cracking. The energy density of an individual pulse determines the transition from surface to bulk damage. These results suggest that peak heat load control should take priority over cumulative heat flux limitation in the service design of W targets for fusion devices.</jats:p>

title: Effects of multi-port distributed injection attacks on unidimensional-modulation continuous-variable quantum key distribution in passive optical access networks

affiliation.name: Shanxi Vocational University of Engineering Science and Technology
Shanxi Vocational University of Engineering Science and Technology
Shanxi University of Finance and Economics

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Unidimensional-modulation (UD) continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has emerged as a promising approach to quantum-secure access networks because it requires comparatively simple and inexpensive hardware. Nevertheless, the resilience of multi-user UD CV-QKD systems to side-channel attacks has not been comprehensively investigated. This study proposes a multi-port distributed injection attacks model adapted to real deployment scenarios. A comprehensive theoretical model of the attack in broadcast architectures is established, and the asymptotic secret key rate is derived under the worst-case assumption that an eavesdropper controls all non-target users. The results demonstrate that the attack biases system parameter estimation, thereby causing overestimation of the secret key rate, and that the multi-user passive optical architecture intrinsically exacerbates this security threat. Furthermore, the analysis is extended to the practical finite-size regime and identifies a critical vulnerability, whereby the attack can induce the system to generate spurious secure keys even when the sample size is inadequate to yield any valid keys in the corresponding attack-free scenario. These findings demonstrate that the multi-port distributed injection attacks pose a significant practical security risk to real-world multi-user UD CV-QKD deployments, and offers valuable theoretical guidance for the security design of quantum-secure access networks.</jats:p>

title: Effect of laser power on the microstructure and microhardness of CpTi/TiC composites deposited on Ti6Al4V by laser metal deposition

affiliation.name: Department of Mechanical Engineering and Industrial Technology, University of Johannesburg
Department of Mechanical Engineering and Industrial Technology, University of Johannesburg

items.abstract: <jats:p>Laser Metal Deposition (LMD) is a laser-based additive manufacturing process used for the deposition of metallic materials and composites. The resulting microstructure and properties are influenced by processing conditions and material composition. This study investigates the combined influence of TiC reinforcement content and laser power on the microstructural characteristics and microhardness of commercially pure titanium (CpTi)/TiC composites deposited on Ti6Al4V substrates. Powder mixtures containing 10–40 wt.% TiC were deposited using a Yb-fibre LMD system at laser powers of 0.8 and 1.6 kW. The deposited composites were characterised using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Vickers microhardness testing. SEM observations revealed differences in the distribution of dispersed features, localised pore-like features, and acicular α/α′-type morphologies within the deposited layers under the investigated processing conditions. The deposited layers exhibited continuous deposit–substrate interfaces in the examined cross-sections, providing qualitative evidence of interfacial continuity. The Ti6Al4V substrate exhibited an average microhardness of 383 HV₀.₁, while the deposited composites exhibited microhardness values ranging from 364 to 460 HV₀.₁. The highest microhardness of 460 HV₀.₁ was obtained for the composite containing 40 wt.% TiC deposited at 1.6 kW. The results indicate that laser power and TiC reinforcement content jointly influence the microstructural characteristics and microhardness of LMD-produced CpTi/TiC composites.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Laser-induced graphene (LIG) provides a scalable, maskless route to porous carbon electrodes, but variability among independently fabricated devices and batches limits reliable manufacturing. Here, a controlled Ag/LIG workflow was used to examine how a one- to three-pass laser sequence affects material structure, electrochemical response, and fabrication reproducibility. SEM indicated pass-dependent network restructuring within the sampled fields, Raman spectroscopy showed greater but spatially nonuniform graphitic ordering, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated greater sp2 character and modest surface deoxygenation with repeated laser exposure. Three-pass electrodes produced an approximately 2.3-fold higher square-wave voltammetric response than one-pass electrodes in ferri/ferrocyanide solution. Cyclic voltammetry, impedance spectroscopy, and direct resistance measurements on representative electrodes showed that the largest resistance decrease occurred between one and two passes, whereas conditional apparent electroactive area continued to increase, with the larger increment occurring between two and three passes; charge-transfer resistance remained comparatively small and showed no systematic dependence on pass number. Reproducibility of the selected three-pass process was evaluated using 18 devices from three fabrication batches and 162 voltammograms: scan-to-scan relative SD was below 0.5%, while device-within-batch and batch relative SDs were 2.6–3.6% and 2.0–4.4%, respectively. These results link controlled multipass processing to staged improvements in electrical transport and electrochemical accessibility and provide a hierarchical framework for quantifying the fabrication reproducibility of porous carbon electrodes.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>A self-consistent two-dimensional numerical model of an inductively coupled plasma (ICP) discharge in helium and He/SiH4 mixtures was developed to investigate the temporal evolution of charged and neutral species and the formation of a strongly electronegative plasma core. The model couples the RF electromagnetic field with plasma-chemical kinetics, charged-particle transport, electron energy balance, electrostatic potential, and gas heating. Particular attention was paid to the influence of negative-ion chemistry on the formation and evolution of the electronegative plasma core. Numerical simulations were performed using two alternative kinetic schemes: one including the formation of SiH4− and another excluding this channel while accounting for H− formation. The results demonstrate that a strongly electronegative central region develops in both kinetic schemes, although its formation time and spatial characteristics differ significantly. At an input power of 750 W and a pressure of 0.2 Torr, the maximum electronegativity reaches approximately 36.84 at 100 s when SiH4− formation is included, compared with 16.51 in the alternative model. The corresponding axial widths of the region satisfying α > 1 are approximately 1.97 and 1.56 cm, respectively. The accumulation of negative ions is accompanied by a pronounced redistribution of the self-consistent electric field and the formation of a broad low-field region in the discharge center. Analysis of neutral-species densities and estimated incident thermal fluxes reveals that atomic hydrogen and SiH are the dominant dissociation products of silane in both kinetic schemes, whereas SiH2, SiH3, and atomic silicon exhibit greater sensitivity to the adopted reaction mechanism. These findings demonstrate that the formation of a strongly electronegative plasma core is preserved under the investigated changes in negative-ion chemistry, while its quantitative characteristics and the relative availability of reactive species depend on the adopted kinetic scheme. The results provide insight into the formation and evolution of the electronegative plasma core and the production of reactive species under conditions relevant to silicon.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate intraoperative identification of tumor boundaries remains a major challenge in surgical oncology, particularly for infiltrative tumors, anatomically constrained lesions, and cancers adjacent to critical vessels, nerves, or functional tissues. Conventional visual inspection, palpation, and preoperative imaging may provide insufficient or outdated information once tissue deformation and surgical manipulation occur. Optical methods can provide real‐time structural, molecular, metabolic, and functional contrast across multiple spatial scales, supporting tumor localization, subsurface margin assessment, localized tissue characterization, and preservation of critical anatomy. This review examines intraoperative optical guidance from a decision‐oriented perspective, organizing current technologies according to the surgical questions they are best positioned to address, from wide‐field localization to depth‐resolved assessment and microscopic or molecular characterization. By comparing the complementary strengths and limitations of these approaches across spatial scales, this review highlights how optical guidance may be tailored to different intraoperative decisions, while also identifying the technical and clinical barriers that continue to limit broader translation.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Single-shot laser-induced dot transfer (LIDT) with a femtosecond-laser interference pattern deposits periodic metal nanodot arrays from a donor film onto a receiver. We examined the effects of receiver material and ambient pressure. A 40 nm Au film on silica was irradiated by one shot of a four-beam interference pattern (785 nm, 240 fs, spacing of the intensity maxima 3.6 µm) at an estimated nominal average fluence of 77 mJ/cm2, and dots deposited on a 40 nm Au film, Si(100) and synthetic silica in vacuum (<3 kPa) and on the Au film in air were quantified by automated particle analysis of scanning electron micrographs. The number of dots decreased in the order Au film (431) > Si (88) > silica (51); the dots on Si had the largest diameter (600 ± 37 nm, mean ± standard deviation), and those on silica formed a ring with an empty centre. Dense arrays were deposited on Si (86 and 97 mJ/cm2) and sapphire (86 mJ/cm2). In air, the numbers of dots (302) and of sites with stacked dots (3 versus 21) were lower. The results suggest that adhesion of molten Au to the receiver and the ambient gas govern the deposition.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Photonic time crystals are spatially uniform media whose material parameters vary periodically in time, opening momentum bandgaps within which the fields of electromagnetic modes can grow exponentially in time. To date, most studies on such crystals have utilized only passive materials with “positive” dispersion (satisfying Foster's reactance theorem). Here we propose a theoretical framework of photonic time crystals based on active materials with “negative” dispersion (non‐Foster materials). We explore two representative classes of isotropic non‐Foster photonic time crystals: a bulk medium with time‐modulated effective permittivity and a metasurface whose surface capacitance is switched in time. We show that an ideal lossless and dispersionless non‐Foster model can produce exceptionally broad momentum bandgaps, with amplification rates increase approximately linearly with momentum and the ability to amplify direct‐current (DC) waves. To move beyond this idealized limit, we further introduce a causal finite‐bandwidth Lorentz/inverted‐Lorentz model. Similar results are found in this model but with truncated bandgaps and conditional DC amplification. These results extend the theory of photonic time crystals to active non‐Foster reactive responses, providing a route to Floquet engineering and a more complete understanding of wave–matter interactions in time‐varying media.</jats:p>

Titanium (Ti) has favourable properties for numerous applications, and Ti parts produced using LPBF are at the forefront of several industry applications. items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: It remains unclear whether the associations of lower-carbohydrate and lower-fat dietary patterns with cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) outcomes vary according to the quality and food sources of macronutrients. Methods: We analyzed 9165 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999–2018, comparing overall, healthy and unhealthy lower-carbohydrate diet (LCD) and lower-fat diet (LFD) scores derived from dietary recalls. Outcomes included advanced CKM syndrome and all-cause, cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular mortality. Analyses included survey-weighted logistic and Cox regression, restricted cubic splines and exploratory mediation analyses. Results: Overall LCD and LFD scores were not significantly associated with advanced CKM or mortality. Higher healthy LCD scores were associated with lower odds of advanced CKM, whereas higher unhealthy LFD scores were associated with higher odds. In the prospective sample, 591 deaths occurred over 70,333 person-years of follow-up. Per 5-point increase in the dietary score, healthy LFD was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.79–0.99), whereas unhealthy LCD was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.00–1.23). Systemic inflammation and biological age acceleration emerged as potential mediators of the association between the healthy LFD score and all-cause mortality. Conclusions: These findings suggest that macronutrient quality and food sources may be more informative for CKM outcomes than carbohydrate or fat restriction alone and highlight the potential importance of considering plant-based protein, high-quality carbohydrates, and unsaturated fats when evaluating dietary patterns.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage (HICH) are neurological disorders associated with high incidence and disability rates, while current therapeutic strategies remain limited. There is an urgent clinical need for highly specific, convenient, and efficient biomarkers, as well as innovative diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma samples were collected from patients with AIS, patients with HICH, and healthy controls. Plasma exosomes were isolated, and differentially expressed long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) were screened using lncRNA microarrays and validated by qRT-PCR. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of candidate lncRNAs for the early identification of AIS and HICH. Correlations between candidate lncRNAs and disease severity and prognosis were assessed in combination with National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale and modified Rankin Scale scores.</jats:p>
                    <jats:p>Bioinformatics analyses were conducted to predict target genes and identify relevant biological functions and signaling pathways through Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses. Furthermore, siRNA interference was used to investigate potential molecular regulatory mechanisms at the cellular level.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A series of differentially expressed plasma exosomal lncRNAs were identified. Several candidate lncRNAs, including NONHSAT016392 for AIS and NONHSAG074724 for HICH, showed satisfactory diagnostic performance, with areas under the ROC curve ranging from 0.7898 to 0.9524.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Specific plasma exosomal lncRNAs may serve as promising biomarkers for the early diagnosis and prognostic assessment of AIS and HICH. These findings also provide a basis for elucidating key molecular pathways involved in disease onset and progression and for developing novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for cerebrovascular diseases.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                  <jats:p>Articular cartilage has a limited capacity for self‐repair, which makes the development of functional scaffolds essential for regeneration. In this study, a polylactic acid (PLA)‐based scaffold was fabricated using a jet spray method, similar to the commercial Powerbone Chondro Matrix without hyaluronic acid, and functionalized with bioactive peptides, the collagen‐binding peptide (CBP) WYRGRL and the collagen‐mimetic peptide (CMP) GFOGER, through cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) surface treatment. CAP increased the hydrophilicity of the scaffold surface, enabling efficient peptide conjugation. Glycosaminoglycan (GAG) analysis, total collagen quantification, and Alcian Blue staining demonstrated that peptide‐functionalized scaffolds significantly enhanced chondrogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) compared with unconjugated groups. Furthermore, qPCR analysis exhibited a significant increase in gene expression of the chondrogenic markers Aggrecan (ACAN), SOX9, and Collagen Type II (COL II), while immunofluorescence staining confirmed a pronounced increase in ACAN and COL II protein levels. These results demonstrate that CAP‐mediated peptide modification of the Powerbone Chondro Matrix enhances the proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs), providing a promising strategy for cartilage tissue engineering.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable bonding between specialty optical fibers and coated silica substrates remains challenging because of the thermal sensitivity of optical coatings and fiber microstructures and the limited contact area. This study proposes a localized CO2 laser-assisted hydroxide-catalysis bonding method combined with a quartz-sleeve-nested structure to improve bonding reliability while limiting thermal impact. The quartz sleeve is polished coplanar with the fiber end face to improve bonding strength and precision. A three-dimensional transient heat-transfer model is established based on finite element analysis to optimize the laser-heating parameters, and bonding experiments are conducted under vacuum using four symmetrically arranged CO2 laser beams. The simulation results show that a total laser power of 0.8 W produces a bonding-region temperature of approximately 235 °C, with an in-plane temperature difference of less than 20 °C. Experimental characterization reveals a continuous bonding interface without obvious bubbles, cracks, or macroscopic deformation. The bonded samples exhibit an average optical path difference of approximately 8.9 nm and an average fracture strength of 5.05 MPa. Furthermore, seven-channel optical transmission tests confirm that all channels retain their basic optical transmission functionality after bonding. These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining localized CO2 laser heating with hydroxide-catalysis bonding for the integration of specialty optical fibers and coated silica substrates with reduced thermal impact.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigated the effects of plasma treatment on the dyeing performance of cotton fabrics dyed with a natural dye extracted from almond leaf (Terminalia catappa L.) with a material-to-liquor ratio (1:20) for 20 minutes using the microwave-assisted extraction method. The extracted dye liquors were applied to plasma-treated and untreated cotton fabrics. Dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma treatment was performed at atmospheric pressure at three different voltages (10, 15, and 20 kV) and three different frequencies (15, 20, and 25 kHz). Colour characteristics were evaluated for colour strength (K/S), CIELAB colour coordinates values, and colour fastness to washing, rubbing, and light.  Among the dyed samples, sample PA22 showed the highest K/S value (16.1). The dyed fabrics exhibited predominantly yellowish shades, with fair to moderate washing fastness, moderate to good resistance to staining on adjacent cotton fabric, and moderate light fastness (grade 3). Wet rubbing fastness ranged from fair to moderate, while dry rubbing fastness ranged from fair to good. These findings indicate that dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma treatment affects the dyeing performance of cotton fabrics dyed with almond leaf extract.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Titanium nanoparticles are important in powder technology, additive manufacturing, catalysis, and biomedical fields due to their high surface area, reactivity, corrosion resistance, and strength-to-weight ratio. Managing particle size and clumping during large-scale production remains challenging. This study develops a coupled Multiphysics framework for investigating titanium nanoparticle during plasma-assisted vapor condensation, by integrating computational fluid dynamics with the Population Balance Model using the Direct Quadrature Method of Moments. It models gas flow, heat transfer, turbulence, nucleation, growth, and particle size changes. ANSYS Fluent solves flow and thermal fields, while formulas calculate particle number density, cell particle count, and size distributions. Results show a plasma core at about 6.20×10³ K, with rapid downstream cooling that promotes nanoparticle formation. Turbulence enhances mixing and heat transfer; particles slightly reduce thermal conductivity and turbulence in some areas. Smaller particles dominate the number-based distribution, while larger particles impact the mass-based distribution. The framework provides a quantitative basis for relating reactor thermal and flow conditions to nanoparticle number density, characteristic diameter, and particle size distribution.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Laser metal deposition (LMD) of 17-4 PH stainless steel produces a thermally softened heat-affected zone (HAZ) that compromises repaired components. Hardness recovery across the clad–HAZ–substrate region was characterised following sub-critical localised laser-based heat treatment (LBHT) at peak surface temperatures of 480–498 °C. Vickers microhardness increased in every zone, most in the HAZ: from 328.3 ± 20.6 HV to 411.0 ± 12.5 HV (+82.7 HV), within the reported H900 range. Hardness scatter decreased throughout. SEM/EDS resolved no change in bulk Cu of the HAZ (2.75–3.46 wt% before, 2.73–3.33 wt% after), so the hardness increase must reflect solute redistribution below the resolution of EDS. Nb-rich particles (up to 4.25 wt% Nb), present in both conditions, are interpreted as markers of solidification microsegregation rather than the primary strengthening agent. The behaviour is consistent with ε-Cu precipitation, the established mechanism in this ageing window, but this is inferred rather than observed: no TEM, EBSD, XRD or atom probe analysis was performed. LBHT recovers HAZ hardness without full-component solution treatment, supporting its use as a targeted route for LMD repair.</jats:p>

title: Smartphone vs. laser meter for DBH measurement: distance-dependent accuracy and operational time efficiency in temperate forests
items.abstract: <jats:p>Aim of study: This study aimed to assess the accuracy and operational time efficiency of smartphone-based diameter at breast height (DBH) measurements compared with a laser meter and traditional calipers. The research specifically evaluated how measurement distance influences accuracy and identified optimal field protocols for temperate forest inventories. Area of study: The study was conducted in temperate mixed forests in the Bursa Region of northwestern Türkiye. Material and methods: A total of 240 trees representing eight temperate species (DBH 8.3–65.9 cm) were measured using three tools: caliper (reference), iPhone Measure app (smartphone), and a handheld laser meter. DBH and measurement time were recorded at four distances: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 m. Accuracy was evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), R2 and Percent Bias (PBIAS), and differences among methods were tested statistically. Main results: Smartphone measurements at 2.0 m showed high accuracy (RMSE = 0.62 cm; R2= 0.992; PBIAS = 0.08%), yielding values statistically equivalent to caliper results (26.85 vs. 26.57 cm, p > 0.05). Both smartphone and laser tools underestimated DBH at 0.5 m (smartphone: –1.81 cm; laser: –3.12 cm) but were comparable to calipers at distances ≥ 1.0 m. Smartphone measurements required 40% less time than calipers (3.04 vs. 4.99 s) and 79% less time than laser meters (14.58 s), with low variability (Standard Deviation, SD = 1.24 s). Accuracy remained stable across species (RMSE: 0.78–1.42 cm). Research highlights: Measurement distance strongly influences digital DBH accuracy, with 2.0 m providing optimal performance. Smartphone tools offer a fast, accurate, and cost-effective alternative for operational forest inventory.</jats:p>

Differential expression, functional enrichment, correlations with hematoma volume and Glasgow Coma Scale scores, competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network construction, protein-coding potential prediction, and RNA-binding protein analyses were performed.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 352 differentially expressed lncRNAs were identified, including 76 upregulated and 276 downregulated lncRNAs, widely distributed across all chromosomes. Functional enrichment linked these lncRNAs to PI3K-Akt signaling, neuromuscular function, and Hsp90 protein binding. Ten lncRNAs strongly correlated with hematoma volume and Glasgow Coma Scale scores and were integrated into a ceRNA network implicating target genes in cell cycle regulation, immune response, and axon guidance. Notably, 12.9% of differentially expressed lncRNAs showed protein-coding potential, with high-confidence candidates enriched in mitochondrial function, small GTPase signaling, and NLRP3 inflammasome assembly. RNA-binding protein analysis highlighted TIA1, TIAL1, and ELAVL family members as key regulators.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study reveals a HICH-specific plasma exosomal lncRNA signature and identifies novel candidates for early biomarkers, while providing insights into the molecular mechanisms driving disease progression.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The local reaction environment at electrified interfaces governs charge transfer, reaction kinetics, and selectivity across a wide range of electrochemical systems; however, it remains difficult to quantify due to the strong coupling between interfacial electrostatics and multiscale mass transport. Numerical simulation provides an effective approach to quantitatively resolving such complex reaction environments. However, commonly used reduced descriptions generally focus on either near-field or far-field transport, thereby missing their mutual coupling and yielding different predictions of ion concentration profiles in the local reaction environment. Here, using the cathodic alkaline water splitting as a representative system, we develop a multiscale full-field transport framework and uncover a pronounced hydroxide accumulation region, characterized by a concentration peak that can exceed the bulk concentration by two orders of magnitude within tens of nanometers of the electrode surface. We further demonstrate that electrolyzer geometry and electrode size exert distinct and systematic control over the local reaction environment. Electrolyzer geometry primarily regulates far-field transport resistance and hydroxide evacuation, whereas electrode size shapes near-field electric-field structure and migration pathways, jointly determining the magnitude and localization of the hydroxide peak. Guided by these insights, we derive a scaling relationship linking peak hydroxide concentration to geometric parameters and operating current density, enabling rapid estimation of the local reaction environment without full multiscale simulation. Together, these results establish geometry-mediated transport as a practical design lever for engineering the local reaction environment in electrochemical systems, with direct implications for multiscale and first-principles modeling of electrochemical interfaces.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Radiotherapy (RT) improves survival in breast cancer but often causes acute radiation dermatitis. In severe cases, moist desquamation (MD), a painful loss of epidermal integrity that impairs comfort and quality of life, can occur. This prospective observational study described healing time to Grade 1, symptom changes, and patient experiences among breast cancer patients with radiation-induced MD managed with Mepilex dressings. Methods: Ten breast cancer patients (aged 49–84 years; mean 58.3) who developed grade 2 to 4 MD on an investigator-designed scale during or after adjuvant RT were enrolled and followed until healing. Dressings were applied by oncology nurses and changed every 2 to 3 days. Nurses had the option to apply Mepilex Lite, Mepilex Border Flex Lite, or Mepilex Ag, with the latter reserved for heavier exudation or suspected infection. Parallel patient- and clinician-reported grading tools, 10-item symptom questionnaires, and photographic documentation were used at each dressing change. The primary endpoint was time to MD resolution, defined as the interval from the first study dressing application to the first assessment documenting Grade 1 MD. Secondary endpoints included symptom trajectories and patient satisfaction. Results: The mean healing time to Grade 1 was 10.4 days (median 10; range 7–19) after application of Mepilex dressings. Three patients used Mepilex Ag. Scores for pain, tenderness, burning, and hypersensitivity decreased, while itch and edema showed minimal change. Nurse-reported assessments showed similar patterns of change across several symptom domains. Patients reported high satisfaction with Mepilex dressings, citing comfort, reduced friction, and improved daily function. As this was an uncontrolled observational study, symptom and healing changes cannot be attributed to Mepilex dressings independently of natural healing, prior or concurrent treatments, or other aspects of care. Conclusions: These findings provide preliminary information on the clinical course and patient experience of MD during Mepilex-based wound care. Further comparative studies are needed to evaluate the contribution of these dressings to symptom relief and wound healing.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Periodic, batch-based public financial reporting in developing countries weakens accountability, yet little is known about whether public institutions are ready to adopt permissioned blockchain for real-time reporting. This study examines how technological, human capital, regulatory and legal, organisational, leadership and political will, and data security and privacy readiness shape adoption readiness intent for permissioned blockchain-based financial reporting in Ghana's public sector, an issue central to accountable and transparent institutions (SDG 16) and resilient digital infrastructure and innovation (SDG 9). The study uses survey data from 300 officials in ministries, local government authorities, state-owned enterprises and regulatory bodies, selected through proportional stratified sampling and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling and one-way ANOVA. The results show that all six dimensions have significant positive effects on adoption readiness intent: technological readiness (β = 0.312, p < 0.001), human capital readiness (β = 0.274, p < 0.001), organisational readiness (β = 0.221, p < 0.001), regulatory and legal readiness (β = 0.198, p < 0.001), leadership and political will (β = 0.189, p < 0.001) and data security and privacy readiness (β = 0.163, p = 0.001). The model explains 69.3% of the variance in adoption readiness intent (R² = 0.693; Q² = 0.481). The findings suggest that infrastructure and skills drive readiness most strongly, that readiness is weakest in data security and privacy (M = 3.48) and the legal framework (M = 3.54), and that Greater Accra institutions score 0.67 points above Upper Region institutions on technological readiness.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Emission factors (EFs) of trace gases and particulate matter are essential for accurate air quality modelling, but can vary with vegetation type, fuel moisture content and combustion conditions. This study aimed to determine the influence of fuel type and moisture content on the EFs of carbon dioxide (CO2), carbon monoxide (CO), methane (CH4), non-methane hydrocarbons (NMHCs), formaldehyde (CH2O), total suspended particles (TSP) and fine particulate matter (PM2.5). Laboratory-scale experimental burns were conducted on four Australian vegetation types: eucalypt leaf litter, mallee heath, pine needles, and banksia (leaves and seeds). Fuels were conditioned to moisture contents from 5% to 30%, incorporating typical fuel moisture conditions for wildfires and planned burns. Fuel type explained more of the EF variability (19–72%) than fuel moisture content (≤14%). Most importantly, eucalypt leaf litter was the only fuel whose emissions consistently increased with fuel moisture: at levels typical of planned burns (~12.5% fuel moisture) rather than wildfires (~5% fuel moisture), its EFs were ~65% higher for PM2.5 (95% confidence interval: 34–94%), ~50% higher for TSP and ~25% higher for CO, consistent with a shift towards smouldering combustion (lower modified combustion efficiency). Incorporating both fuel type and moisture content for eucalypt fuels can improve emission estimates in fire smoke modelling in Australia.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The electrochemical nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) is proposed to be one of the most promising and practical methods to synthesize ammonia in ambient environments. Single-atom catalysts have been investigated broadly from both experimental and theoretical points of view. In this article, a series of molybdenum- and sulfur-codoped graphene structures (dopants: MoSn, n = 1–3) are studied to evaluate their performance in the NRR. Energy and wave function analysis results show that the side-on N2 configuration on MoSn@gra shows better potential. At the same time, the side-on configuration is extraordinarily stable in Mo,S-doped graphene (Mo-gra-1) with a proportion of 97.07% calculated by Boltzmann distribution. Furthermore, Mo-gra-1 possesses the best coordination environment among the selected structures, showing the best performance with merely 0.20 V applied potential needed. Therefore, carefully controlling the proportions of Mo and S on defective graphene, especially around 1:1, will achieve the best efficiency in N2 fixation and the NRR.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Glycolaldehyde (GA), glyoxal, and methylglyoxal are precursors of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), which play a role in the pathobiology of diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer. In a model system of inflammation, GA was generated from serine by myeloperoxidases. GA has been detected in cigarette smoke and the atmosphere, and GA-containing flavoring products are manufactured by the food industry. GA exhibits mutagenic activity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To clarify the mechanism of its mutagenicity, its reactions with five deoxynucleosides were examined. In the dG reaction, the glyoxal-related adducts 1,N2-glyoxal-dG and N2-carboxymethyl-dG were detected. In the 5-methyl-dC reaction, 5-methylcytosine, 5-formyl-dC, and dT were formed. Cytosine and dU were produced during the dC reaction. Base release was predominant in the dT and dA reactions. The autooxidation of GA to glyoxal and the generation of reactive oxygen species were considered as mechanisms underlying these reactions. These modifications, if present in DNA, may induce gene mutations and epigenetic alterations. Next, we focused on the detection of GA in food. High GA levels were detected in carbohydrate-rich and heat-processed foods. To our knowledge, this is the first report of the detection of GA in food.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results suggest that, in addition to endogenous and environmental GA, dietary GA may also affect physiological AGE levels or induce DNA damage and enhance the risk of various diseases, including cancer.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) is an emerging noninvasive treatment for refractory ventricular tachycardia when conventional therapies are ineffective or unsuitable. Recent clinical studies have shown substantial reductions in arrhythmia burden with acceptable early toxicity, although treatment responses are heterogeneous and recurrent ventricular tachycardia remains common. The biological mechanisms underlying STAR remain uncertain, with electrical remodeling, inflammation and edema, and delayed fibrosis proposed as potential contributors. The widely used single dose of 25 Gy has not been validated in formal dose-finding studies. Although advances in cardiac imaging have improved myocardial scar characterization, determining the appropriate treatment volume and radiation dose remains challenging. Integration of electroanatomic mapping and multimodal cardiac imaging with radiotherapy planning is feasible, but uncertainties in target delineation and image registration remain. Long-term safety is insufficiently characterized, particularly regarding injury to cardiac and adjacent extracardiac structures. STAR should therefore remain a multidisciplinary, protocol-based treatment requiring standardized planning, dose optimization, and longer prospective follow-up.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Vertical wind variations link surface conditions with the overlying airflow and help characterize aeolian forcing in the Kumtag Desert. Existing field observations describe winds close to the ground, but how the timing of wind-speed peaks and the spatial extent of stronger winds change with height remains unclear. This study examined vertical variations in wind speed and direction from 10 to 200 m above ground in the Kumtag Desert across selected periods and terrain settings. We used the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model driven by the fifth-generation European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts reanalysis (ERA5). Evaluation against 10 m wind speeds at Mangya and Dunhuang stations guided the selection of four five-day periods, totaling 20 days. Hourly wind speeds and directions were extracted at 20 heights from 10 to 200 m above ground level, at 10 m intervals. Above 10 m, the winds were interpolated from the diagnostic 10 m wind and the native mass-level winds. Regional-mean profiles, spatial distributions and local profiles were compared. Regional-mean wind speed increased from 10 to 150 m in all four periods. The largest increase occurred between 10 and 20 m, with weaker increases between 80 and 150 m. Between 150 and 200 m, speeds remained nearly constant or decreased slightly in spring and autumn but increased slightly in summer and winter. Summer had the highest speeds at every height. Winter ranked lowest at 10 m but second highest at 200 m, where wind speed was 1.443 times its 10 m value. Diurnal peaks shifted from 14:00 to 19:00 Beijing Time (BJT, UTC + 8) at 10 m to nighttime or early morning at 200 m. The diurnal wind-speed amplitude, defined as the range of the 24 h composite, generally increased with height. Strong winds persisted over the southern highlands, while stronger lowland winds became more widespread aloft. The increase in mean wind speed from 10 to 200 m differed among the four local analysis windows. At a given height, the ranking of the four representative periods by mean wind speed varied among windows.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>We propose an algebraically corrected finite volume element method for convection-diffusion-reaction problems on general triangular meshes. A solution-dependent symmetric correction matrix is added to the algebraic system. The matrix is constructed with a symmetric upwind-type limiter, which is modified so that no extrapolation across the interface is performed at interface nodes when the diffusion coefficient is discontinuous. We prove that, for problems with both smooth and discontinuous diffusion coefficients, the resulting nonlinear scheme admits a solution and satisfies the discrete maximum principle without any mesh condition. We also establish the coercivity of the corrected scheme and derive an optimal $H^1$ error estimate for smooth diffusion coefficients, under a weakly acute mesh condition that is needed only in the diffusion-dominated regime. Numerical experiments show that the method achieves the optimal $H^1$ and $L^2$ convergence rates and confirm the discrete maximum principle.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>In this paper, focusing on the interaction between UO2 and liquid sodium in the presence of dissolved oxygen, the original experimental setup is used to determine the change in the corrosion layer thickness over time under controlled conditions. Experimental evidence of the outward growth mechanism of the trisodium uranate is provided, based on the markers’ method. The formalism of heterogeneous kinetics is used to model the reaction. <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In water treatment, one of the most intriguing modern controversies revolves around whether magnetic fields can affect the molecular and bulk properties of aqueous solutions. Of particular interest are changes in water surface tension and viscosity, as well as the scaling potential of mineral-laden waters. The experimental literature has remained inconclusive about the mechanisms underlying these effects, proposing that interactions occur but remaining vague about the possible mechanisms. This has led to a discrepancy between experimental observations and theory, hindering the adoption of these treatment approaches. In this work, we quantify the effects of magnetic treatment on aqueous solutions in a controlled system and critically examine proposed mechanistic interpretations. We find that experiments reveal changes in pH, ORP, dynamic viscosity, density, and microbubble and nanobubble populations in response to an applied magnetic field. Dissolved gas in the solution dramatically alters the response profile. We also observe long-lived effects (~12 h) commonly termed magnetic memory. We then demonstrate that a simple linear or quadratic model describing interactions between the water or gases in the system and the magnetic treatment does not adequately capture the observed effects. From this, we postulate that magnetic interactions with the hydrogen-bonding network best describe the observed effects.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>A sampled Lorentz-adapted Parseval frame is constructed from smooth boostlet windows on the timelike and spacelike branches of the 2D Fourier plane. For the massive Klein–Gordon field, the real field is extended complex linearly and the Pauli–Jordan form is kept bilinear. This convention yields an antisymmetric boostlet commutator matrix and an exact rapidity-integral representation pairing opposite energy branches. Spacelike-separated centers give entrywise decay of every algebraic order in invariant distance. Timelike-separated centers select the rapidity of the connecting four-vector, with a uniform stationary-phase expansion away from rapidity-tile boundaries. Causal sparsity is formulated as a quantitative entrywise threshold property, supplemented by exact scale and branch zeros. A Sobolev coefficient-summability criterion gives mass-shell convergence of finite frame truncations for a restricted class whose Fourier transforms have vanishing trace on the null lines, and hence gives controlled finite-matrix approximation of the commutator form on that class. The boostlet estimates are consistent with the established causal wavefront geometry of the state-independent propagator.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Reaction time is a vital neuromotor skill influencing athletic performance, particularly in sports that demand rapid responses to visual stimuli. Among the various measures of reaction time, the Nelson’s hand reaction time test is a standardized tool commonly used to evaluate upper limb responsiveness. Badminton and cricket involve distinct physical and cognitive demands, which may result in differences in reaction time profiles among athletes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To compare hand reaction time, as measured by the Nelson’s hand reaction time test, between recreational badminton players and recreational cricket players, and to determine which sport is associated with superior neuromuscular reactivity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methodology:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional comparative study was conducted involving 40 male recreational athletes aged 18–25 years with healthy body mass index (BMI), comprising 20 badminton and 20 cricket players. Reaction time was measured using the Nelson’s hand ruler method. Each participant completed ten trials, and the mean of the total responses was recorded. An independent sample t – test was applied to compare mean values between the group analysis and BMI was considered a confounding variable and was controlled using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA).</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>An innovative dual‐wideband dual‐polarized antenna with a shared‐aperture scheme is introduced for mobile communications. A patch antenna is excited via microstrip‐to‐slotline baluns for the generation of a wide lower frequency band, while a crossed‐dipole antenna loaded on the patch is introduced to realize a wide upper frequency band. Furthermore, to optimize impedance matching and keep the radiation patterns stable across the lower and upper operating bands, metallic baffles are introduced. A prototype is designed, fabricated, and measured. It achieves dual‐wide operating bands of 0.68–0.96 GHz (34.1%) and 1.66–2.73 GHz (48.7%), in‐band port isolation beyond 30 dB, and steady half‐power beamwidths of 65° ± 6° and 77° ± 9° corresponding to the lower and upper bands, respectively. The antenna possesses excellent impedance matching, high in‐band isolation, low cross‐polarization, stable radiation patterns, and a relatively compact form factor, which makes it well‐suited for base station application scenarios.</jats:p>

<jats:p>Subject. This article discusses the emerging system of knowledge about the digital ruble protection as a State monetary form, payment infrastructure and the institution of public trust. 
Objectives. The study aims to substantiate the definition of the digital ruble cybersecurity as an independent interdisciplinary field of knowledge, and define its object, subject, boundaries, axiomatic provisions, categorical apparatus and methodological basis.
Methods. For the study, I used the methods of systems, structural-functional, institutional and risk-based approaches, conceptualization, comparative analysis, and targeted content analysis. 
Results. The article proposes the author's definition of the cybersecurity of the digital ruble, and formulates its axiomatic provisions. It also establishes that Russian and international studies are not combined into an independent subject, and introduces an interconnected system of categories.
Conclusions. The independence of the new field is confirmed by a specific object, an integrative research question, its own categories and methodology. The results provide the basis for standards, cyber resilience indicators, scenario testing, applied research, and specialist training.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Radiant energy density, defined as radiated heat energy per unit erupted volume, is widely used to estimate erupted volume from thermal observations of lava domes, but its marked decrease with silica content remains poorly understood. Conventional radiation models assume vertically uniform temperatures and steady thermal conditions, yet cannot explain the observed low radiant energy density, indicating that transient surface cooling must be considered. Air cooling forms a cooled thermal boundary layer at the upper lava surface, referred to here as a surface skin, while the interior remains hot. We develop a shallow‐layer model that couples unsteady surface‐skin growth with viscoplastic spreading and computes radiative heat flux across ranges of silica content and thermal conductivity. The model identifies two regimes: high thermal conductivity, in which conduction homogenizes temperature across the dome thickness, and low thermal conductivity, in which cooling remains confined to the thin surface skin. In the low‐conductivity regime, total radiative heat loss is primarily controlled by radiating surface area. Silica‐rich lava has greater yield strength and spreads over a smaller area, resulting in lower radiant energy density. Timescale comparisons indicate that natural lava domes typically fall within the low‐conductivity regime, and the observed decrease in radiant energy density for silica‐rich lava aligns with model predictions. These results demonstrate that accounting for surface‐skin formation and yield‐strength‐governed spreading is essential for estimating lava volume from thermal observations.</jats:p>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To develop and internally validate a machine learning-based predictive model for radiation dermatitis (RD) in cervical cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 251 cervical cancer patients receiving pelvic external beam radiotherapy were prospectively enrolled and randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a 7:3 ratio. In the training set, LASSO regression was used to select predictors, and four models—logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and XGBoost—were constructed. Hyperparameter tuning was performed using grid search, model stability was assessed via 5-fold cross-validation, and DeLong tests were used to compare AUC differences among models. Model performance was evaluated in the validation set using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, precision, and F1 score. Calibration of the optimal model was assessed using calibration curves, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and the Brier score.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>LASSO regression identified five predictors: age, immobilizer type, total dose, hypertension, and PNI. In the validation set, the LR model achieved an AUC of 0.810, sensitivity of 0.780, specificity of 0.760, accuracy of 0.773, and F1 score of 0.821; the AUCs for RF, SVM, and XGBoost were 0.854, 0.777, and 0.766, respectively. Overall, the LR model demonstrated excellent specificity comparable to the best-performing model, with good discrimination and calibration in the internal validation cohort, and was therefore selected as the optimal model. The calibration curve showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, with a Hosmer-Lemeshow test P = 0.080 and a Brier score of 0.168.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The LR model based on age, immobilizer type, total dose, hypertension, and PNI demonstrates good predictive performance for RD in cervical cancer patients receiving radiotherapy. As an internally validated model with readily available predictors, it holds potential to assist in early identification of patients at high risk for RD, providing a reference for individualized nursing care and preventive interventions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The extensive multi-source heterogeneous datasets available in oil and gas regions, including geological, drilling, logging, and drill-stem test data, provide a robust basis for geothermal resource assessment. The Moxi Gas Field in central Sichuan is located within a high terrestrial heat-flow anomaly in the Sichuan Basin and therefore has favorable geothermal conditions. The gas field has entered the mid-development stage, during which intensified water invasion and high water production have become major challenges. Because geothermal development can synergistically enhance natural gas production, priority geothermal units must be identified to maximize the combined benefits of gas and geothermal exploitation. In this study, a three-dimensional geological model was constructed from multi-source heterogeneous data, and a grid-cell-optimized volumetric heat-in-place method was applied. Compared with the planar geothermal resource assessment based on one-dimensional steady-state heat conduction, the grid-cell-optimized method improves computational accuracy by more precisely characterizing reservoir-temperature heterogeneity and estimating reservoir volume. The results show that temperatures in the Longwangmiao Formation of the Moxi Gas Field range from 135 to 149.9 °C, indicating a medium-temperature geothermal system. The total volume of formation water is 1.175 × 109 m3, and the hydrothermal geothermal resource amounts to 6.44 × 1017 J, equivalent to approximately 22 million tonnes of standard coal. The distribution of hydrothermal geothermal resources is controlled by the spatial accumulation of formation water, with resources concentrated mainly in water-accumulation units along gentle structural slopes and structural lows. Accordingly, favorable units should satisfy two criteria simultaneously: geothermal-resource enrichment and location within a water-invasion pathway. Two priority development units were identified using these criteria. Numerical simulations for Well MX210 indicate that geothermal-water production can extend the stable gas-production period, supporting the practical applicability of the proposed selection method.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD) is a serious adverse effect of tumor radiotherapy, with no effective treatment or key target. We integrated DNA methylation, transcriptomic, and proteomic data from mouse myocardium collected 12 weeks after cardiac irradiation in a mouse model of RIHD to characterize radiation-associated molecular alterations and prioritize candidate genes. Myocardial injury in mice was assessed by H&E staining, transmission electron microscopy, and serum BNP measurements. Injury in irradiated H9c2 cells was assessed by cell viability and LDH release. Candidates were screened by cross-layer direction, three-layer overlap, co-expression networks, and differential, pathway, and sensitivity analyses. Irradiation caused myocardial histological and ultrastructural damage and raised serum BNP; in H9c2 cells, viability fell and LDH release rose. PHLDA3 was the only gene overlapping all three omics layers. Both RNA and protein were upregulated, with FDR support for the proteome model (FDR = 0.0358) but not for RNA (0.0713). In GSE255063, which also contributed to the co-expression network, Phlda3 expression was higher in irradiated mice at both 1 day and 6 weeks, with statistical support only at 1 day. Immunohistochemistry in an independent group of mice showed stronger myocardial PHLDA3 staining after irradiation. Pathway analyses showed negative enrichment of mitochondrial gene sets, positive enrichment of extracellular matrix organization gene sets, and an increase in the inferred TGFβ transcriptional response score. Three-layer integration prioritized PHLDA3 for further study in radiation-induced myocardial injury. Its functional role remains to be established.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Topological photonic crystals have become critical platforms for optoelectronics, and topological corner states (TCSs) are ideal for optical sensing due to their robust field localization. However, conventional corner states are strictly constrained by the bandgap width, and their radiation losses significantly deteriorate near the band edge, hindering independent control of the resonance frequency and radiative lifetime. Ideal bound states in the continuum (BIC) can theoretically yield an unbounded quality factor (
                    <jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>
                    -factor) through destructive interference of radiation channels, but they remain intrinsically dark modes. Realizing quasi-BIC conventionally requires symmetry breaking, which inevitably weakens the mode localization. Furthermore, such states lack topological robustness and are highly sensitive to fabrication perturbations. To resolve these issues, we propose a topological design that introduces a peripheral cladding composed of a bandgap-free photonic crystal. By actively eliminating the original topological bandgap, this strategy immerses discrete TCS resonances into the radiative continuum. Consequently, a far-field excitable quasi-bound state in the continuum is formed without introducing symmetry breaking. This design relaxes the restrictive bandgap constraints on the operational frequency while preserving the inherent spatial robustness of the corner states. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the mode maintains strong sub-wavelength field confinement at the corner, achieving a high sensitivity of 726 nm RIU
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and an ideal theoretical ultrahigh
                    <jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>
                    -factor of 4.98 × 10
                    <jats:sup>9</jats:sup>
                    across the refractive index range of 1.30–1.38. Our work elucidates the controllable transition mechanism between the topological bandgap and the radiative continuum, paving a new path for robust on-chip integrated biochemical sensing, with promising prospects for trace detection in biodetection, chemical analysis, and medical diagnostics.
                  </jats:p>

                  <jats:p>In order to prepare for possible future operation of JT–60SA with tungsten plasma facing components, a H–mode scenario of JT–60SA at high power and high current is considered as reference in order to investigate the tungsten transport behavior and assess the amount of electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) which is predicted to be required in order to avoid central accumulation of tungsten. The modeling is performed with the ASTRA transport code in combination with the TGLF-SAT2 quasi–linear turbulent transport model and with neoclassical transport of impurities computed by the drift-kinetic solver NEO and the FACIT model. The impact of argon as additional seeded impurity is also considered, not only in the core behavior but also on the possibility of achieving tungsten screening in the pedestal region. The main result is that these H–mode conditions in JT–60SA achieve a so far largely unexplored domain of parameters, in which a reactor–like very low collisionality is combined with high rotation levels. In contrast to the usual domain of operation of present medium size tokamaks, where tungsten neoclassical transport is in the plateau to Pfirsch–Schlüter regime, in the predicted JT–60SA conditions toroidal rotation has a beneficial effect in increasing the strength of the temperature screening, enabling operation without any strong central tungsten accumulation and, in the most unfavorable conditions of high tungsten concentration and low rotation, requiring only 2 MW of central ECRH power to avoid locally negative electron heat fluxes in the center. Within the limited predictive capabilities of the present modeling approach for pedestal parameters, a sufficiently large and realistic domain of parameters in terms of argon concentration and plasma rotation, as well as of relative density and temperature logarithmic gradients, can also be expected to lead to the dominance of tungsten temperature screening in the JT–60SA pedestal.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In burning plasmas, zonal flows (ZFs) excited by toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) play a crucial role in improving energy confinement. In this work, strong self-generated ZFs are analyzed in a multi-

                    TAE system through nonlinear hybrid simulations using the CLT-K code, where the ZFs are driven by self-beat interactions of TAEs. The results show that the strong ZFs dominate the nonlinear stage and significantly suppress the TAE activity. The ZF mode structures consist of the
                    <jats:inline-formula>

                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">

                          <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                          <mml:mn>0</mml:mn>
                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    and
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>

                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">

                          <mml:mn>1</mml:mn>
                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    harmonics, and are directly correlated with the spatial structures of TAEs. Further analysis of the ZF kinetic energy evolution demonstrates that a finite residual between the Reynolds and Maxwell stresses, arising from toroidal geometry, enables net energy transfer from TAEs to ZFs, with an additional contribution from the energetic particles (EPs) pressure response. In addition, the linear Lorentz force contributes either to ZF pumping or damping depending on the stage of the evolution. Strong ZF generation is favored in regimes with high EP pressure and low viscosity. A self-regulating process is identified: stronger TAEs drive stronger ZFs, which in turn regulates the TAE activity. These findings provide both numerical and physical insights into the role of ZFs in regulating EP-driven instabilities in tokamak plasmas.

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Recent studies have shown that 3-pentanone remains aqueous-stable and non-emulsifying while altering wettability under extremely harsh reservoir conditions (e.g., 372.15 K and 200,000 ppm). This study investigates bypassed-oil recovery using aqueous 3-pentanone in heterogeneous carbonate rock under high-temperature, high-salinity (HTHS) conditions, with an emphasis on how preferential flow affects the ketone’s phase partitioning, in situ accumulation, and convective oil displacement. A spontaneous imbibition (SI) experiment was first conducted using formation brine (FB: 224,358 ppm), sulfate-rich injection brine (IB: 54,471 ppm), and 1.1 wt % 3-pentanone in IB (3pIB) to evaluate 3-pentanone-induced wettability alteration and oil recovery from bypassed regions. Corefloods were then performed by injecting 3-pentanone at its aqueous solubility limit in FB (0.3 wt %) and IB (1.1 wt %) under secondary and tertiary flooding conditions in carbonate cores selected to represent preferential-flow behavior. The SI experiment showed that 3-pentanone enhanced capillary-driven imbibition and recovered additional oil beyond that achieved with IB alone. In corefloods, IB and 3pIB injections improved oil recovery relative to FB injection. Material-balance analysis showed that preferential flow accelerated 3-pentanone breakthrough to 0.27 PVI, compared with the 1.92 PVI predicted by the analytical solution, and delayed in situ ketone accumulation. Nevertheless, the high K-value of 3-pentanone enabled continued partitioning into unswept regions. The early ketone breakthrough and effluent pH response indicate that preferential flow generated bypassed regions where salinity gradients between injected and resident brines promoted the release of 3-pentanone from the aqueous phase and its transport into these bypassed regions, thereby facilitating wettability alteration and additional oil recovery.</jats:p>
