<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Tungsten (W) is a prominent plasma-facing material for deuterium–tritium (D–T) fusion reactors, yet T fuel retention in W poses critical challenges to safety and operational viability. This study systematically compares three baking methods—vacuum baking, H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    gas atmosphere baking, and hydrogen (H) plasma baking—for removing D retained in W at 513 K, simulating realistic conditions for T removal in reactors. Experimental results demonstrate that D removal efficiencies reach 75% for vacuum baking after 16 h, 83% for H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    atmosphere baking after 16 h, and 99% for H plasma baking after 1 h. The superior performance of H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    atmosphere and H plasma baking is primarily driven by hydrogen isotope (HI) exchange, with efficiency strongly dependent on the concentration of H introduced into W. Higher H concentrations promote more complete exchange, leading to significantly reduced D retention. A multi-isotope Fill Level model was developed to simulate the end-to-end H plasma exchange process. The simulation reproduces the experimentally observed D removal kinetics and the emergence of HD desorption, with the D retention in good agreement with measurements. The pronounced disparity between H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    atmosphere baking and H plasma baking is fundamentally governed by the quantity of H entering W: H plasma promotes significantly greater H ingress, thereby enhancing HI exchange and resulting in a drastic reduction in D retention. This work provides both experimental validation and modeling support for HI exchange as an efficient T removal strategy.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>During the operation of the tokamak device, the high heat load released by the core plasma instability events severely affects the structure and performance of tungsten-based divertor materials. For the expected Type I ELMs in future long-pulse steady-state fusion devices, the coaxial gun discharge plasma parameters are designed to simulate the characteristics of low-medium energy density. Under constant initial conditions (discharge frequency, gas-prefilled), the total accumulated heat flux is kept constant by varying the energy density and the number of pulses. By combining the plasma-material interaction process, the temperature evolution of tungsten (W) target under different heat loads and its damage effects are comparatively studied. The results show that when the total energy is fixed, the thermal deposition time scale and the instantaneous temperature gradient lead to different types of damage, including roughening, grain loss, blistering, crack networks, and cracking accompanied by melting. Low-energy-density multi-pulse impacts cause slow heat deposition and small temperature gradients, increasing surface roughness via cyclic thermal stress. High-energy-density impacts involving only a few pulses cause rapid heat deposition and steep temperature gradients, inducing high thermal stresses that lead to blistering and cracking. The energy density of an individual pulse determines the transition from surface to bulk damage. These results suggest that peak heat load control should take priority over cumulative heat flux limitation in the service design of W targets for fusion devices.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Vulnerable-plaque rupture accounts for the majority of life-threatening cardiovascular events, yet conventional molecular imaging probes cannot stratify plaque vulnerability to enable early rupture-risk warning. Herein, we report a plasmonic spatial-confinement enhanced DNAzyme nanomachine (PDM) gated by endogenous HClO and miRNA-155 for high-contrast atherosclerotic plaque imaging. Dual-input activation restricts fluorescence turn-on specifically within foam cells, where plasmon-enhanced fluorescence and spatial-confinement boost signal output and reaction kinetics. In vitro experiments demonstrate specific foam-cell activation, affording a 9.6-fold higher-fluorescence ratio between foam and normal cells and minimizing off-foam cell signal leakage. In ApoE−/− mice, PDM produces unique gradient imaging feature which can realize precisely distinguish stable and vulnerable plaques and achieve non-invasive risk stratification and early rupture warning, providing a promising molecular-imaging tool for atherosclerotic risk stratification.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As power-electronic devices become increasingly dominant in modern power systems, the small-signal stability of high-penetration photovoltaic (PV) power systems transmitted via LCC-HVDC has become a critical issue. Under the latest Chinese grid-code requirements for renewable-energy integration, the specified positive- and negative-sequence control strategies inject periodic, sequence-coupled components that render the system characteristic periodically time-varying, thereby invalidating conventional time-invariant small-signal methodologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To address this, a linear time-periodic (LTP) modeling method is introduced here. Then, the stability boundaries of the current-loop gains are quantitatively determined by Floquet theory, and the dominant unstable oscillation modes are identified through participation factor analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that increasing PV penetration substantially narrows the allowable range of the current-loop integral gains, and the unstable modes are predominantly governed by either the PV inner current control loops or the dynamic interactions between synchronous generators and AC grid networks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings clarify how high PV integration reshapes the parametric stability margins of grid-connected power converters, and the analysis is validated against time-domain simulations of the nonlinear model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: What’s in a meal: preliminary findings on the energy density of children’s meals in the Irish foodservice sector
items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In Ireland, 17.7% of children are living with overweight or obesity
                    <jats:sup>(1)</jats:sup>
                    . Food served in the foodservice sector is estimated to account for 13% of children’s dietary energy intake in Ireland
                    <jats:sup>(2)</jats:sup>
                    . There is limited evidence on the energy density of children’s meals sold in foodservice outlets in Ireland. To address this evidence gap, the aim of this study was to determine the median energy content of popular children’s meals sold in Irish foodservice outlets in 2024 and to examine if outlets offer different portion sizes for younger and older children.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    Popular children’s meals were identified using a market research survey commissioned by the Food Safety Authority of Ireland and implemented by Ipsos B&A. A convenience sample of these popular children’s meals were collected from standalone restaurants, hotel restaurants, takeaways and pubs that serve food in Dublin in 2024. Meals were analysed for their energy content (kcal/meal) by an accredited laboratory, using the energy calculation for food in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011
                    <jats:sup>(3)</jats:sup>
                    . Descriptive statistics were determined, and a subsequent comparison was made with the European Food Safety Authority’s Average Requirement (AR)
                    <jats:sup>(4)</jats:sup>
                    for daily energy intake (kcal/day) in boys and girls (adjusted to a moderately physical activity level (PAL)) aged 3 years (PAL=1.4) and 12 years (PAL=1.6). Meal portion sizes offered on menus for children of different age groups were collected. Statistical analysis was completed using RStudio v4.4.0.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A convenience sample of n=84 children’s meals was collected including chicken nuggets and chips (n=18), burger and chips (n=17), chicken curry and chips/rice (n=17), pasta and sauce (n=16), and sausage and mash/chips (n=16). Beef burger and chips had the highest median energy (kcal) content containing 1046.18 kcal/meal (IQR:210.80; min-max 740.94-1449.96), followed by chicken curry and rice/chips containing 908.20 kcal/meal (IQR:576.10; min-max 369.20-2342.64), chicken nuggets and chips containing 892.50 kcal/meal (IQR:123.17; min-max 629.44-1157.20), sausage and mash/chips containing 814.80 kcal/meal (IQR:261.88; min-max 503.36-1115.96) and pasta and sauce containing 486.28 kcal/meal (IQR:191.63; min-max 287.64-782.40). The highest median energy density was measured in beef burger and chips, which contributed 95.45% of the AR for energy in 3-year-old girls, in contrast to 48.12% of the AR for energy in 12-year-old boys. The lowest median energy density was measured in pasta and sauce which contributed 44.37% of the AR for energy in 3-year-old girls, in contrast to 22.37% of the AR for energy in 12-year-old boys. No outlet (n=0) offered different portion sizes for younger and older children.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study found some popular children’s meal options that were energy dense. Despite younger children requiring less energy intake than older children, outlets did not offer smaller portions. There is a need to reduce the energy density of some children’s meals sold in Irish foodservice outlets.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tungsten (W) remains unclear. Here, we compare the surface morphology evolution and subsurface bubble distributions of coarse-grained and nano-grained W under fusion-relevant He plasma irradiation. The samples were exposed simultaneously to 90 eV He ions at 1173 K. Although both microstructures ultimately developed similar fuzz composed of nanoscale tendrils, their early-stage evolution of surface roughening exhibited distinct differences. In the nano-grained W film, ∼600 nm thick, surface roughening was initiated by anomalous bubble growth at grain junctions. In contrast, coarse-grained W exhibited pronounced crystallographic-orientation-dependent roughening. Subsequent tendril nucleation and growth occurred in both microstructures, preferentially at highly convex surface regions. Moreover, subsurface bubbles were confined mainly to a shallow region approximately 100–200 nm beneath coarse-grained W, whereas they permeated the entire nano-grained film. These results indicate that GB-mediated bubble dynamics primarily govern surface evolution during the fuzz-incubation stage, while interface curvature and capillary-driven diffusion dominate tendril nucleation and subsequent growth. Thus, GBs exert a decisive influence during early-stage surface roughening but have limited effect on the later development of fuzz. These findings provide insight into the distinct and common mechanisms governing He-induced surface modification in W with different grain sizes and support a capillary-growth framework for fuzz formation.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The performance of lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) is fundamentally limited by the sluggish kinetics of polysulfide conversions, where defect engineering offers a promising yet double‐edged solution. While vacancies can modulate catalytic spin states, achieving both high activity and long‐term stability remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we propose a “heteroatom‐pinning” strategy that stabilizes sulfur vacancies (Vs) via phosphorus doping in FeS, constructing an asymmetric Vs–P motif in P‐FS‐Vs‐2. Through experimental and theoretical analyses, we decipher the atomic‐scale origin of enhancement: the Vs–P pairs fine‐tune the ligand field, driving the Fe site into an optimal intermediate‐spin state via strong d‐p‐p orbital hybridization. This optimized electronic structure orchestrates balanced polysulfide adsorption/desorption, facilitates interfacial charge transfer, and lowers both kinetic and thermodynamic barriers for polysulfide conversion, as evidenced by a distinct volcano relationship between spin state and activity. The designed cathode delivers an exceptional combination of durability (0.030% capacity decay per cycle and 86.6% energy efficiency over 1986 cycles at 1.0 C) and remarkable rate performance (583.7 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate density functional theory descriptions of layered materials require exchange–correlation approximations that remain reliable as the nature of interlayer bonding changes with thickness. Here, we use diffusion quantum Monte Carlo (DMC) to benchmark density functional approximations for bilayer, few-layer, and bulk arsenic. DMC predicts equilibrium interlayer separations near 3.4–3.5 Å for three bilayer arsenene stackings, whereas bulk gray arsenic adopts a substantially more compact structure despite sharing the same nominal adjacent-layer registry with one of the bilayers. This contrast reveals a nontrivial thickness-driven evolution from a large-spacing, weakly coupled bilayer to the compact, chemically bonded structure of bulk gray arsenic. Among the tested approximations, SCAN+rVV10 most consistently reproduces the DMC equilibrium structures and relative stacking energies, while LDA, PBE+D2, and vdW-optB86b generally favor overly compressed geometries and overstabilize the bulk-like A1B–1 stacking. Based on this benchmark, SCAN+rVV10 predicts a thickness-dependent sequence from A1A1 to A1B1 and finally to bulk-like A1B–1 stacking. The structural evolution is accompanied by a stacking-dependent closure of the band gap associated with increasing interlayer As pz hybridization. These results demonstrate that the accuracy of density functional approximations for arsenene depends on the interlayer-bonding regime and establish DMC benchmarks for describing its evolution from the bilayer to the bulk limit.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study introduces a Double-Inertial-Embedded Two-Step Mann (DIETM) algorithm for approximating a common fixed point of two quasi-nonexpansive mappings in a real Hilbert space. The proposed scheme incorporates two inertial terms into a two-step Mann framework, and its weak convergence is established under suitable assumptions. Numerical experiments in function spaces demonstrate its convergence behavior and computational efficiency compared with classical and inertial iterative methods. To investigate its practical applicability, DIETM is employed to optimize the output weights of an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) within a hybrid CNN–ELM framework for MRI-based dementia classification. Brain MRI images from the OASIS Alzheimer’s Detection dataset were classified into four dataset-defined categories: Non-Demented, Very Mild Dementia, Mild Dementia, and Moderate Dementia. Following duplicate control and group-aware stratified partitioning, the images were divided into training, validation, and held-out test sets, with brightness augmentation applied only to the training set. Pretrained VGG16 and DenseNet121 networks were employed as fixed-feature extractors and integrated with the proposed DIETM-ELM optimization framework. The proposed approaches were evaluated against end-to-end CNN models, conventional machine learning classifiers, and alternative ELM-based methods. On the held-out test set (N=614), VGG16 + DIETM-ELM achieved an accuracy of 87.13%, balanced accuracy of 89.03%, and macro-F1 score of 89.01%, representing the highest observed performance among the evaluated VGG16-based models. DenseNet121 + DIETM-ELM further improved classification performance, achieving an accuracy of 89.41%, balanced accuracy of 90.97%, and macro-F1 score of 90.84%, although DenseNet121 + SVM attained a slightly higher accuracy of 90.88%. These findings demonstrate the potential of DIETM-based ELM optimization across different CNN feature extractors for multiclass MRI classification. However, the single-dataset evaluation, lack of verified subject-level independence, and absence of external validation limit conclusions regarding its generalizability and clinical applicability.</jats:p>

<jats:p>
                    Dietary supplementation of poultry diets with essential oils is a natural strategy to mitigate stress and enhance the quality of poultry products. This study investigated the impact of tea tree oil (TOL) or walnut oil (WO), alone and in combination, on performance, carcass traits and quality, blood chemistry, and antioxidant activity in broilers reared under normal stocking density (NSD) and high stocking density (HSD) conditions. A total of 520  d-old Cobb 500 broiler chicks were randomly distributed to eight groups according to a 2 × 4 factorial design. All chicks were randomly allocated to eight experimental groups, with five replicates per group. Each replicate consisted of 16 birds in HSD groups and 10 birds in NSD groups. The two factors were stocking densities (16 and 10 birds  m
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>

                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    diet), WO (5 mL WO kg

                    diet), and combination (5 mL TOL + 5 mL WO kg
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    diet). There were significant interactions between treatments and stocking densities for performance criteria (average weight gain (AWG), feed intake (FI), and feed conversion ratio (FCR)), carcass traits (dressing percentage, breast, and thigh yield), and blood metabolites (glucose, cholesterol, triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein (HDL), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), and antioxidant activity, as well as omega-3 and the ratio of omega-3 to omega-6. Dietary WO significantly increased final body weight and AWG compared with TOL and the control group at both stocking densities (

title: Continuous gradient composite solid electrolyte with differentiated functions toward electrodes for high-performance lithium metal batteries
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In response to the development demand for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with high energy density and high safety, this study reports a composite solid electrolyte (LPCNE) prepared from poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP), cyclopentane-1,1-dicarbonitrile (CPDCN), and Li6.4La3Zr1.4Ta0.6O12 (LLZTO). Through gravitational sedimentation, a functionally oriented continuous gradient structure forms inside LPCNE, in which the PVDF-HFP rich layer facing the cathode offers excellent oxidation resistance, while the high modulus LLZTO rich layer facing the lithium metal anode (LMA) effectively suppresses lithium dendrite growth. Such a continuous gradient structure eliminates the interfacial impedance caused by delamination between the organic and inorganic phases, achieving a smooth compositional transition. The incorporation of CPDCN as α-H free nitrile plasticizer increases the ionic conductivity of LPCNE to 0.69 mS·cm−1, and the coordination of CPDCN with metal atoms on the LLZTO surface significantly reduces the concentration of free cyano groups, thereby effectively suppressing side reactions between cyano groups and lithium metal. Consequently, the Li/LPCNE/Li symmetric cell exhibits stable cycling for over 2000 h, and the LiFePO4/LPCNE/Li cell delivers a discharge specific capacity of 158.3 mAh·g−1 at 0.2 C with 78.4% retention after 650 cycles. Moreover, LPCNE possesses a wide electrochemical stability window of 4.75 V, enabling the LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2/LPCNE/Li cell to deliver a discharge specific capacity of 163.9 mAh·g−1 at 0.1 C with 70% retention after 250 cycles. This study achieves differentiated functionality by adjusting the gradient distribution of the composite solid electrolyte components, providing an innovative solution for high-performance LMBs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Large regions of ectodomains of fusion subunits of spikes of enveloped viruses transform into thermostable hairpin structures important for fusion between viral and cell membranes. This study concerns the HIV Gp41 ectodomain whose hairpin is between the fusion peptide (FP) that binds the cell membrane and the membrane-proximal external region (MPER) that binds the viral membrane. FP/MPER contact is investigated with a large FP_HM construct produced by native chemical ligation between FP synthesized with 13CO labeling at specific Gly’s and HM that includes hairpin and MPER, and is expressed in bacteria with 2H labeling. 13C–2H rotational-echo double-resonance NMR of membrane-bound FP_HM shows that ∼1/4 of FP 13CO spins are ∼3.5 Ǻ from 2H spins. These NMR data support van der Waals contact between MPER and Gly-16′s at the edges of the FP intermolecular antiparallel β sheet. This contact lengthens the hairpin to the outer leaflets of the two membranes and promotes their close apposition and perturbation that accelerates formation of the stalk fusion intermediate. We also discovered that producing FP_HM by ligation requires 2 M imidazole in addition to 6.7 M guanidinium chloride (GuCl). HM forms folded oligomers in GuCl, and imidazole induces oligomer dissociation and increases the concentration of reactive monomers. FP_HM and unreacted HM form oligomers, and their separation is achieved by ligation of H6G6D4K_FP with tagless HM purified from inclusion bodies, followed by HM release with low-pH wash and FP_HM release with enterokinase cleavage. These discoveries will be useful for ligation when reactants form folded oligomers in GuCl.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Systemic inflammation may contribute to postmenopausal bone loss. We examined whether four routine inflammatory indices, the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), are associated with prevalent osteoporosis, T-scores and trabecular microarchitecture. Methods: In this retrospective single-centre study, 551 postmenopausal women undergoing spinal surgery with an intraoperative bone specimen were assessed. Osteoporosis was defined as a T-score of −2.5 or lower at the lumbar spine, femoral neck or total hip. Pre-operative blood counts, T-scores at three sites and histomorphometric parameters were analysed by correlation and multivariable logistic regression. Results: All four indices were higher in women with osteoporosis (p < 0.001) and correlated inversely with the three T-scores and with trabecular area, perimeter, area percentage and number, and positively with trabecular separation (|r| = 0.13–0.30). NLR (OR 1.531, 95% CI 1.232–1.903) and PLR (OR 1.011, 1.006–1.017) remained associated after adjustment, whereas MLR did not. Areas under the ROC curve were 0.779 for NLR, 0.759 for PLR and 0.798 for their combination, indicating moderate discrimination. Conclusions: NLR and PLR were independently associated with prevalent osteoporosis and a poorer trabecular microstructure, but discrimination was only moderate and the retrospective design precludes causal or predictive inference.</jats:p>

<jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Study Design:</jats:bold>
                    Randomized controlled trial.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Objectives:</jats:bold>
                    The objective of this supplemental analysis was to confirm superiority of fusion of P-15L (PearlMatrix
                    <jats:sup>TM</jats:sup>
                    P-15 Peptide Enhanced Bone Graft) compared with local autograft control at 6-, 12-, and 24-months.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Methods:</jats:bold>
                    Skeletally mature patients with degenerative disc disease were randomized 1:1 to P-15L or the local autograft (control) during single-level transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion with a polyetheretherketone cage and supplemental pedicle screw fixation. The data analysis used a gatekeeping strategy such that fusion rates at 6-, 12-, and 24-months could not be compared unless (1) the primary endpoint demonstrated that P-15L was non-inferior to the control with respect to Composite Clinical Success at Month 24, and (2) Kaplan-Meier (KM) and statistics confirmed the superiority of P-15L relative to control in the time-to-fusion distribution. If the conditions of the gatekeeping strategy were met, fusion rates at the individual timepoints could be analyzed with the Wald z-test.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Results:</jats:bold>
                    All conditions of the gatekeeping strategy were met; thus, fusion rates at the individual timepoints were analyzed. The Wald z-test for superiority revealed that KM fusion rates of the P-15L group were superior to the control group at 6-, 12-, and 24-months (P<0.0001 at all timepoints). Compared with control, P-15L demonstrated a 30.7%, 27.3%, and 26.2% higher fusion rate at 6-, 12-, and 24-months, respectively.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Conclusions:</jats:bold>
                    Together, the results from the composite clinical success endpoint, time-to fusion, and the Wald z-tests robustly demonstrate that P-15L was superior to autograft in facilitating fusion at 6-, 12-, and 24-months.
                  </jats:p>

The anisotropic conductivity introduced by helium channels alters the velocity and temperature distributions, further complicating the MHD flow. In addition, localized hot spots exceeding the design temperature limit are found near the top of the U-turn and in the outlet reduced activation ferritic/martensitic steel walls, suggesting that enhanced cooling is required in these locations.
                  </jats:p>

title: DSAF-Net: Uncertainty-Aware Spatio-Temporal Attention Fusion for Robust Multimodal Fault Diagnosis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable fault diagnosis in industrial environments suffers from the inherent limitations of unimodal perception: visual sensors are vulnerable to environmental noise, while timeseries sensors lack spatial localization capabilities. Existing multimodal fusion strategies rely on static concatenation or equal-weight voting, which implicitly assume that all modalities are equally reliable at all times—a flawed assumption in harsh oilfield environments where rain, occlusion, and electromagnetic interference can abruptly corrupt one sensor stream. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes DSAF-Net, a robust multimodal learning network that synergizes heterogeneous spatio-temporal data for accurate fault identification. DSAF-Net constructs a spatio-temporal dual-stream architecture—a spatial stream based on an enhanced YOLO11 detector and a temporal stream based on a dual-branch LSTM—whose core is an uncertainty-aware spatio-temporal Attention Fusion module that computes adaptive per-class attention weights from calibrated prediction entropy, learning to suppress noisy sensors while amplifying the trustworthy modality in real time. Controlled corruption experiments covering illumination reduction, Gaussian noise, simulated rain, motion blur, and electromagnetic interference show that DSAF-Net improves Fault Recall from 89.5% to 94.6% and Macro-F1 from 92.9% to 95.7% under a strict well-level split while degrading substantially more gracefully under modality corruption. Experiments on a real-world oilfield dataset demonstrate that DSAF-Net achieves a Fault Recall of 94.6% and a False Alarm Rate of only 0.5%, significantly outperforming singlemodal baselines and static fusion strategies. These results indicate that uncertainty-aware decision-level fusion can improve the reliability of automated well surveillance and reduce unplanned downtime and manual inspection costs in harsh oilfield environments.</jats:p>

title: Dietary nutrient density and frailty syndrome in elderly
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Diet quality is an important determinant of healthy aging. The Elderly Nutrient Rich Food (E-NRF7.3) score, based on European dietary recommendations, assesses nutrient density in the diets of older adults. The aim of the study was to investigate the relationship between the nutrient density of the diet and the occurrence of frailty syndrome (FS) among the elderly.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study included 140 adults aged ≥ 60 years. Dietary nutrient density was assessed using the E-NRF7.3 algorithm based on three-day dietary records. Frailty syndrome was evaluated according to Fried’s five criteria. Frail and pre-frail individuals were combined into one group (“FS+preFS”), while participants without FS symptoms formed the “noFS” group.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>At least one FS symptom was identified in 45% of participants. In univariate analysis, the “FS+preFS” group was significantly older, less physically active, reported poorer health, and had higher rates of smoking, dietary supplement use, and hypertension. They were less likely to spend time outdoors and be exposed to sunlight. Robust participants had 
higher intakes of water, polyunsaturated fatty acids, sodium, calcium, iodine, thiamine, and riboflavin, and slightly higher intakes of plant protein, dietary fiber, iron, and zinc. Regression analysis, adjusted for sex revealed such associations for dietary fiber, calcium, sodium, and trend for potassium; adjusted for sex and age revealed only for dietary fiber and calcium. The mean E-NRF7.3 score was 13.9 in the “noFS” group and 14.9 in the “FS+preFS” group (p = 0.592 univariate analysis; p = 0.803 regression analysis).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite the higher intake of some nutrients considered recommended, such as dietary fiber and calcium, by people without symptoms of frailty, we did not demonstrate that a higher E-NRF7.3 score is associated with the number of frailty symptoms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Perdew–Zunger self-interaction correction (PZ-SIC) makes approximate density functional theory (DFT) exact for all one-electron densities, but sacrifices exactness for uniform densities. I show that an alternative to the orbital density ansatz employed in PZ-SIC restores the uniform density limit. The new ansatz can be expressed as a local-hybrid-like functional including an orbital-dependent local mixing functional. This approach also eliminates the need to evaluate approximate density functionals on lobed one-electron densities extracted from smooth many-electron densities, thereby reducing orbital dependence and lobed density error. Restoring the uniform limit and reducing lobed density error does not solve the “paradox” of SIC: the present approach can still worsen a semilocal functional’s good description of equilibrium properties such as atomization energies. Regardless, the approach does provide another step toward strongly constrained and broadly accurate self-interaction-corrected DFT.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Poor fast-charging performance limits the practical application of natural graphite as an anode for lithium-ion batteries. Although a spatially uniform LiF-rich interphase can stabilize solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry and facilitate interfacial Li+ transport, LiF generated by fluorinated-electrolyte decomposition is often nonuniformly distributed and difficult to regulate. Here, we construct a reactive fluoride nanointerface on natural graphite through a cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB)-assisted reaction between aluminum nitrate and ammonium fluoride. The resulting nanointerface consists of uniformly distributed AlF3 species that participate in SEI evolution during cycling. During cycling, the AlF3-derived layer undergoes interfacial F/O exchange with oxygen-containing SEI intermediates, incorporating O into the Al coordination environment to form Al–O–F and inducing the coupled formation of LiF and Al–O–F. In the resulting LiF/Al–O–F-rich composite SEI, Al–O–F regulates LiF distribution through bridging and anchoring effects, producing a compact and structurally stable LiF-rich interphase. This interphase suppresses side reactions, alleviates polarization, and promotes homogeneous Li+ transport. Consequently, SGR@15% AlF3 delivers 93.2% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 1 C and 315.9 mAh g–1 after 800 cycles at 5 C. This work shifts LiF formation from random electrolyte decomposition to reactive-fluoride-interface-mediated interfacial conversion, offering an effective strategy for stable SEI construction in high-rate natural graphite anodes.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) is an additive manufacturing technique that is capable of fabricating customised parts from a variety of materials. Titanium (Ti) has favourable properties for numerous applications, and Ti parts produced using LPBF are at the forefront of several industry applications. This study aimed to optimise the process parameters of commercially pure Ti (cpTi) using LPBF by following an established hierarchical approach. The process began by studying the LPBF single tracks to optimise the laser power and scanning speed, followed by evaluating the double layers to optimise the hatch distance and attain the final process parameters. The results showed that the LPBF technology may be effective in producing parts from elemental Ti powder. Future studies should focus on optimising the properties of cpTi for specific industrial applications.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted considerable attention for applications in information storage, anticounterfeiting, and intelligent sensing due to their long-lived emission characteristics. However, the triplet excited states of organic phosphorescent molecules are highly susceptible to nonradiative deactivation caused by molecular motions and oxygen quenching, making the construction of stable microenvironments crucial for achieving efficient long-lived RTP. Herein, we develop a polymer confinement strategy for constructing long-lived organic RTP films by incorporating 9,10-diaminophenanthrene (DAphe) into a poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) matrix. The confined polymer network and weak intermolecular interactions effectively restrict the excited-state molecular motions of DAphe and suppress triplet nonradiative decay, enabling the DAphe@PVC films to exhibit persistent phosphorescence emission centered at approximately 520 nm under 365 nm excitation, with a maximum phosphorescence lifetime of 3.36 s. Systematic investigations reveal that the RTP properties of DAphe@PVC can be regulated by varying DAphe loading content, PVC K value, film thickness, temperature, and thermal treatment conditions. Measurements under air and nitrogen atmospheres further reveal the contribution of oxygen-induced quenching to triplet-state deactivation. Furthermore, the incorporation of typical PVC additives, including epoxidized soybean oil (ESO), methyl tin mercaptide (MTM), and dioctyl phthalate (DOP), produces distinct and reproducible RTP responses associated with changes in the PVC formulation. This work establishes a relationship between PVC matrix confinement, polymer microenvironment variations, and RTP behavior, providing a new strategy for developing long-lived polymer-based RTP materials and optical indicators of polymer formulation changes.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Multimodal hazard detectors combining vision and audio are usually validated and quantized on synthetically corrupted inputs, so their behavior under real sensor degradation is untested. We evaluate degradation-aware learned audio-visual fusion on a physically captured benchmark: 640 trials (80 test pairs in eight conditions) recorded on a Zynq-7020 system-on-chip with a USB camera and its microphone, covering real noise (signal-to-noise ratio −3.6 to 16.2 dB), exposure-locked low light, and physical occlusion. Across ten fusion networks of two architectures, learned fusion outperformed fixed-weight late fusion under occlusion by 10 to 31 points, but it tended to be less accurate when both sensors were usable, relying on an audio branch weakened by the real acoustic path. Networks with identical validation accuracy ranged from 79% to 90% on real data. Real degradation also exposed a quantization failure unseen in synthetic tests: INT8 post-training quantization lost 15 points under occlusion, recalibration did not fix it, and block-wise mixed precision recovered most of the loss. On the ARM processor alone, the deployed system matched its offline accuracy (88.8%), beat all-INT8 by 15 points under occlusion, and decides 0.87 s after each 5 s recording. This is a laboratory proof of concept rather than a safety validation.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Case overview/synopsis</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Banas Dairy was Asia’s largest dairy cooperative. It transported liquid milk from its Palanpur plant, Gujarat to Faridabad plant, Delhi National Capital Region. For this transportation, Banas dairy used railway milk tankers (RMTs) and road transport. These modes inherently had some concerns. For example, in RMTs there were frequent delays, repetitive milk transfers and increased costs due to demurrage charged by Indian Railways (IR). Along with that, another grave issue was maintaining the quality of milk. In trucking mode, truck drivers had to undergo risks of pilferage, road accidents and police harassment. In 2021, the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) offered the ToT service on its Western Dedicated Corridor of India (The Economic Times, 2025a). Part A of this case was positioned around six months before the Banas Dairy actually adopted the ToT. That time, conundrum was whether Banas Dairy would change its transportation mode to the ToT. The conundrum faced by Banas Dairy would have to be resolved under the able guidance of Mr Sangram R. Chaudhary, managing director of Banas Dairy. The change was to be implemented in the immediate future to overcome the cons posed by the RMTs and road transport. Part B of this case, which was based on 2023–2026 and covered the period after the shift to ToT mode, showed another dilemma – how to optimize the return journey of the ToT. This case study detailed the operations of the DFCCIL and the salient features of the ToT. It highlighted logistics improvements, savings in fuel costs and the positive environmental effects of innovative logistics, especially in rail transport, in a developing economy such as India. This is a teaching note supplementing the “Neither truck nor train, rather truck on train: innovative freight fusion or patchwork?” case study.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Motivation</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In spatial omics, multi-omics data have the potential to delineate tissue architecture more faithfully than any single modality, but unsupervised spatial domain detection remains difficult because different modalities exhibit distinct sparsity patterns and noise characteristics. Existing methods have made progress in combining spatial and multimodal signals, yet how to introduce cross-modal information while preserving reliable modality-specific representations and avoiding non-local spot mixing remains insufficiently explored. To address this challenge, we present SPAMO, a cross-modal fusion framework for unsupervised spatial multi-omics domain detection.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>SPAMO learns modality-specific graph representations by combining a spatial-based KNN graph shared across modalities with a modality-specific feature based KNN graph, performs neighborhood-constrained cross-modal attention over co-located and neighboring spots, and uses gated residual fusion to integrate unimodal and cross-modal information. Across Human Lymph Node, Mouse Brain, and simulated benchmarks, SPAMO achieves competitive or improved domain-detection performance, with the clearest gains on real datasets. These results support neighborhood-constrained cross-modal fusion as an effective strategy for retaining modality-specific representations while incorporating complementary multi-omics information.</jats:p>

Most notably, magnetic perturbations are intentionally applied in tokamaks to suppress edge localised modes (ELMs). However, despite growing confidence in the method, a complete understanding of the process involving all relevant mechanisms is yet to be gained. In this work, we present an integral kinetic plasma response model in the large-aspect-ratio limit capable of appropriately resolving finite Larmor radius effects of ions. <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In order to prepare for possible future operation of JT–60SA with tungsten plasma facing components, a H–mode scenario of JT–60SA at high power and high current is considered as reference in order to investigate the tungsten transport behavior and assess the amount of electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) which is predicted to be required in order to avoid central accumulation of tungsten. The modeling is performed with the ASTRA transport code in combination with the TGLF-SAT2 quasi–linear turbulent transport model and with neoclassical transport of impurities computed by the drift-kinetic solver NEO and the FACIT model. The impact of argon as additional seeded impurity is also considered, not only in the core behavior but also on the possibility of achieving tungsten screening in the pedestal region. The main result is that these H–mode conditions in JT–60SA achieve a so far largely unexplored domain of parameters, in which a reactor–like very low collisionality is combined with high rotation levels. In contrast to the usual domain of operation of present medium size tokamaks, where tungsten neoclassical transport is in the plateau to Pfirsch–Schlüter regime, in the predicted JT–60SA conditions toroidal rotation has a beneficial effect in increasing the strength of the temperature screening, enabling operation without any strong central tungsten accumulation and, in the most unfavorable conditions of high tungsten concentration and low rotation, requiring only 2 MW of central ECRH power to avoid locally negative electron heat fluxes in the center. Within the limited predictive capabilities of the present modeling approach for pedestal parameters, a sufficiently large and realistic domain of parameters in terms of argon concentration and plasma rotation, as well as of relative density and temperature logarithmic gradients, can also be expected to lead to the dominance of tungsten temperature screening in the JT–60SA pedestal.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>During the operation of the tokamak device, the high heat load released by the core plasma instability events severely affects the structure and performance of tungsten-based divertor materials. For the expected Type I ELMs in future long-pulse steady-state fusion devices, the coaxial gun discharge plasma parameters are designed to simulate the characteristics of low-medium energy density. Under constant initial conditions (discharge frequency, gas-prefilled), the total accumulated heat flux is kept constant by varying the energy density and the number of pulses. By combining the plasma-material interaction process, the temperature evolution of tungsten (W) target under different heat loads and its damage effects are comparatively studied. The results show that when the total energy is fixed, the thermal deposition time scale and the instantaneous temperature gradient lead to different types of damage, including roughening, grain loss, blistering, crack networks, and cracking accompanied by melting. Low-energy-density multi-pulse impacts cause slow heat deposition and small temperature gradients, increasing surface roughness via cyclic thermal stress. High-energy-density impacts involving only a few pulses cause rapid heat deposition and steep temperature gradients, inducing high thermal stresses that lead to blistering and cracking. The energy density of an individual pulse determines the transition from surface to bulk damage. These results suggest that peak heat load control should take priority over cumulative heat flux limitation in the service design of W targets for fusion devices.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Achieving a homogeneous dispersion of carbon black is a primary objective in the fabrication of lithium–ion batteries (LIBs). This study investigates the synthesis and application of carbon black (CB) and silica (SiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ) hetero–aggregates as functional conductive additives in aqueous lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode slurries. The electrostatic repulsion of the silica particles decreased the conductive additive agglomerate diameter from 5.5 to 0.8  in pure water, demonstrating an improved dispersion of the conductive additive. The improved dispersion was also evident in the particle size distributions of LFP cathode slurries by an increase in the fine fraction from 39.0 vol.‐% to 48.6 vol.‐%. However, rheological amplitude sweep tests revealed that the SiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    surface inhibits the formation of a stable viscoelastic gel network of the slurry, which resulted in a disrupted percolating network within the dried electrode. By compacting the electrodes, the particle‐particle contacts were restored and the manufactured half‐cells containing hetero–aggregates showed similar discharge capacities at 3C with up to  mAh/g compared to  mAh/g for the CB reference. Therefore, hetero–aggregates of carbon black and SiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    are suitable as conductive additive and offer significant potential in reducing the necessary mechanical energy input for the mixing step.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>A self-consistent two-dimensional numerical model of an inductively coupled plasma (ICP) discharge in helium and He/SiH4 mixtures was developed to investigate the temporal evolution of charged and neutral species and the formation of a strongly electronegative plasma core. The model couples the RF electromagnetic field with plasma-chemical kinetics, charged-particle transport, electron energy balance, electrostatic potential, and gas heating. Particular attention was paid to the influence of negative-ion chemistry on the formation and evolution of the electronegative plasma core. Numerical simulations were performed using two alternative kinetic schemes: one including the formation of SiH4− and another excluding this channel while accounting for H− formation. The results demonstrate that a strongly electronegative central region develops in both kinetic schemes, although its formation time and spatial characteristics differ significantly. At an input power of 750 W and a pressure of 0.2 Torr, the maximum electronegativity reaches approximately 36.84 at 100 s when SiH4− formation is included, compared with 16.51 in the alternative model. The corresponding axial widths of the region satisfying α > 1 are approximately 1.97 and 1.56 cm, respectively. The accumulation of negative ions is accompanied by a pronounced redistribution of the self-consistent electric field and the formation of a broad low-field region in the discharge center. Analysis of neutral-species densities and estimated incident thermal fluxes reveals that atomic hydrogen and SiH are the dominant dissociation products of silane in both kinetic schemes, whereas SiH2, SiH3, and atomic silicon exhibit greater sensitivity to the adopted reaction mechanism. These findings demonstrate that the formation of a strongly electronegative plasma core is preserved under the investigated changes in negative-ion chemistry, while its quantitative characteristics and the relative availability of reactive species depend on the adopted kinetic scheme. The results provide insight into the formation and evolution of the electronegative plasma core and the production of reactive species under conditions relevant to silicon.</jats:p>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma cell mastitis (PCM) is a benign inflammatory breast disease that mainly affects non-lactating women. This condition often pursues a persistent or relapsing clinical course, and refractory cases are characterized by extensive lesions, severe symptoms, unsatisfactory cosmetic outcomes, and a high risk of recurrence. However, no widely accepted criteria have been established for defining individuals at high risk of PCM. Early recognition and timely management in this population may help reduce subsequent disease burden and shorten the overall course of treatment. We therefore designed this study to identify clinical and imaging features associated with the subsequent development of PCM and to provide evidence for early risk identification.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This multicenter nested case-control study will be led by Longhua Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, in collaboration with several participating centers. A total of 300 women with features indicating a high risk of PCM will be enrolled. Baseline data will include general characteristics, clinical signs and symptoms, breast ultrasonographic findings, and contrast-enhanced breast magnetic resonance imaging parameters. Participants who receive a pathological diagnosis of PCM during follow-up will constitute the case group. Controls will be selected by risk-set sampling from cohort members who remain free of PCM at the time each case is diagnosed. Cases and controls will be matched by age and enrollment date. Telephone follow-up will be conducted every 14 days during the first 3 months and monthly thereafter. Follow-up will end at 12 months or when PCM is diagnosed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to investigate the relationships between clinical and imaging features at the initial visit and subsequent disease progression in women at high risk of PCM. The findings may facilitate improved early recognition, risk stratification, and follow-up management, and may also provide evidence for the formulation of future early intervention strategies.</jats:p>

title: Flow Dynamics, Particle Transport, and Deposition Across Laminar, Transitional, and Turbulent Backward-Facing Step Flows

affiliation.name: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Georgia Southern University, 1332 Southern Dr, Statesboro, GA 30458, USA

items.abstract: <jats:p>Particle deposition in separated flows depends on both the carrier-flow structure and particle size, yet their combined effects can vary across flow regimes. This study investigates particle transport and wall deposition downstream of a backward-facing step for nine Reynolds numbers ranging from 500 to 8000 and particle diameters from 10 to 100 μm. Large-eddy simulation coupled with Lagrangian particle tracking is employed to examine deposition efficiency, spatial deposition distributions, and particle transport pathways. In the laminar regime, deposition efficiency remains approximately 81–85% for particles smaller than about 35 μm and generally decreases at larger diameters. The transitional regime exhibits pronounced nonmonotonic variations, with deposition efficiency reaching approximately 12% near 35–40 μm at Re = 3000 before recovering to approximately 58% at 60 μm. In the turbulent regime, deposition efficiency remains within a comparatively narrow range of approximately 54–59%. Spatial deposition distributions and particle trajectories reveal diameter-dependent transport characteristics even when global deposition efficiencies are similar. The results indicate that particle inertia must be considered together with the Reynolds-number-dependent carrier-flow structure when interpreting deposition behavior. The predicted deposition efficiencies remain conditional on the adopted numerical framework, injection conditions, and particle–wall interaction assumptions.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Alpha peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (α-PRRT ) has emerged as a promising advance in the treatment of neuroendocrine tumours (NETs), offering higher linear energy transfer and potent cytotoxicity than beta(β)-PRRT e.g.177Lu DOTATATE. Although 177Lu DOTATATE has improved outcomes, most patients eventually progress, highlighting the need for more effective and durable strategies. The development of alpha therapies, such as 225Ac-, 213Bi-, and 212Pb-labelled radiopharmaceuticals, represents a promising approach to overcome these limitations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted a comprehensive review of published clinical trials, on-going studies, and congress abstracts using PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and major oncology and nuclear medicine meeting proceedings. Eligible studies included clinical trials evaluating α-PRRT in advanced NETs. Data on study design, patient characteristics, efficacy and safety were extracted.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Ten completed and five on-going trials were identified. Across completed studies, objective response rates ranged from 40% to 70%, with disease control rates frequently approaching 100%. Median progression free survival was often not reached at 18–24 months. Toxicities were favourable, mostly mild, transient haematologic or gastrointestinal adverse events, with limited grade 3–4 renal or marrow toxicity. Preliminary results from the ALPHAMEDIX 02 trial demonstrated promising efficacy in both radioligand therapy naïve and previously treated patients. However, evidence remains limited, with most data derived from retrospective, early-phase studies</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Current findings suggest that α-PRRT provides encouraging and durable antitumour efficacy with acceptable toxicity in advanced NETs, including β-PRRT refractory disease. As prospective data continue to emerge, α-PRRT holds significant promise as a next-generation theragnostic modality.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The present study investigates a stochastic SEIS epidemic model that integrates logistic recruitment and a general awareness-driven incidence function. The model is rigorously formulated and shown to possess a unique global positive solution that remains within $\mathbb{R}^{3}_{+}$ almost surely. To analyze the long-term dynamics, we derive sufficient conditions for disease extinction and persistence by introducing the stochastic thresholds $\tilde{R}_e$ and $\tilde{R}_p$. Specifically, Theorem 2 establishes that $\tilde{R}_e < 1$ guarantees extinction, while Theorem 3 shows that $\tilde{R}_p > 1$ ensures persistence. Furthermore, our analysis confirms that for $\tilde{R}_s > 1$, the system is asymptotically stable under stochastic perturbations and possesses a unique ergodic stationary distribution, a result proven via Has’minskii’s theory. The theoretical analysis is further validated by numerical simulations that reveal noise-induced extinction, persistence under certain initial conditions, and convergence to a unique stationary distribution. Overall, the findings highlight the critical role of awareness-driven incidence and stochastic fluctuations in shaping epidemic dynamics. From a control perspective, they suggest that targeted interventions affecting transmission, recovery, latency, and vaccination can effectively reduce the effective reproduction number below the critical threshold. The analytical framework developed herein offers a robust foundation for examining epidemic behavior and is readily extendable to other classes of stochastic epidemic models.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Contact with polymeric particulate materials may change the response of enzymatic colorimetric assays through analyte partitioning, filtration losses, or matrix-dependent effects. This study examined apparent phenylalanine (Phe) signal recovery following contact with particles derived from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles, polypropylene (PP) plates, and cellulose-based paper cups. Materials were characterized by FTIR and Raman spectroscopy and contacted with buffered Phe solutions (20, 60, or 100 &#x00B5;m) at particle loadings of 1, 3, or 10 mg/mL for nominal durations of 2, 6, 24, 48, and 96 h. After 0.45-&#x00B5;m filtration, filtrates were analyzed by an enzyme/developer-based assay at 450 nm. Apparent signal recovery was normalized to concentration- and time-matched Phe-only controls. Across 45 conditions per material, mean apparent recoveries were 70.5% for PET (range 40.3&#x2013;91.2%), 41.9% for PP (7.1&#x2013;85.9%), and 7.3% for cellulose-based particles (0.2&#x2013;24.6%). PET showed a loading-associated decline in recovery, whereas PP exhibited more variable, nonmonotonic profiles. The pronounced suppression observed for cup-derived material showed that effects were not confined to synthetic plastic particles. Because measurements were made on processed filtrates, reduced colorimetric response cannot be assigned uniquely to Phe adsorption. Potential contributions include particle-associated analyte removal, soluble matrix constituents, and filter-passing particulate matter. These findings identify substantial material-dependent changes in the apparent Phe analytical response under controlled buffer conditions and support the use of matrix-matched and orthogonal measurements to distinguish analyte depletion from assay interference.</jats:p>

title: LCS.jl v1.0: a high-performance, multi-platform computational model in Julia for turbulent particle-laden flows

affiliation.name: Institute of Science Tokyo (Tokyo, Japan)

items.abstract: <jats:p>Multiphase turbulent flow phenomena are observed not only in industrial devices but also in environmental flows, and direct numerical simulation plays a key role in their investigation. Many numerical models have been developed; nevertheless, few models are highly optimized for GPU platforms, which represent the current mainstream in high-performance computing. In this study, we developed LCS.jl (Lagrangian Cloud Simulator in Julia), a single-source and multi-platform multiphase turbulence simulation model implemented in the Julia language and KernelAbstractions.jl. Validation results confirmed that the present fluid and particle statistics agree well with those obtained in prior studies. For GPU execution, the GPU-side prefix-scan implementation reduced the particle communication cost by approximately 88 % relative to the CPU-delegated sequential implementation. LCS.jl achieved CPU performance comparable to the original Fortran implementation, with similar intra-node scaling behavior. For GPUs, strong-scaling efficiency was approximately 70 % up to 256 GPUs, and weak-scaling efficiency was approximately 80 % up to 216 GPUs on TSUBAME4.0 (a GPU supercomputer at the Institute of Science Tokyo). LCS.jl achieved a maximum estimated speedup of approximately 16.3× on GPUs over CPUs. Execution on both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs further supported portability across GPU architectures. A trial heterogeneous execution achieved an approximately 68 % reduction in execution time compared to the CPU-only configuration even in configurations where the GPU was not the primary compute device. These results demonstrate that LCS.jl is a multiphase turbulence simulation platform that achieves both portability and scalability across a variety of computational resource configurations.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Particle films composed of diatomaceous earth (SiO2), kaolinite, or calcium carbonate have not been widely adopted for post-bloom pest management in pome fruits. Concern about visible residues on fresh market fruits has been a major factor limiting summer use. Repeated use of particle films has also been associated with secondary pest outbreaks. Studies were carried out with these three materials for codling moth, Cydia pomonella (L.), control in apple, in combination with horticultural mineral oil, microencapsulated pear ester (PEMEC), ethyl (2E,4Z)-2,4-decadienoate, and several essential oils. Repeated applications of SiO2 with a surfactant increased counts of woolly apple aphid, Eriosoma lanigerum Hausman. However, the substitution of 1.0% mineral oil for the adjuvant significantly reduced this secondary pest problem. The addition of PEMEC with SiO2 or kaolinite significantly improved performance, likely due to enhanced neonate wandering across the particle film. Each particle film was effective in reducing oviposition. Commercial essential oil products differ among themselves but can provide additional control as a topical treatment for eggs and adults. Coverage, rate, and timing are the key factors influencing the success of these summer programs. Reconsideration and reconfiguration of post-bloom particle film-based programs and seasonal use with processing pome fruit is warranted.</jats:p>

<jats:p>
                    An elevated red blood cell distribution width (RDW, >14.0%) is associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD). Individuals with spinal cord injuries (SCI) have a greater risk for CVD and are reported to have an elevated RDW compared to population based normative data. Anthropometric factors (age, sex, and BMI) have minor influences on RDW but these factors have not been controlled in SCI comparisons when analyzing factors that may have larger influences on RDW(e.g. inflammation). Additionally, positive adaptations associated with aerobic exercise training parallel decreases in RDW in non-injured (NI) populations but similar longitudinal assessments in SCI have not been completed. Therefore, the purpose of this investigation was to compare 1) RDW in SCI and anthropometrically matched NI and 2) RDW in SCI performing 6-months of aerobic exercise training. SCI displayed a larger RDW (n=25,13.5±1.4%) compared to NI (n=22, 12.5±0.4%, P<0.05). Additionally, in SCI (n=37), RDW decreased following exercise training (Pre:14.2±0.3%, Post:13.6±0.2%, P<0.05). Aerobic capacity increased with training in all individuals (1.22±0.07 to 1.37±0.07 L·min
                    <jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>
                    , P<0.05) but the magnitude of increase was greater in those with pre-training RDW ≤14.0% (n=18, Δ+0.19±0.03 L·min
                    <jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>
                    ) compared to those with elevated RDW >14.0% (n=19, Δ+0.11±0.02 L·min
                    <jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>
                    , P<0.05). These findings suggest that RDW is elevated in SCI and are reduced with 6-months of aerobic exercise training. An elevated RDW at the initiation of aerobic exercise training may limit cardiorespiratory gains. Although it is unknown if an elevated RDW is the result of injury, inflammation, or reduced physical activity, routine assessment of RDW appears to be a useful biomarker representing cardiovascular health in SCI.
                  </jats:p>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The limited efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in gastric cancer is largely attributed to the low immunogenicity of tumor cells. Given that immunogenic cell death (ICD) can enhance tumor immunogenicity, exploring whether Shen Qing WeiChang Formula (SQWCF), a patented traditional Chinese medicine for gastric cancer, can induce ICD holds potential translational significance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:italic>In vitro</jats:italic>
                      , the ICD-inducing capacity of SQWCF and its impact on DC and T-cell activation were evaluated by immunofluorescence, ELISA, co-culture assays, flow cytometry, qPCR, and western blot. Pharmacological inhibition assays of signaling pathways associated with DC maturation further evaluated their respective contributions to DC maturation.
                      <jats:italic>In vivo</jats:italic>
                      , subcutaneous transplantation tumor models and tumor rechallenge models were used to assess SQWCF-triggered ICD and its regulation of DC and T-cell immunity.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      SQWCF can induce ICD in gastric cancer cells, including the exposure or release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and the modulation of immune-related mediators. The SQWCF and the ICD it induces can promote DC maturation, characterized by increased expression of maturation markers and the ability to present antigens.
                      <jats:italic>In vivo</jats:italic>
                      , SQWCF shows the ability to induce ICD, promote cDC1 and cDC2 maturation, increase intratumoral cDC2 and CD8
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      T-cell infiltration, and increase infiltration of cDC1s in draining lymph nodes, potentiating T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity. Mechanistic analyses indicated that the NF-κB signaling pathway is mainly involved in DC maturation by SQWCF and the ICD it induced, although contributions from other pathways could not be excluded. In a co-culture system, DCs exposed to SQWCF-treated tumor cells supported enhanced T-cell-mediated antitumor activity, including an increased proportion of CD8
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      T-cells and cytotoxicity to tumor cells.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>SQWCF mediates dual immunostimulatory actions — direct DC activation and ICD-driven DC maturation together with T-cell priming — via NF-κB signaling, underscoring its translational potential in gastric cancer immunotherapy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage (HICH) are neurological disorders associated with high incidence and disability rates, while current therapeutic strategies remain limited. There is an urgent clinical need for highly specific, convenient, and efficient biomarkers, as well as innovative diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma samples were collected from patients with AIS, patients with HICH, and healthy controls. Plasma exosomes were isolated, and differentially expressed long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) were screened using lncRNA microarrays and validated by qRT-PCR. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of candidate lncRNAs for the early identification of AIS and HICH. Correlations between candidate lncRNAs and disease severity and prognosis were assessed in combination with National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale and modified Rankin Scale scores.</jats:p>
                    <jats:p>Bioinformatics analyses were conducted to predict target genes and identify relevant biological functions and signaling pathways through Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses. Furthermore, siRNA interference was used to investigate potential molecular regulatory mechanisms at the cellular level.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A series of differentially expressed plasma exosomal lncRNAs were identified. Several candidate lncRNAs, including NONHSAT016392 for AIS and NONHSAG074724 for HICH, showed satisfactory diagnostic performance, with areas under the ROC curve ranging from 0.7898 to 0.9524.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Specific plasma exosomal lncRNAs may serve as promising biomarkers for the early diagnosis and prognostic assessment of AIS and HICH. These findings also provide a basis for elucidating key molecular pathways involved in disease onset and progression and for developing novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for cerebrovascular diseases.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

<jats:p>
                    Magnetised plasma configurations in fusion devices are unavoidably subject to magnetic perturbations. Most notably, magnetic perturbations are intentionally applied in tokamaks to suppress edge localised modes (ELMs). However, despite growing confidence in the method, a complete understanding of the process involving all relevant mechanisms is yet to be gained. In this work, we present an integral kinetic plasma response model in the large-aspect-ratio limit capable of appropriately resolving finite Larmor radius effects of ions. Benchmarking against a prior differential model based on a finite Larmor expansion to second order demonstrates the necessity of the integral model due to unphysical modes in the solution of the former. Further, we investigate the isotope dependence of the linear plasma response in both approaches. We find that for identical plasma parameters, the linear response shows no significant variation between hydrogen and deuterium. Scanning the shielding current as a function of plasma rotation gives qualitatively different predictions for the ion resonance. While the finite Larmor radius expansion produces a narrow feature near the fluid resonance condition, the integral model reveals a substantially broader effective kinetic ion resonance shifted towards the condition where the

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In order to prepare for possible future operation of JT–60SA with tungsten plasma facing components, a H–mode scenario of JT–60SA at high power and high current is considered as reference in order to investigate the tungsten transport behavior and assess the amount of electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) which is predicted to be required in order to avoid central accumulation of tungsten. The modeling is performed with the ASTRA transport code in combination with the TGLF-SAT2 quasi–linear turbulent transport model and with neoclassical transport of impurities computed by the drift-kinetic solver NEO and the FACIT model. The impact of argon as additional seeded impurity is also considered, not only in the core behavior but also on the possibility of achieving tungsten screening in the pedestal region. The main result is that these H–mode conditions in JT–60SA achieve a so far largely unexplored domain of parameters, in which a reactor–like very low collisionality is combined with high rotation levels. In contrast to the usual domain of operation of present medium size tokamaks, where tungsten neoclassical transport is in the plateau to Pfirsch–Schlüter regime, in the predicted JT–60SA conditions toroidal rotation has a beneficial effect in increasing the strength of the temperature screening, enabling operation without any strong central tungsten accumulation and, in the most unfavorable conditions of high tungsten concentration and low rotation, requiring only 2 MW of central ECRH power to avoid locally negative electron heat fluxes in the center. Within the limited predictive capabilities of the present modeling approach for pedestal parameters, a sufficiently large and realistic domain of parameters in terms of argon concentration and plasma rotation, as well as of relative density and temperature logarithmic gradients, can also be expected to lead to the dominance of tungsten temperature screening in the JT–60SA pedestal.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Although first-principles calculations exhibit high accuracy, their prohibitive computational cost and limited screening throughput remain major bottlenecks. Here, we systematically established a first-principles database of elastic constants for 30 common stable and metastable second phases in aluminum alloys, which span multiple crystal systems and space groups. Twenty-six composition-weighted intrinsic elemental features were screened via Pearson correlation analysis, recursive feature elimination, and exhaustive subset search, yielding two core features. Four new descriptors with well-defined physical significance, which are the relative difference in first ionization energy, the absolute difference in valence electron count, the atomic size mismatch, and the absolute Pauling electronegativity difference, were then introduced to construct machine learning models for the bulk modulus and shear modulus under small-sample conditions. The Ridge regression model for bulk modulus prediction achieved a five-fold cross-validated coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.94 and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 7.02 GPa, while the random forest (RF) model for shear modulus prediction achieved an R2 of 0.92 and an RMSE of 7.59 GPa. SHAP analysis identified average melting point and atomic molar volume as the key features for bulk modulus, while average melting point and d-orbital valence electron count were key features for shear modulus. First-principles results for three representative phases, Al3Er, Al3Ta, and Al3Ti, are in good agreement with previously reported values, confirming the reliability of the density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Deviations between model predictions and first-principles values were within 6% for all three phases, demonstrating robust predictive performance. Further electronic structure analysis revealed that the degree of d-orbital hybridization and the strength of bond directionality are the key microscopic origins that determine the shear modulus. The proposed physics-driven machine learning framework enables high-throughput screening of the elastic properties of second phases in aluminum alloys across diverse crystal structures and provides a physical basis for precipitate design in next-generation high-strength aluminum alloys.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Designing a helical spring means finding a wire diameter, a coil diameter and a number of coils that give the required loads at the required lengths while keeping the stresses, the safety factors and the geometry within limits. Metaheuristic optimizers can solve this task, but they must be run again for every new requirement, and purely data-driven inverse models rarely guarantee feasible designs. This study proposes a Machine Learning (ML)-based inverse design framework for compression, extension and torsion springs that combines a learned proposal with closed-form spring physics and verification by the calculation engine of the open-source Open Design Optimization Platform (ODOP). A dataset of 150,000 designs covering 17 materials was generated with Latin hypercube sampling and evaluated with ODOP. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and a K-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) search propose the wire diameter and the spring index. A physics-based correction then computes the number of coils and the free length or the initial tension so that the required spring rate and load points are met exactly, and 14 candidates per requirement are checked against all default ODOP constraints. On 2,713 unseen requirements, the framework returned a design that met the requirement within 1% and satisfied all default constraints for 89.8%, 90.3% and 100% of the compression, extension and torsion cases, compared with at most 5.8% for a direct inverse ANN. It needed 14 design evaluations and about 1–2 ms per requirement. Over five independent runs, the standard deviation of its success rate was at most 2.1 percentage points, and the success rate stayed above 80% in 36 of 41 tests with a material that was excluded from training. A genetic algorithm with the same physics-based correction solved all requirements and found 21–32% lighter designs, but it needed about 1,900 evaluations per requirement; when it was started from the framework candidates, 182 evaluations were enough for 98–100% success. When fatigue, buckling and hook checks were added to the selection rule, the success rate fell to 34–82%, which shows that these checks must be part of the requirement in cyclic applications. The framework is therefore best used as a fast generator of verified starting designs that can be refined when weight or additional checks are critical.</jats:p>
