<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>During the operation of the tokamak device, the high heat load released by the core plasma instability events severely affects the structure and performance of tungsten-based divertor materials. For the expected Type I ELMs in future long-pulse steady-state fusion devices, the coaxial gun discharge plasma parameters are designed to simulate the characteristics of low-medium energy density. Under constant initial conditions (discharge frequency, gas-prefilled), the total accumulated heat flux is kept constant by varying the energy density and the number of pulses. By combining the plasma-material interaction process, the temperature evolution of tungsten (W) target under different heat loads and its damage effects are comparatively studied. The results show that when the total energy is fixed, the thermal deposition time scale and the instantaneous temperature gradient lead to different types of damage, including roughening, grain loss, blistering, crack networks, and cracking accompanied by melting. Low-energy-density multi-pulse impacts cause slow heat deposition and small temperature gradients, increasing surface roughness via cyclic thermal stress. High-energy-density impacts involving only a few pulses cause rapid heat deposition and steep temperature gradients, inducing high thermal stresses that lead to blistering and cracking. The energy density of an individual pulse determines the transition from surface to bulk damage. These results suggest that peak heat load control should take priority over cumulative heat flux limitation in the service design of W targets for fusion devices.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Clubs, leagues and data vendors hold game-level performance data separately, and sharing such data is often restricted. This study examines which box-score differences are associated with National Basketball Association (NBA) game results and whether federated learning (FL) can match centralised models without pooling raw data. Using 49,899 games from the 1979–80 to 2024–25 seasons, we built home-minus-away differentials for 14 box-score statistics, measured their association with the result, and compared logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM) and k-nearest neighbours (KNN) classifiers. Hyperparameters were chosen on the 2023–24 season, and the 2024–25 season was used only for testing. Because the inputs are recorded during the game being classified, the task is post-game outcome classification rather than pre-game forecasting. An FL framework was then simulated with the 30 franchises as clients. Field-goal percentage (r = 0.62) and field goals made (r = 0.57) showed the strongest associations with winning. All classifiers far exceeded the 0.549 accuracy of always predicting a home win; SVM reached 0.9081 and LR 0.9088, a difference that was not significant. Federated LR matched an identically configured centralised LR (paired difference 0.00 percentage points; 95% CI −0.43 to 0.43) and beat franchise-only models by 0.94 points. Under severe label skew, FedProx and a simple intercept recalibration recovered most of the lost accuracy. With client-level differential privacy, accuracy stayed above 0.90 at ε ≈ 4. A pre-game variant based on rolling averages reached 0.63 accuracy, again with no loss under federation.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Intravenous (IV) fluid contamination is a common cause of misleading laboratory results. Machine learning approaches may complement fixed rules, delta checks, and manual review, but developing and validating models requires technical expertise that has limited widespread adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>FluidFlagger is an open-source application that packages a model-development and evaluation work flow for contamination detection behind a browser-based interface that requires no programming knowledge. Pretrained models were evaluated retrospectively against focused expert-adjudication labels in held-out basic metabolic panel (BMP) and complete blood count (CBC) subsets (127 and 37 labeled contaminated specimens, respectively) and against previously optimized comparator model outputs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>BMP classifiers discriminated contamination with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (auROCs) of 0.974 (real-time) and 0.969 (retrospective); CBC classifiers achieved 0.763 and 0.879. Specificity exceeded 97% for all models, whereas sensitivity was variable, reflecting a predominance of mild contamination events and the need for local threshold calibration.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>FluidFlagger provides an accessible framework for training and validating institution-specific models for detecting IV fluid contamination, lowering the barrier to local evaluation across laboratories of varying informatics expertise. Prospective clinical use requires local integration, threshold evaluation, validation, governance, and monitoring.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Heavy metal accumulation in the aquatic system poses critical challenges for wastewater treatment. Forward osmosis is a promising membrane technology for the rejection of heavy metals in wastewater. However, the prediction of heavy metal removal using membranes remains scarce. To address this gap, various machine learning algorithms including RF, XGBoost, SVR, MLP, and hybrid stacking have been developed to simultaneously predict heavy metal % removal and water flux. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost and hybrid stacking showed the strongest overall predictive performance. Hybrid stacking achieved a removal efficiency R2 of 0.9897, whereas XGBoost achieved R2 0.9977 for water flux. The model was further validated using 5-fold cross-validation. To enhance interpretability, partial dependence plots and Shapley additive explanations were used to evaluate the feature importance. Model interpretability analysis revealed that the contact angle, zeta potential, draw solution concentration, and DS type were the dominant features. The interpretable algorithm provides theoretical guidance on the forward osmosis membrane and various operating conditions for heavy metal rejection.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Language development in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heterogeneous, yet it remains unclear which features of everyday conversation are specific to autism rather than shared with general developmental delay, and how these features relate to cognitive ability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study applied an interpretable computational pipeline to 34,946 child utterances produced by 115 children in five ASDBank corpora, comprising cross-sectional samples of children aged 21-79 months and longitudinal recordings of autistic boys aged 30-117 months. Thirty-seven features spanning grammar, vocabulary, pragmatic contingency and frozen neural language-model measures (GPT-2 surprisal, context gain and MiniLM semantic contingency) were extracted from transcripts, aggregated per child, and analysed with nested, repeated cross-validation, SHAP attribution, language-cognition interaction models, Gaussian mixture profiling and mixed-effects growth models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      In the primary comparison of 16 autistic children with 16 age- and IQ-matched children with developmental delay, autistic children were best distinguished by grammatical (AUC = 0.74) and pragmatic features (AUC = 0.71), and reduced question asking was the only difference surviving false-discovery correction (
                      <jats:italic>g</jats:italic>
                       = −1.45). Language-model features added little discriminative value, and no language domain separated autistic from language-matched typically developing toddlers. Spontaneous lexical diversity tracked receptive vocabulary (
                      <jats:italic>ρ</jats:italic>
                       = 0.58), and language-vocabulary coupling was strong in the autism and delay groups but absent in typically developing children. Autistic children varied along a continuous dimension of language level plus an independent conventionality dimension rather than forming discrete subtypes, and immediate lexical repetition of the adult’s preceding turn declined as utterance length grew.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study shows that interpretable conversational markers, particularly initiation through questions, carry autism-specific information beyond developmental level. The difference in question-asking remained consistent across alternative cross-validation approaches and after adjustment for sex, and the repetition findings were stable across alternative automatic definitions, although their agreement with specialist identification of echolalia has not been established. Because the primary comparison involved 16 children per group, classification performance carries considerable uncertainty and requires external replication in independent samples. The proposed models may contribute to a better understanding of autism-related language patterns and, with further validation, offer complementary insights to support clinical assessment and professional judgment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable surface water quality monitoring can support sustainable water resource management and contribute to SDG 6 by helping identify locations that may warrant further investigation. Because WQI-based classes are ordered, evaluating the direction and magnitude of classification errors is relevant to interpreting monitoring results. This study aimed to compare multiclass and ordinal classification in terms of accuracy, error patterns, and the quality of predicted probabilities. A total of 1344 samples from four different water bodies in Ukraine (the Rika River, Lake Pisochne, and the Burulka and Leninsky ponds), subject to varying levels of anthropogenic and recreational pressure, were analyzed. Five water quality classes defined by WQI were predicted using pH and the concentrations of Ni, Co, Zn, Fe, Cu, and Mn. Eleven models were evaluated using repeated nested stratified cross-validation with 25 outer folds. Cumulative Ordinal XGBoost and Cumulative Ordinal CatBoost ranked highest by mean Accuracy, Macro-F1, and QWK, with values of 0.9818, 0.9788, and 0.9955 for XGBoost and 0.9817, 0.9786, and 0.9955 for CatBoost, respectively. The Nadeau–Bengio corrected test detected no statistically significant differences in Macro-F1, QWK, mean absolute class error, or severe error rate between the two ordinal models or between either the ordinal model and its multiclass counterpart. Most incorrect predictions differed from the true class by one level. No critical errors were recorded according to the criteria defined in the study. Cumulative Ordinal CatBoost had the lowest Multiclass Brier Score (0.0285) and ECE (0.0140), whereas the multiclass XGBoost model had the lowest Log Loss (0.0587). Permutation importance analysis showed that Co was the most important feature across all 11 models. In multiclass XGBoost, Cu had the highest mean absolute SHAP value for class III (Satisfactory), while pH ranked first for classes IV (Good) and V (Excellent). In Cumulative Ordinal XGBoost, pH also ranked first for P(Y > 4). Ablation analysis of the multiclass and ordinal XGBoost models showed the greatest performance decline after Co was removed. Evaluating error direction, probability calibration, and feature contributions alongside classification accuracy provides a basis for selecting models to support surface water quality monitoring. Validation on other water bodies and sampling periods is needed before using these models to guide monitoring decisions in new settings.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Machine-learning surrogates can accelerate structural assessment, but accuracy on a random split provides limited evidence for use outside the training domain. This study evaluates 14 regression methods on 432 paired numerical configurations of slotted cold-formed steel beams with mode-specific local- and distortionalbuckling capacities. Geometry, steel-grade and slot-length hold-outs are combined with size-matched controls, matched-configuration transfer, training-only validation, split-conformal intervals, estimator repetitions, applicability screening and SHAP sensitivity. XGBoost attains in-distribution mean absolute errors of 0.064 and 0.105 kN m for the two targets, yet its geometry-shift errors rise to 13.813 and 9.150 kN m. Perforation transfer is strongly model-dependent: Gaussian-process errors reach 8.898 and 6.463 kN m, while leading tree models approximately match a baseline that transfers the corresponding known slot-length response. Reduced training size explains only a small part of the observed deterioration. Nominal 90% intervals also lose coverage under shifts; mean XGBoost geometry-shift coverage across 30 calibration allocations falls to 0.37% and 2.85%. A training-specific combined range and covariance screen rejects all shifted queries in this benchmark, while retaining 88.5% of the fixed in-distribution test set. These findings support a conditional credibility audit with explicit abstention and uncertainty checks rather than deployment based on aggregate accuracy alone.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Retailers, airlines and hotels sell limited or perishable inventory to customers whose willingness to pay changes with time, season and competition. Online sales and live data now make frequent price changes possible, so pricing has become a major lever for revenue. Poorly set prices either lose sales or leave money on the table. Gap. Existing reviews usually cover a single industry or a single technique, such as reinforcement learning, and rarely compare demand forecasting, price optimization and real-world business constraints together, and they pay little attention to how pricing models are validated before launch. Novelty. This survey links demand estimation, price optimization and business guardrails in one framework across retail, airline and hotel pricing. It contributes a literature review, an industry comparison, a technique taxonomy, a reference architecture and a forecast-guided pricing algorithm. Method. Peer-reviewed studies from 2015 to 2026 were collected from IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar using a PRISMA-style protocol. Studies were compared on datasets, preprocessing, demand model, optimization method, validation design and business metrics. Results. Gradient-boosted trees and neural networks produce the most accurate demand forecasts, while bandits and reinforcement learning adapt prices best when demand is uncertain or changing. Reported revenue gains depend heavily on simulation assumptions, and few studies test on real market experiments. Fairness, competitor reactions and limits on price changes are seldom evaluated. Conclusion. Effective dynamic pricing needs accurate demand models, exploration that is safe for the business, and clear pricing rules. Future work should focus on realistic evaluation, fairness and explainable pricing decisions for customers.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The oceanic habitat conditions that Pacific salmon encounter during the pelagic life stage have a substantial effect on their distribution, growth, and survival. Fisheries and monitoring data collected in coastal marine and freshwater areas are often linked to conditions in oceanic habitat to attempt to explain patterns in salmon population productivity as their marine rearing habitats continue to change (Connors et al. 2020; Kitada et al. 2025; Ohlberger et al. 2025). However, a substantial source of uncertainty in such analyses stems from knowledge gaps regarding the habitats that salmon utilize while at sea. For this reason, many research efforts have worked to characterize the oceanic ranges of each species and how they relate to environmental factors like sea surface temperature (e.g., Abdul-Aziz et al. 2011; Langan et al. 2024; Alabia et al. 2025). Yet, these characterizations often present a coarse view of salmon distributions generated through summarizing or smoothing catch data over large spatial scales. In order to address contemporary challenges to salmon management, such as evaluating if and where/when high seas competition among species may take place (Ruggerone et al. 2023) or enhancing the effectiveness of enforcement activities against Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing, new approaches are needed to maximize the spatiotemporal insight gained from composite historical datasets.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Mental health issues within workplace environments constitute a significant global concern. According to the World Health Organization (2024), anxiety and depression together contribute to an estimated loss of over one trillion U.S. dollars in productivity each year. Although awareness of this problem has grown across organizations, most existing initiatives remain reactive, intervening only after symptoms appear rather than proactively identifying individuals at risk. The present research employs a predictive and data-centric methodology to anticipate employee vulnerability to mental health challenges, drawing on the Mental Health in Tech Survey dataset hosted on Kaggle. Guided by the CRISP-DM process model and supported by the job demands resources (JD–R) theoretical framework, the study incorporated comprehensive data preprocessing, feature construction, and machine learning techniques. To evaluate model effectiveness, several performance metrics were applied, such as accuracy, F1-score, precision, recall, and ROC-AUC, along with a feature importance analysis that connected statistical patterns to conceptual insights. Among the tested algorithms, the Random Forest model demonstrated the best results, achieving 87.2% accuracy and an ROC-AUC of 0.93. Key predictors identified included organizational support and familial history of mental health conditions. These findings highlight the value of combining psychological theory with computational modelling to generate actionable intelligence. Such an approach can inform early detection strategies, help destigmatize mental health concerns, and promote the development of more supportive and resilient workplace cultures.</jats:p>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how National Climate Change Policy (NCCP) influences firm-level climate risk disclosure (CRD). The study also investigates whether the policy affects transition- and physical-risk disclosure differently, and how analyst coverage, political connections and CSR intensity shape this relationship.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study uses firm-year data for companies listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange from 2007 to 2022. CRD is measured using a hybrid computational linguistics framework that combines Word2Vec embeddings, semantic expansion and multi-stage expert validation to construct separate disclosure indices for transition and physical risk. The empirical analysis employs an exposure-based difference-in-differences design.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that NCCP affects climate disclosure selectively rather than uniformly. The policy significantly increases physical-risk disclosure, whereas transition-risk disclosure declines in the baseline specification. Dynamic estimates support parallel trends and indicate that the effects emerge gradually. Further analysis shows that policy-relevant political connections are associated with stronger disclosure responses, while higher CSR intensity mitigates the decline in transition-risk disclosure and amplifies the increase in physical-risk disclosure. Analyst coverage provides suggestive evidence of an information-intermediary channel.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings suggest that climate policy alone may not be sufficient to ensure broad-based transparency in a weak-enforcement environment. Stricter mandatory rules, better institutional coordination and external monitoring may improve corporate climate transparency.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study provides evidence from a climate-vulnerable emerging economy and introduces a validated text-based CRD measure that distinguishes transition-risk from physical-risk disclosure and shows that policy effects depend on political access, external monitoring and strategic capacity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The oil and gas industry increasingly seeks sustainable, locally sourced drilling-fluid additives, but their performance varies with material type, formulation, and operating conditions. This structured review synthesizes 46 included studies identified through searches of Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect, supplemented by forward and backward citation tracking. The review evaluates agricultural/bio-based, nanoparticle, and industrial/food-processing waste additives for water-based drilling fluids and examines machine-learning (ML) approaches for prediction and optimization. Reported agricultural and bio-based additives were commonly evaluated at concentrations of approximately 3–6 wt%, with fluid-loss reductions. Nanoparticle additives were generally evaluated at lower concentrations of 0.5–1.5 wt% and included studies addressing elevated-temperature conditions, whereas industrial and food-processing waste additives covered a wider concentration range of about 0.1–10 wt%. Across the ML studies reviewed, artificial neural networks, Random Forest, XGBoost, support vector machines, and hybrid/ensemble models reported R² values mostly above 0.85, with several studies reporting values mostly above 0.99 (minimum reported 0.78) for specific prediction tasks. However, validation strategies, dataset transparency, and generalization testing varied substantially. Key gaps include inconsistent experimental reporting, limited long-term and field-scale validation, sparse life-cycle assessment, and limited external validation of ML models. Future progress requires standardized testing, transparent datasets, leakage-resistant validation, and field-relevant performance assessment.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge, and timely diagnosis is essential for effective treatment and disease control. Automated analysis of chest X-ray images using machine learning has shown strong potential for supporting clinical diagnostics. Previous studies using hyperparameter-optimized machine learning algorithms, including convolutional neural networks (CNN), support vector machines (SVM), and decision trees, have achieved high classification performance on TB chest X-ray datasets, with accuracies exceeding 98%. In this work, we extend these investigations by evaluating the performance of a fine-tuned vision–language model (VLM) for tuberculosis classification and comparing its performance with traditional machine learning approaches. The study uses a publicly available TB chest X-ray dataset and evaluates models using standard clinical performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, precision, F1-score, and specificity. Traditional optimized models such as SVM, CNN, and decision trees achieved accuracies of 99.58%, 99.50%, and 98.33%, respectively. The proposed VLM-based approach achieved a test accuracy of 99.67%, with precision, recall, and F1-score values of 0.9967. These results demonstrate that fine-tuned transformer-based VLM architectures can achieve performance comparable to, and slightly better than, optimized classical machine learning models for TB chest X-ray classification. The findings highlight the potential of VLMs for AI-assisted medical imaging diagnostics and future multimodal clinical decision-support systems.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Strong performance on a familiar email dataset can overstate how well a phishing detector handles other mail. We audited a public corpus of 18,650 labeled emails and found that 419 messages in the original test set (6.81%) also appeared in training. Removing empty entries and duplicates left 17,513 messages. We compared four classifiers based on term frequency–inverse document frequency with four fine-tuned transformers. We used three seeded train, validation, and test partitions and trained with either the original class proportions or an equal number of examples per class. Validation data guided model and threshold selection. We tested the selected models on held-out messages and on 11,502 synthetic emails labeled as English in E-PhishLLM. RoBERTa’s mean F1 fell from 98.56% on the primary test sets to 62.56% on E-PhishLLM. Multinomial naive Bayes had the highest mean F1 on that challenge (72.57%). In a separate exploratory comparison, Qwen3-4B flagged one of 5506 legitimate emails on E-PhishLLM and detected 53.64% of the phishing emails. For 15 of 16 model and training settings, mean false-positive rates on E-PhishLLM exceeded the 1% validation cap. These results show why phishing evaluations should report recall and false positives on other corpora alongside within-corpus F1.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are attractive nanoscale emitters, yet their response to energetic electron excitation remains poorly understood and often unstable, limiting cathodoluminescence (CL) spectroscopy, radiation‐detection applications, and electron‐beam‐based device processing. Here, we investigate the CL response of giant‐shell CdSe/CdS QDs and strategies to improve its stability through combined in situ CL and photoluminescence (PL) measurements. Spectral and lifetime analysis reveals efficient multiexciton excitation, leading to blueshifted emission and faster dynamics, while charge accumulation contributes to cathodobleaching. Using indirect excitation to reach sub‐pA effective currents, we demonstrate partial recovery of long‐lived neutral‐exciton emission and strongly reduced cathodobleaching, although biexciton emission persists even at these low currents. Furthermore, replacing long insulating ligands with shorter ones strongly suppresses biexciton emission, consistent with improved charge drainage. Our work presents two complementary methods to control the CL response of QDs under electron‐beam excitation, providing a practical route toward stable CL for spectroscopy and imaging, fast scintillation, and electron‐beam‐compatible photonic devices.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Hybrid manufacturing combines two or more manufacturing processes to exploit their complementary strengths while mitigating their limitations. Flow forming is a cold-forming process used to manufacture seamless, dimensionally precise tubular components with rotational symmetry. The conventional production of titanium flow-forming preforms commonly involves deep drilling of solid stock, which generates substantial material waste; wire-based additive manufacturing offers the potential to reduce this waste by producing preforms closer to the required geometry. For reactive materials such as titanium, directed energy deposition using an electron beam (DED-EB) is particularly suitable because processing takes place in a vacuum environment. This study investigates the feasibility of fabricating Ti-6Al-4V tubular preforms by wire-based DED-EB and subsequently cold flow forming them. The additively manufactured preform was flow-formed to a 50% wall-thickness reduction without through-thickness rupture, whereas a further reduction to 75% resulted in extensive surface cracking and local rupture. The results demonstrate that DED-EB Ti-6Al-4V can accommodate substantial compressive and shear deformation, although the achievable reduction is limited under the process conditions investigated. The study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating DED-EB preforms into a flow-forming process chain for titanium components and indicates the potential of this hybrid route to improve material efficiency; this potential was not quantified in the present work.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Existing cyberattack detection methods for smart grids such as Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) often suffer from limited adaptability, delayed response, and inadequate coordination in distributed energy systems. These techniques may struggle to detect stealthy or coordinated attacks, especially under communication delays or system uncertainties. This paper proposes a novel Snitch Digital Twin (Snitch-DT) architecture for cyber-physical anomaly detection in grid-connected wind farms using Smart Voltage Source Converters (VSCs). Each wind generator is equipped with a local Snitch-DT that compares real-time operational data with high-fidelity digital models and generates trust scores for measured signals. These trust scores are coordinated across nodes to detect distributed or stealthy cyberattacks. The performance of the Snitch-DT system is benchmarked against previously published Artificial Neural Network (ANN)- and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based detection frameworks. Simulation results using an IEEE 39-bus wind-integrated test system demonstrate improved attack detection accuracy, faster response time, and higher robustness under various cyberattack scenarios.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The development of lightweight, non-toxic, and flexible radiation shielding materials is critical for modern medical, aerospace, and industrial applications where conventional lead and concrete shields are impractical. In this study, polystyrene-based composites reinforced with cadmium oxide and bismuth oxide at weight fractions ranging from 5 to 25 wt% were fabricated via a solution casting technique. The macroscopic structural integrity of the composites was confirmed through bulk density measurements, indicating the absence of large-scale voids and ensuring the physical suitability of the samples for subsequent attenuation experiments. Gamma-ray attenuation measurements were conducted experimentally using a narrow-beam geometry and a sodium iodide doped with thallium scintillation detector across the energy range of 0.511–1.765 MeV. The experimental results were validated against theoretical calculations using the XCOM database, showing excellent agreement with relative deviations predominantly below 5%. The linear attenuation coefficient increased systematically with filler concentration, with bismuth oxide consistently outperforming cadmium oxide due to its higher atomic number of 83 versus 48, which enhances photoelectric absorption in the low-to-intermediate energy regime. At 0.662 MeV, the 25 wt% bismuth oxide/polystyrene composite achieved a linear attenuation coefficient value of 0.1239 cm⁻
                    <jats:sup>1</jats:sup>
                    , representing an 11.7% enhancement over the 25 wt% cadmium oxide/polystyrene composite. This highest concentration formulation demonstrated a half-value layer of 5.60 cm and a shielding efficiency of 11.65% at a fixed thickness of 1 cm at 0.662 MeV, marking a 26.7% reduction in required thickness and a 34% improvement in efficiency compared to pure polystyrene. Benchmarking against conventional materials revealed that the 25 wt% bismuth oxide/polystyrene composite has an areal density of 7.62 g/cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , making it 11.0% lighter than ordinary concrete while approaching the weight efficiency of lead, alongside offering superior flexibility and significantly lower toxicity compared to conventional lead and cadmium-based alternatives. These findings establish polystyrene–bismuth oxide composites as a promising, lead-free alternative for next-generation radiation shielding in weight-sensitive and environmentally conscious applications.
                  </jats:p>

title: Terahertz Integrated Sensing and Communication for Ground-to-UAV Channels: A Survey of Channel Modeling, Waveforms, and Beam Management
items.abstract: <jats:p>Terahertz (THz) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is emerging as a key enabler of sixth generation (6G) networks, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are among its most challenging yet valuable host platforms. Over ground-to-UAV links, THz-ISAC payloads promise ultra-high-rate to backhaul and millimeter-level sensing within the stringent size, weight, and power budget of a hovering drone. Realizing this promise requires a coherent understanding of four tightly coupled pillars: the ground-to-UAV THz channel, beam management, the ISAC waveform and its transceiver realization, and system-level performance. This survey is organized around these four pillars. We first consolidate the propagation fundamentals of aerial THz links, including altitude-dependent molecular absorption and UAV-specific non-stationarity, together with the measurement and modeling literature that underpins them. We then review beam management, covering near-field beam-pattern transformation, alignment and tracking under misalignment, and wideband hybrid beamforming that combats beam squint with true-time-delay architectures. We next contrast the candidate ISAC waveforms — OTFS, DFT-s-OTFS with superimposed pilots, and SI-DFT-s-OFDM with flexible guard intervals — in terms of PAPR, power-amplifier efficiency, Doppler robustness, and sensing accuracy, and assess the transceiver hardware against the UAV payload envelope. Finally, we discuss system-level performance, including localization bounds, spectral efficiency, and sensing/vision-aided mobility management, along with use cases and open challenges. Throughout, quantitative claims are traced to their source documents and to the specific figures from which they stem.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>
                    Organic electrode materials are attractive for proton batteries because of their structural designability and high theoretical capacity. However, achieving fast and durable proton storage remains a grand challenge, as dense π–π stacking in conjugated organic polymers limits redox‐site accessibility and slows charge transport under harsh conditions. Here, we report an electron‐deficient fused‐ring conjugated polymer (CAPT) as a high‐capacity, high‐rate anode for proton batteries operating at low temperatures. The full π‐conjugation across the fused‐ring skeleton and the strong electron‐deficient effect of hexaazatriphenylene and pyrazinoquinoxaline motifs synergistically promote H
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    accessibility to 24‐electron C═O/C═N redox sites, enabling substantial active‐site utilization and a reduced activation energy of 10.31 kJ mol
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    . The dense redox‐active architecture of CAPT promotes fast and stable H
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    storage. Consequently, CAPT delivers a specific capacity of 558.2 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and high‐rate performance (180.7 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    at 30 A g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ). Remarkably, the proton battery based on the CAPT polymer anode exhibits an exceptional energy density at −60°C (83.88 Wh kg
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) and excellent cycling stability at −80°C (95.6% capacity retention over 8000 cycles). This work provides fundamental insights into the molecular design of multi‐electron organic polymer anodes for advanced proton batteries operating under extreme conditions.

items.abstract: <jats:p>Geometric calibration of a four-channel plane-mirror interferometer requires separating translation–yaw coupling from beam-pointing and mirror-orientation effects. This numerical study examines paired ranges acquired at matched positions with nonzero and zero yaw. A scaled analytic Jacobian identifies weak parameter combinations, and an equal-budget search compares 70 four-level yaw sets. The eight-parameter model has full local numerical rank but a condition number of 9.42×105. Fixing two mirror angles at their synthetic truth reduces the condition number to 2519. The selected yaw levels are {−2.4,−1.8,1.8,2.4} mrad. Four solver configurations are compared over 100 synthetic recalibrations. Their similar held-out residuals conceal differences in parameter recovery: an additive decomposition assigns 3.67 nm RMS to yaw-reference mismatch within a 3.70 nm total residual. Controlled noise/yaw switches further separate calibration-induced parameter error from validation-side mismatch. These results identify survey and angular-reference requirements for the declared geometry and provide a local numerical design screen; physical accuracy remains to be established experimentally.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Prestressed concrete (PSC) beam ends deteriorate faster when they are located underneath bridge deck expansion joints. Traditionally, inspection and maintenance decisions rely on subjective assessments of deterioration and often lack correlation with structural capacity. This paper presents a capacity-based condition matrix to support condition-state (CS) and request-for-action (RFA) decisions on deteriorated I-shaped PSC beam ends. A detailed methodology based on the strut-and-tie method was developed to assess beam-end capacity under various deterioration scenarios. The margin of safety and capacity-to-demand ratio were evaluated using experimental results and in-service bridge details, respectively. Sensitivity analyses were conducted, and a 15% capacity reduction was established as a threshold for RFA submission. According to the analysis results, capacity reduction is approximately proportional to the percentage of strands that are exposed while section loss or bearing area loss without exposed strands do not affect the beam-end shear capacity. The capacity-based beam-end condition matrix is a significant contribution to the state of the art and practice compared with the qualitative classifications or ratings given in current specifications and guidelines. This matrix streamlines the process of assigning CSs and RFA submissions, improving structural safety while minimizing unnecessary inspections and repairs.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Winged piles can significantly enhance the lateral capacity of deep foundations, yet their performance in Malan loess remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a combined experimental and numerical study of the lateral behavior of I-beam winged bored piles in loess, integrating reduced-scale laboratory tests on five pile configurations, a validated three-dimensional finite-element framework (mean absolute error 9.6% at the serviceability limit, s = 0.1D), and a 25-case prototype-scale parametric study. Mechanistically, the upper wing plates act as an embedded collar restraining shaft rotation: under identical lateral loads, the four-wing configuration reduced pile-head displacement by 22% and peak bending moment by 12% relative to a monopile. The rotation pivot point (z ≈ 0.73 L) and the critical section for maximum bending moment (z ≈ 0.385 L) remained essentially invariant across configurations, corroborating post-test flexural crack mapping. The number of wings (Nw) emerged as the sole first-order design variable, with the capacity-enhancement ratio captured by η = 1 + 0.0313(Nw − 1); within the investigated conditions, the four-wing pile gained approximately +10% capacity at s = 0.1D (η = 1.10), against only +1.6% for the two-wing configuration (η = 1.02). The enhancement ratio was insensitive to soil parameters within the investigated ranges (η = 1.07–1.11 across Es = 8–30 Mpa, c = 8–36 kPa, and φ = 20∘–25∘), wing embedment saturated at dw ≈ 1.0 m, and remaining geometric variations were secondary (within ±3–4%). The closed-form equation reproduced the 19 fitting cases with a mean absolute percentage error of 0.95% and predicted three independent hold-out cases between −4.2% and +2.4%. The validated framework provides an experimentally grounded lateral design methodology for winged piles in loess, addressing a gap in current Chinese foundation standards, including JGJ 94-2008.</jats:p>

                    <jats:italic>Purpose</jats:italic>
                    . A Geant4-based model was created to simulate radiation transport within a novel radiotherapy system developed by Convergent Radiotherapy and Radiosurgery (Convergent RnR; Haifa, Israel). This treatment device incorporates a Bragg-diffraction x-ray lens to focus x-rays from a conventional x-ray tube towards a small but finite focal spot with quasi-monoenergetic photons.
                    <jats:italic>Methods.</jats:italic>
                    The simulation model included an x-ray tube and a CRnR focusing lens consisting of single-crystal aluminum tiles. To validate the Geant4 model of this device, transverse and longitudinal in-air and in-water dose distributions from the converging beam field were calculated and compared to radiochromic film measurements.
                    <jats:italic>Results.</jats:italic>
                    The implemented Monte Carlo (MC) simulation model predicted a mean photon energy of 53.96 keV and showed agreement within 0.5% when compared with the SpekPy calculation. Both the simulation and experiment produced an attenuation characteristics of 3.2 mm Al. In-water tissue maximum ratios showed percentage differences ⩽3% at depths of 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, and 70 mm. Exceptions were observed at 80, and 85 mm, likely due to reduced film statistics, local dose variations, and positioning uncertainty. A gamma analysis of in-water scanning dose distributions demonstrated a >96% pass rate for the 2%/2 mm criterion and >99% for the 3%/3 mm criterion across all focal depths.
                    <jats:italic>Conclusions.</jats:italic>
                    In this study, CRnR’s converging beam radiotherapy system was implemented in Geant4 to demonstrate the device operation and characterize its physical and dosimetric outputs. The MC simulation implemented in this work successfully demonstrated converging dose distributions with Bragg-diffraction physics, which were in good agreement with radiochromic film measurements. This simulation model may be used to further refine the converging beam system design for clinical implementation, including validation of the treatment planning system.

items.abstract: <jats:p>Power grid operators face growing end-of-service-life pressure as aging transformers and transmission lines encounter renewal mandates, climate-intensified degradation, and renewable-integration stresses. Retirement decisions require transparent condition-assessment and prognostic evidence on whether to replace, refurbish, life-extend, or retain each asset. This review synthesizes evidence across aging standards, coupled environmental-stress degradation modeling, multi-criteria assessment, AI-driven remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, federated learning (FL), and explainable AI (XAI). Evidence is deepest for power transformers. Overhead-line studies chiefly address degradation, condition indices, thermal rating, and inspection; evidence for retirement-specific AI, FL, and XAI remains limited in this corpus. Other asset classes are treated selectively for methodological transferability. Task-level evidence is strongest for dissolved gas analysis and health-index assessment, whereas multi-criteria assessment and survival models provide structured decision inputs with limited utility-scale validation of retirement outcomes. Emerging approaches—attention-based Transformer architectures, federated learning, knowledge distillation, and neuro-symbolic reasoning—are constrained by sparse failure labels, cross-regional data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and limited explanation standards. A major gap persists: the weak coupling between climate-specific degradation physics, economic life-cycle optimization, and policy eligibility rules. Future work should prioritize hybrid digital-twin and AI frameworks integrating physical constraints, privacy-preserving collaboration, auditable explanations, and standardized validation datasets for defensible retirement decisions.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Shielding performance inferred from attenuation or nominal thickness can misrepresent the response of a finite semiconductor detector. This study uses Geant4 to map energy deposited in a silicon sensor of dimensions 20 mm × 20 mm × 0.5 mm behind polyethylene (PE) and PE–aluminium (PE–Al) shields under controlled photon, electron, and proton fields. Event-level scoring separates primary survival, residual entry energy, shield-generated secondaries, and finite shield coverage. The proton response was strongly non-monotonic near range-out: effective suppression occurred between 8–9 mm PE at 30 MeV and between 20–25 mm PE at 50 MeV, in agreement with NIST PSTAR projected ranges. For photons, short shield-to-sensor gaps increased silicon energy deposition, consistent with enhanced acceptance of shield-generated secondaries. At the final 100 mm gap, adding 0.5 mm Al to 25 mm PE improved the photon-response reduction by 3.083 ± 0.558 percentage points under the reference physics list; the uncertainty is a two-sided 95% sampling confidence-interval half-width and excludes physics-model uncertainty. An XCOM narrow-beam calculation gave 1.01 percentage points of additional uncollided primary-photon number removal, a different observable that cannot be subtracted from the detector-response change to quantify a secondary contribution. A finite-size test further showed that oblique protons could traverse an edge-clipped path in a nominally thick shield. Within the discrete candidate set, 25 mm PE was the lowest-mass configuration with positive mean response reduction in all four benchmark fields. These results define transport and geometry regimes that should be checked before a shielding design is advanced to mission-specific modelling or experimental qualification.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:p>INTRODUCTION: The pterygomaxillary space represents a complex anatomical region of considerable importance in oral and maxillofacial surgery, particularly in implant rehabilitation of the atrophic posterior maxilla. Its anatomical complexity arises from its close relationship with the infratemporal fossa, pterygopalatine fossa, nasal cavity, and orbit.
AIM: The aim of this lecture is to present the surgical and topographic anatomy of the pterygomaxillary region and highlight its clinical significance for the safety, predictability, and success of contemporary dental implantology.
LECTURE CONTENT: The lecture will address the topographic boundaries and anatomical relationships of the pterygomaxillary region, with particular emphasis on its communication with the infratemporal and pterygopalatine fossae. Important neurovascular structures within this region will be presented, including the terminal branches of the maxillary artery, the maxillary nerve (V2), the pterygopalatine ganglion, and associated venous structures. Special attention will be given to the clinical significance of these anatomical relationships in the planning and placement of pterygomaxillary implants in patients with severe bone atrophy. The role of preoperative three-dimensional radiological assessment, particularly cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), in evaluating anatomical variations, available bone volume, and relationships with adjacent structures will also be highlighted.
CONCLUSION: Detailed knowledge of the surgical and topographic anatomy of the pterygomaxillary region, combined with precise preoperative radiological assessment, is essential for appropriate planning and safe execution of pterygomaxillary implant placement. An individualized anatomical approach contributes to reducing surgical risks and achieving more predictable clinical outcomes.
 </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates the influence of L2 cache design parameters—including capacity, associativity, cluster topology, and private versus shared organization at the cluster level—on energy consumption and silicon area in clustered embedded multicore systems. To establish a foundational understanding of the architectural trade-offs, we first employ simulations using gem5 across eight MiBench benchmarks, together with area estimates from CACTI, identifying configurations that minimize energy and area, as well as those balancing both metrics. We then employ separate Random Forest regression models for energy and area to model these relationships based on simulation data, achieving R2 scores of 0.9970 for energy prediction and 0.9936 for area prediction on a held-out architectural test set. To examine how the definition of the energy objective influences architectural selection, we consider two distinct evaluation regimes. In Regime A, total L2 cache energy and absolute silicon area are minimized, whereas Regime B considers total L2 cache energy normalized by the number of cores assigned to the target benchmark, together with absolute cache area. Both regimes are evaluated on an eight-core system organized into different cluster configurations. Rather than relying exclusively on a single weighted score, our methodology addresses cache design trade-offs through multi-objective optimization. Pareto front analysis is used to identify non-dominated configurations, followed by TOPSIS ranking to assess potential compromises among these configurations. The results reveal that Regime A identifies workload-dependent minimum-energy cluster organizations, whereas Regime B consistently identifies single-cluster, eight-core configurations with 256 KB capacity and 8-way associativity under the adopted energy normalization. In Regime B, private and shared cache configurations exhibit identical objective values on the Pareto front. Consequently, TOPSIS cannot discriminate between solutions with identical objective values, and no unique global optimum is established across all benchmarks and evaluation regimes. These findings highlight the importance of objective formulation when interpreting energy-area trade-offs and selecting L2 cache architectures for embedded multicore systems.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Restricting the atom-centered
basis functions of the embedded subsystem to those centered on the subsystem itself (
                    <jats:italic>the monomer expansion approximation</jats:italic>
                    ) is commonly used in frozen-density embedding theory (FDET)
based simulations as well as in conventional QM/MM type of simulations. Despite its widespread use, its influence on the FDET results has rarely been investigated independently from another approximation—the one used for the non-additive kinetic-energy component of the embedding potential. In the present work, we disentangle these two sources of error by comparing monomer- and supermolecular basis expansions for a series of alkali-metal cation–radical complexes exhibiting widely different tendencies toward charge transfer. Additionally,
we show that the effective environment LUMO introduced by Englert
                    <jats:italic>et al</jats:italic>
                    (2026
                    <jats:italic>J. Chem. Phys.</jats:italic>
                    <jats:bold>164</jats:bold>
                    084122) remains a good predictive tool even if the monomer expansion is employed. It provides a unified physical interpretation of the influence of both the basis-set restriction and the approximation to the non-additive kinetic potential. These results clarify the conditions under which the monomer expansion constitutes a reliable approximation and provide guidelines for setting up approximations used in the FDET eigenvalue equation.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Two approaches to production planning were compared in a multi-stage production system and experimentally verified under actual operating conditions at an automotive-industry company. Under centralized planning, a common schedule was prepared for technologically and materially interdependent production orders. Under decentralized planning, individual departments generated and scheduled their own orders from aggregated demand. Forward, backward, and bottleneck-oriented scheduling were applied in both approaches. Order completion times, workstation busy times, due-date performance, and the relationship between departmental and system-wide results were analyzed. In centralized forward scheduling, mechanical processing accounted for the largest share of cumulative workstation busy time (54.87%). In decentralized planning, overall order completion depended on the coordination of local schedules, particularly the availability of components for assembly. The results showed that departmental performance alone was insufficient to assess the entire production system. They also distinguished late completion from the requirement to start production before the permitted release date. The two approaches had different information and coordination requirements, but the results did not establish an unconditional advantage for either approach.</jats:p>

<jats:p> Abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed visual effects (VFX) production, particularly in the areas of automated rotoscoping, matchmoving, and clean plate generation. These processes, which traditionally require extensive manual intervention, technical expertise, and considerable production time, are increasingly supported by AI-driven software and machine learning algorithms. Automated rotoscoping enables the identification and isolation of foreground objects from backgrounds, while AI-assisted matchmoving facilitates the tracking of camera movements and the integration of computer-generated elements into live-action footage. Similarly, clean plate generation uses intelligent image-processing techniques to reconstruct backgrounds by removing unwanted objects, wires, shadows, and other production elements. Although these technologies offer substantial improvements in production efficiency, their accuracy and reliability remain important considerations, particularly in complex production environments involving rapid movement, motion blur, transparent objects, intricate edges, lighting variations, and dynamic backgrounds. This article examines the applications of AI in automated rotoscoping, matchmoving, and clean plate generation, with particular emphasis on evaluating accuracy, consistency, processing efficiency, and production suitability. It also discusses the challenges associated with AI-generated visual effects and proposes an evaluation framework incorporating quantitative and qualitative performance indicators. The study highlights the importance of combining automated workflows with professional human supervision to achieve reliable and production-ready visual effects.

Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Automated Rotoscoping, Matchmoving, Clean Plate Generation.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Tungsten (W) is a prominent plasma-facing material for deuterium–tritium (D–T) fusion reactors, yet T fuel retention in W poses critical challenges to safety and operational viability. This study systematically compares three baking methods—vacuum baking, H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    gas atmosphere baking, and hydrogen (H) plasma baking—for removing D retained in W at 513 K, simulating realistic conditions for T removal in reactors. Experimental results demonstrate that D removal efficiencies reach 75% for vacuum baking after 16 h, 83% for H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    atmosphere baking after 16 h, and 99% for H plasma baking after 1 h. The superior performance of H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    atmosphere and H plasma baking is primarily driven by hydrogen isotope (HI) exchange, with efficiency strongly dependent on the concentration of H introduced into W. Higher H concentrations promote more complete exchange, leading to significantly reduced D retention. A multi-isotope Fill Level model was developed to simulate the end-to-end H plasma exchange process. The simulation reproduces the experimentally observed D removal kinetics and the emergence of HD desorption, with the D retention in good agreement with measurements. The pronounced disparity between H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    atmosphere baking and H plasma baking is fundamentally governed by the quantity of H entering W: H plasma promotes significantly greater H ingress, thereby enhancing HI exchange and resulting in a drastic reduction in D retention. This work provides both experimental validation and modeling support for HI exchange as an efficient T removal strategy.
                  </jats:p>

title: Rényi Entropy Production for Markov Chains: Kolmogorov–Nagumo Averages, Fluctuation Symmetry and Detailed Balance

affiliation.name: Dipartimento di Matematica “Tullio Levi-Civita”, Università di Padova, via Trieste 63, 35131 Padova, Italy

items.abstract: <jats:p>In stochastic thermodynamics, entropy production is defined as the average, over all possible evolutions of a system, of an observable that measures the asymmetry between a trajectory and its time reversal. It admits several equivalent formulations, among them the difference between time-reversed and direct path entropies and the Kullback–Leibler divergence between forward and backward path measures. Replacing the linear average with the exponential Kolmogorov–Nagumo average, the step that leads from Shannon to Rényi entropy, we show that this equivalence is lost: the exponential analogues of the entropy-difference and of the divergence formulations become two different quantities, a difference between a Rényi cross-entropy and a Rényi entropy, and the Rényi divergence between path measures. Only the latter qualifies as a Rényi entropy production. For finite-state Markov chains, both rates are non-negative, vanish if and only if detailed balance holds, and reduce to the usual entropy production in the Shannon limit; the Rényi divergence rate is also governed by the cumulant generating function of entropy production and satisfies a Gallavotti–Cohen-type symmetry. An explicit three-state example illustrates the results.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Type of the article: Research ArticleBilal Tawfeeq Younes, - Corresponding author, email: bilal.tawfeeq@uomosul.edu.iqAbstractManufacturing organizations face increasing pressure to reduce energy use and environmental burdens while maintaining reliable production. This study examines the association between perceived green energy management and perceived sustainability of production processes at the employee-perception level and tests the statistical indirect association through perceived environmental innovation in a single production plant of Al-Hikma Pharmaceuticals and Medical Supplies Company in Baghdad, Iraq, analyzed as an in-depth single-organization case. A quantitative cross-sectional survey yielded 320 usable employee responses from production-related, engineering and maintenance, quality assurance, supply chain, health-safety-and-environment, and managerial departments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 showed that perceived green energy management was positively associated with perceived environmental innovation (β = 0.584, p &amp;lt; 0.001) and perceived sustainability of production processes (β = 0.330, p &amp;lt; 0.001). Perceived environmental innovation was also positively associated with perceived sustainability of production processes (β = 0.346, p &amp;lt; 0.001). The specific indirect association was significant (β = 0.202, 95% CI [0.143, 0.261], p &amp;lt; 0.001); the direct association remained significant, indicating a pattern consistent with partial mediation. The model explained 34.1% of the variance in perceived environmental innovation and 36.3% in perceived sustainability of production processes.</jats:p>

title: Collaborative storytelling as a practice of feminist knowledge production
﻿Design of a PBL-based Immersive Content Production Curriculum
container-title: Journal of Problem Based Learning in Higher Education
items.abstract: <jats:p>This case describes the design and implementation of a Problem-Based Learning (PBL) course in immersive content production and reports students’ and experts’ perceptions of it. Although the immersive content industry is expanding, systematic curricula are scarce. The 15-week course, “3D·VFX Content Production Practice,” was taught to 29 third-year media content students. In weeks 1–7, students built skills in Substance Painter and Unreal Engine; in weeks 8–15, six teams responded to an ill-structured client scenario by producing interactive 3D videos of local sites in Chungbuk, Korea. Data were drawn from a survey, reflective journals, team artifacts and interviews with three industry experts. Students described growth in self-directed learning, creative design and team communication, and 62% reported being satisfied. Experts judged the workflow close to industry practice. Teamwork burden and problem complexity emerged as challenges, suggesting that problem scope should match students’ skills and teams be formed deliberately.</jats:p>

title: ALGAE-BASED BIOFERTILIZERS: PRODUCTION, AGRICULTURAL APPLICATIONS AND SUSTAINABILITY

affiliation.name: Department of Botany, Ram Dayalu Singh (R.D.S.) College, Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (BRABU), Muzaffarpur, Bihar, India.

container-title: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
items.abstract: <jats:p>Interest in algae-based biofertilizers has grown because they are rich in nutrients, promote plant growth and offer a more sustainable option than chemical fertilizers. Microalgae, macroalgae and cyanobacteria support crop productivity in three ways: they enrich the soil with nutrients, fix nitrogen and produce biologically active compounds. This review covers how these biofertilizers are made and formulated, from cultivation systems and biomass harvesting to the different product forms available. It also looks at their use in agriculture, mainly for better seed germination, root development, nutrient uptake, soil fertility and crop yield. The environmental benefits are highlighted as well, namely nutrient recovery from wastewater, use of carbon dioxide and a reduced need for chemical fertilizers. Yet some limitations persist. Production is expensive, formulations can be unstable, contamination is a risk and field performance is not consistent. Even so, algae-based biofertilizers are a promising route towards sustainable agriculture and better environmental management.</jats:p>

title: Machine-Learning-Based Prediction of Production Disruptions in Supply Chains
A Review of Research on RFID-Based Automatic Identification Systems for Mixed-Model Production
items.abstract: <jats:p>With the continued advancement of intelligent manufacturing strategies and the sustained growth of demand for personalized customization, manufacturing enterprises are accelerating the transformation of their production modes from traditional high-volume, single-variety production lines to flexible mixed-model production with multiple varieties and small batches. While improving flexibility, mixed-model production introduces a series of management difficulties, including diverse workpiece types, intersecting process routes, and frequent material distribution. Traditional barcode and quick response (QR) code identification technologies are gradually showing limitations in long-distance reading, parallel processing of multiple targets, and adaptation to harsh environments. Radio frequency identification (RFID) technology has become a core supporting technology for solving these problems because of its contactless operation, long reading distance, penetration-based identification of multiple targets, and strong resistance to interference. This paper systematically reviews research progress on RFID technology in multi-variety, small-batch mixed-model production. It first describes the fundamentals of RFID technology and the core characteristics of the mixed-model production mode. It then compares the three mainstream identification technologies of barcodes, QR codes, and RFID. On this basis, a layered system architecture comprising a perception layer, network layer, data layer, and application layer is constructed, and the integration of RFID middleware with digital twin technology is discussed. The evolution of key technologies is reviewed, with emphasis on multi-tag anti-collision algorithms, including ALOHA-based, tree-based, hybrid, and machine-learning-based algorithms, as well as high-precision positioning and tracking methods based on received signal strength indicator (RSSI), phase, and holography. Typical cases in bearing manufacturing, garment production, and automotive mixed-model assembly are used to analyze practical application results. Finally, the paper discusses trends in the deep integration of RFID with artificial intelligence, digital twins, passive Internet of Things technologies, and green low-carbon manufacturing, and identifies current research challenges and open problems, with the aim of providing a scientific basis for decision-making by manufacturing enterprises undertaking digital and intelligent production-line transformation.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This study aims to examine the effect of agricultural public expenditures on agricultural production in the EU-27 countries and Türkiye using annual data for the period 2001-2023. Agricultural value added is employed as a proxy for agricultural production, while agricultural employment and agricultural land are included in the model as control variables. Second-generation panel data methods are employed to account for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity. The stationarity properties of the variables are examined using the Cross-Sectionally Augmented Dickey-Fuller test, while long-run coefficients are estimated using the Augmented Mean Group estimator. The baseline model results indicate positive and statistically significant relationships between agricultural public expenditures, agricultural employment, and agricultural value added for the overall panel. However, the coefficient of agricultural public expenditures loses its statistical significance in alternative model specifications that control for fertilizer use and agricultural capital stock. Furthermore, the coefficient of agricultural land is found to be negative and statistically insignificant for the overall panel.</jats:p>

title: The Superhero Media Production Goes Darker: The Dawn of Superhero Horror

affiliation.name: University of Ss. Cyril and Methodius in Trnava

items.abstract: <jats:p>Media productions inspired by superhero comic books represented a global media megatrend in the first two decades of the 21st century. However, even before reaching its peak, this trend began to encounter audience fatigue with superheroes. In an effort to continue capitalising on this trend and revitalise audience interest, a new approach in production can be observed, commencing with the tendency of incorporating darker superheroes and horror elements and culminating in more graphic and explicit content, which even led to an increase in the age ratings from PG-13 to R for some released titles. The ultimate result is the emergence of media works that are inspired by or based on comic superheroes but presented using the conventions and expressive techniques of the horror genre, possibly representing a new genre in mainstream media production – superhero horror. The study examines this approach in superhero media production to reflect on its scope by analysing examples from recently released films, TV series and digital games, as well as the planned direction of superhero media universes. A partial objective is to define the superhero horror subgenre and its potential influence on the future development of superhero media productions across various media, based on an analysis of the current state of the market and a case study of a representative title of this genre. The study indicates how dark superhero media titles already are today, and how (terrifying) they could become in the future.</jats:p>

<jats:p>Subject. This article looks at a mix of theoretical, methodological, and practical questions about organizing internal audits of the use of drones in crop farming in the context of the digitalization of the agro-industrial complex. 
Objectives. The article aims to develop theoretical principles and practical recommendations for organizing internal audits of agro-drones usage in crop production, an audit methodology that includes checking the validity of routes and application rates, monitoring the completeness and quality of work, evaluating resource use efficiency, as well as creating an algorithm for integrating telemetry data into the accounting system for automated material write-offs. 
Methods. For the study, we used analysis and synthesis, a systems approach, classification, comparison, generalization, as well as risk management methods and modeling of control procedures. 
Results. The article presents an author-developed three-level methodology for internal auditing of agro-drone usage and proposes an algorithm for integrating telemetry data into the accounting system, consisting of seven consecutive steps – from creating a digital flight mission to monitoring deviations by the internal audit service. The article also presents an author-developed form of an electronic primary document, the Log of Agro-Drone Performed Operations, which ensures the transformation of technical information into an accounting document. 
Conclusions and Relevance. The proposed method and algorithm create
a closed-loop system for managing the use of agro-drones – from planning flight missions to material write-offs and evaluating effectiveness. The approach ensures accurate accounting by automatically generating primary documents based on verified telemetry data, preventing unwarranted resource write-offs. This turns internal auditing into a tool for managing the risks of digitalizing crop production. The results obtained can be used by internal audit services and management of agricultural organizations of various sizes to improve control and risk management systems when implementing drone technologies, and they can also be applied in the educational process when training specialists in economic security, auditing, and accounting in the agricultural sector.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Subsurface hydrogen (H2) production offers a promising alternative to energy-intensive surface electrolysis by using the Earth’s natural and geochemical processes. However, the technical feasibility of different production pathways remains an important challenge. To address this, this review establishes a unified framework comparing three major pathways: mineral-, thermal-, and hydrocarbon-sourced H2. We assess the operational trade-offs of each system. Mineral-sourced pathways face severe uncertainties regarding deep exploration and caprock containment. Thermal-sourced systems are strictly constrained by geographic scarcity and equipment degradation. Within hydrocarbon-sourced pathways, thermochemical methods are highly scalable but require extensive carbon management. Consequently, the microbial degradation of residual oil emerges as a strategic alternative that bypasses the need for new drilling by repurposing existing petroleum infrastructure. Because this microbial pathway offers unique near-term potential, this review closely examines the critical gap between theoretical laboratory yields and actual reservoir-scale recovery. We highlight the subsurface mass-balance dynamics that govern net H2 production, demonstrating how competing microorganisms and multi-phase flow limitations act as severe subsurface losses. Ultimately, this review establishes that commercializing subsurface biohydrogen relies not only on stimulating generation but on actively overcoming these complex retention and recovery barriers.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Cheese whey is a source of bioactive peptides whose potential as functional food ingredients depends on which sequences are released during processing and what happens to them after ingestion. This review examines enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation, and physical pretreatments for peptide production and assesses the evidence for blood pressure regulation, glycemic control, antioxidant activity, and other bioactivities. It also evaluates how polymeric nanoparticles, liposomes, hydrogels, and emulsions address bitterness, gastrointestinal degradation, and barriers to intestinal absorption. Human intervention studies report changes in serum urate and selected cognitive outcomes for specific hydrolysates or peptide-enriched preparations, with limited evidence linking these effects to individual sequences. Encapsulation can improve digestive stability or epithelial transport in experimental models, while evidence for improved bioavailability in humans remains limited. For practical development, manufacturers should select the carrier according to the intended site of action, quantify marker peptides after processing and storage in the finished food, and validate the efficacy and safety of the intended serving in controlled human studies.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:p>Subject. Factors determining the dynamics of nickel production in Russia.
Objectives. To identify the factors influencing the volume of nickel production in Russia, as well as to assess the nature of the interrelationships between nickel production, world nickel prices, the exchange rate of the US dollar against the ruble and investments in fixed assets.
Methods. The information base of the study was the annual data for 2006–2024. Methods of descriptive statistics, correlation and regression analysis, logarithmic modeling, time series stationarity tests, information criteria for choosing the lag length, Granger causality tests, cointegration analysis, ARDL approach and error correction model are used. Additionally, the sensitivity of the results to the structural periods of 2008–2009, 2020 and 2022–2024 and the exclusion of observations for 2021 was checked.
Results. A moderate negative relationship has been revealed between the volume of nickel production and the exchange rate of the US dollar against the ruble. Linear and logarithmic regression models showed a statistically significant negative correlation of nickel production only with the exchange rate, whereas no statistically significant coefficients were obtained for world nickel prices and fixed asset investments. Granger's causality tests did not reveal stable short-term predictive relationships. The Johansen test and the ARDL bounds test did not provide convincing evidence of a long-term cointegration relationship. A negative and statistically significant error correction factor in the reduced ECM showed the presence of a dynamic correction mechanism. The main result for the exchange rate remains after excluding the observation for 2021.
Conclusions. The development of the Russian nickel industry is explained not only by the macroeconomic factors considered, but also depends on a wider range of long-term industry and institutional conditions.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The Paralympic Games, a global sporting event that features athletes with physical disabilities, are growing in terms of digital engagement, rights-holding broadcasters, and audience reach. While scholarship on the global circuits of Paralympic media production sheds light on differences between countries, the Central and Eastern European region remains understudied. This paper examines the structural conditions for the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Paralympic Games in Slovenia, Poland, and Hungary to better understand how media systems with a shared history of post-socialist transition, yet distinct sport priorities, navigated the coverage. Drawing on the comparing media systems framework from a contextualist perspective, we identify three distinct factors that shape coverage: the structure of public service media, the role of governing bodies and news agencies, and political circumstances. While similarities exist in how media organizations in the three countries used content supplied by the International Paralympic Committee (IPC), notable differences can be observed in their outputs and approaches to coverage. Despite the IPC’s evidence suggesting growth in the global reach of the Paralympics, structural barriers on the national levels exist that limit audience access to content.</jats:p>
