<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Patients receiving radiotherapy for esophageal cancer may consult large language model chatbots about treatment-related adverse effects, but the safety of their advice is uncertain. We submitted 42 researcher-developed, patient-oriented questions once each to ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao through public web interfaces, obtaining 168 responses. Five blinded expert raters assessed potential harm, accuracy, and perceived empathic communication; information quality, visible source transparency, and formula-based readability were also evaluated. Twenty-one responses (12.5%) were classified as potentially unsafe; six could delay clinical assessment and ten involved potentially harmful self-management advice. Unsafe-response proportions ranged from 7.1% to 16.7% across models, with no statistically significant overall difference (Cochran’s Q = 1.981,

                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                     < 0.001, W = 0.149). Visible source-transparency indicators were limited, and formula-estimated readability differed across models. These single-query findings indicate that favorable accuracy ratings do not preclude potentially unsafe advice and cannot establish stable model rankings, patient comprehension, or clinical outcomes.

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tungsten (W) remains unclear. Here, we compare the surface morphology evolution and subsurface bubble distributions of coarse-grained and nano-grained W under fusion-relevant He plasma irradiation. The samples were exposed simultaneously to 90 eV He ions at 1173 K. Although both microstructures ultimately developed similar fuzz composed of nanoscale tendrils, their early-stage evolution of surface roughening exhibited distinct differences. In the nano-grained W film, ∼600 nm thick, surface roughening was initiated by anomalous bubble growth at grain junctions. In contrast, coarse-grained W exhibited pronounced crystallographic-orientation-dependent roughening. Subsequent tendril nucleation and growth occurred in both microstructures, preferentially at highly convex surface regions. Moreover, subsurface bubbles were confined mainly to a shallow region approximately 100–200 nm beneath coarse-grained W, whereas they permeated the entire nano-grained film. These results indicate that GB-mediated bubble dynamics primarily govern surface evolution during the fuzz-incubation stage, while interface curvature and capillary-driven diffusion dominate tendril nucleation and subsequent growth. Thus, GBs exert a decisive influence during early-stage surface roughening but have limited effect on the later development of fuzz. These findings provide insight into the distinct and common mechanisms governing He-induced surface modification in W with different grain sizes and support a capillary-growth framework for fuzz formation.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>In this study, the effects of coronatine (COR) treatment on bioactive compounds, glucosinolate metabolism and hypoglycemic activity of broccoli and radish sprouts under UV-A irradiation were investigated. COR treatment increased the contents of phenolics and ascorbic acid in broccoli and radish sprouts under UV-A irradiation. Furthermore, genes and transcription factors involved in glucosinolate biosynthesis were significantly upregulated following COR treatment under UV-A irradiation, thereby promoting glucosinolate accumulation. Meanwhile, COR treatment increased sulforaphane and sulforaphene formation in broccoli and radish sprouts, respectively, with these increases coinciding with enhanced glucosinolate levels and myrosinase activity under UV-A irradiation. These results indicate that COR treatment could enhance glucosinolate biosynthesis and hydrolysis, thereby promoting the accumulation of glucosinolates and their hydrolysis products in broccoli and radish sprouts. Additionally, broccoli and radish sprouts alleviated glucose and lipid metabolism disorders induced by a high-fat diet and streptozotocin. Moreover, broccoli sprouts exhibited stronger hypoglycemic activity than radish sprouts both in vitro and in vivo. Overall, COR treatment enhanced the nutritional and hypoglycemic potential of broccoli and radish sprouts under UV-A irradiation. This finding supports the potential application of COR treatment for developing functional foods based on sprouts.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Data-driven lithium-ion battery state-of-health (SoH) estimation can appear to be accurate when the input signals contain closely related information to the capacity-based target or when training and test observations originate from the same cell. This study examines information admissibility and generalization using 16 CALCE and NASA batteries. The SoH is reconstructed from raw discharge records, and a declared 70–100% capacity retention scope is employed. A separate constant protocol analysis removes this target-based range restriction. Histogram-based gradient boosting (HGB) is assessed using nested leave-one-battery-out validation, training-only feature selection, and equal-battery evaluation. The constant-protocol cohort comprises 4590 observations from 10 cells; the variable-protocol cohort comprises 165 independently labeled observations from 6 cells. Full-discharge HGB achieved mean battery-level RMSEs of 1.500 SoH percentage points from electrical features and 1.333 when cycle age was included, although a paired battery bootstrap interval for the age-related improvement crossed zero. Under variable protocols, pooling a retrospective CALCE task with a pre-reference NASA task, electrical-plus-age HGB attained an RMSE of 2.697 and did not outperform age-only linear regression (2.003); the same ordering held within each source separately. Their paired battery-level RMSE difference (HGB minus linear age) was +0.694 percentage points with a 95% interval of [+0.174, +1.160]. A feature audit identified full-discharge derivative statistics that are strongly associated with reciprocal capacity, limiting claims of capacity independence despite the exclusion of explicit capacity integrals. When feature extraction was censored at the first 3.6 V crossing, HGB RMSE increased to 2.282 without age and 1.716 with age (4589 cycles); a fixed first 600 s observation achieved 1.366 and 1.126, respectively (4590 cycles). Tuned LSTM and transformer models using raw 3.6 V prefixes did not outperform the engineered-feature HGB under the evaluated protocols. At 3.6 V, returned age-only HGB had an RMSE of 5.636 on the same 4589 cycles compared with 2.282 for censored electrical HGB. Zero-shot NASA-to-CALCE and CALCE-to-NASA transfer increased the electrical-only RMSE to 4.424 and 3.055, respectively, under shifts in chemistry, cell format, cycling conditions, and capacity reference procedures. A post hoc CALCE charge/discharge completeness screen removed 89 observations; across the 4501 retained test cycles, retrained HGB improved RMSE from 1.465 to 1.114 without age and from 1.298 to 1.091 with age, relative to the original models evaluated on identical observations. Without SoH-based range selection, the constant-protocol full-discharge study included 6299 cycles and achieved RMSEs of 2.288/2.195 for electrical-only/electrical-plus-age HGB. These results delineate the value and limitations of electrical predictors under explicitly defined observation windows, protocol quality controls, and dataset shift; they do not establish generalized accuracy for field deployment.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Abdominal pain is a prevalent consequence of both gastrointestinal surgery and an important symptom of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Despite advances in medical treatments, patients with IBD continue to have a significant lifetime risk of requiring surgery. Patients with IBD may experience pain of varying intensity when compared to non-IBD patients, this may complicate assessment and management of pain, including challenges with daily- and post-operative pain management in those with hyperalgesia and difficulties managing late-stage presentation of complex intra-abdominal disease in those with hypoalgesia. The perception of pain is multifactorial, and like the idiopathic aetiology of IBD is likely to have genetic and environmental contributors. There has been increasing interest in the role of voltage gated channels Nav 1.7, 1.8 and 1.9 in visceral pain transmission, the expression of which is genetically determined. This review aims to summarise the literature linking sodium channels Nav 1.7, 1.8 and 1.9, abdominal pain and IBD, including a focus on therapeutic potential.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>This critical review evaluates whether C-terminal proendothelin-1 (CT-proET-1) improves short-term mortality prediction in adults with sepsis beyond routine clinical assessment, including illness severity and lactate when available. In a mixed intensive care cohort that included patients with sepsis, higher CT-proET-1 was associated with mortality after adjustment for age and lactate. Among patients with septic shock, discrimination between survivors and nonsurvivors varied across studies. The ratio of CT-proET-1 to mid-regional proadrenomedullin was associated with mortality in two studies, but these analyses did not isolate the contribution of CT-proET-1. None of the reviewed studies independently validated an improvement in mortality prediction from adding CT-proET-1 to routine clinical assessment, with or without mid-regional proadrenomedullin. An elevated concentration may accompany organ dysfunction and increased risk, but does not identify a specific, reversible vascular disorder or establish a basis for modifying treatment.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background and Clinical Significance: Gastric-type adenocarcinoma (GAS) is the most common human papillomavirus (HPV)-independent adenocarcinoma of the cervix. Because it arises deep in the endocervical canal, can look deceptively bland, and is not detected by HPV testing, its diagnosis is often delayed. Case Presentation: A 57-year-old woman had six months of postmenopausal bleeding. At a local hospital, a Pap smear was read as atrophic vaginitis, and her bleeding improved after hysteroscopic polypectomy and curettage. One week later, surveillance computed tomography for a resected benign mesenteric tumor incidentally showed a 2.7 × 2.6 cm cervical mass. High-risk HPV testing was negative, CA19-9 rose from 42 to 73 U/mL (5.2 U/mL after surgery), and biopsy showed adenocarcinoma in situ. Radical hysterectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy revealed a 3.3 cm HPV-independent GAS with deep-third stromal invasion, no lymphovascular invasion, and 25 negative nodes (FIGO 2018 stage IB2). The tumor was p16-negative, ER/PR-negative, and diffusely CK7-positive, with null-pattern p53 staining. No adjuvant therapy was given. Conclusions: This case adds a documented interval of one week between polypectomy and CT detection of a 2.7 cm tumor, the course of CA19-9 around surgery, and the reasoning for observation without adjuvant therapy in stage IB2 disease. Improvement of bleeding after polypectomy did not exclude a coexisting cervical mass; when sampling is limited or clinical, imaging, and pathological findings are discordant, the evaluation should continue. A negative HPV test, mildly elevated CA19-9, and a p16-negative, p53-aberrant mucinous adenocarcinoma are supportive but nonspecific clues that should prompt consideration of GAS, not establish it.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Breast ultrasound lesion segmentation and image-level diagnostic classification are closely related tasks. However, existing multi-task approaches often rely mainly on shared encoded features, without explicitly exploiting lesion localization information for classification, and may suffer from gradient competition between segmentation and classification objectives. This study proposes MT-RWKV, a lightweight multi-task framework for joint breast ultrasound lesion segmentation and three-class image-level classification. Methods: MT-RWKV uses a shared Vision-RWKV backbone, a progressive segmentation decoder with a high-resolution edge bypass, and Residual Mask Gating for segmentation-guided classification. A mask-path gradient scaler controls classification feedback to the segmentation branch. Performance on BUSI and BUS-UCLM was summarized using five-fold cross-validation. Thresholds were selected on validation data and fixed for test evaluation. Additional experiments examined gradient scaling, multi-task optimization, mask correction, and computational efficiency. Results: MT-RWKV achieved a Dice score of 83.09 ± 0.75%, classification accuracy of 94.87 ± 0.45%, and AUC of 98.12 ± 0.18% on BUSI. On BUS-UCLM, Dice was 94.53 ± 0.45%, accuracy was 97.07 ± 0.67%, and AUC was 98.06 ± 0.43%. Values represent means ± standard deviations across five folds. The model contained 6.98 million parameters and required 12.46 GFLOPs, with an inference time of 9.83 ms per image in the common efficiency benchmark. Conclusions: Explicit segmentation guidance and controlled mask-path feedback supported joint lesion localization and three-class classification on two public breast ultrasound benchmarks. MT-RWKV combined favorable predictive performance with a compact shared architecture.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Hospital-acquired pneumonia, particularly in intensive care unit (ICU) settings, remains a leading global healthcare challenge. Resolving the etiology of lower respiratory tract infections relies on clinical data, microscopy, culture, and molecular methods. While multiplex molecular panels can detect genetic material from fastidious organisms or bacterial remnants post-antibiotic initiation, a positive result does not definitively prove the presence of viable pathogens or their etiological role. Given the substantial costs and limited routine feasibility of molecular diagnostics, there is an urgent need for tools to optimize their application in daily clinical practice. This study aimed to evaluate the concordance between multiplex PCR molecular diagnostics and conventional microbiological cultures of lower respiratory tract specimens, accounting for the spectrum of detected pathogens, semi-quantitative molecular loads, and agar-based culture results. Furthermore, we aimed to propose a diagnostic algorithm to support clinical decision-making. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 163 endotracheal aspirate results obtained via intubation from adult, mechanically ventilated ICU patients at the Governor’s Specialist Hospital in Lublinie between October 2023 and December 2025 who presented with suspected bacterial pneumonia. Exclusion criteria included an age under 18 years and the administration of antibiotic therapy ≤ 7 days prior to sample collection. Multiplex PCR molecular testing evaluated specific pathogen species, viral–bacterial co-infections, and log-transformed semi-quantitative loads (104–107 copies/mL). These results were correlated with direct Gram-stained smear microscopic evaluations (Gram-positive/Gram-negative bacteria) and quantitative agar-based microbiological cultures (Columbia, Chocolate, MacConkey, and Chapman agars) processed according to current diagnostic standards. Results: Bacterial genetic material was detected by multiplex PCR in 114 identifications (69.9%), with polymicrobial infections (≥2 species) observed in 65 cases (39.9%). The overall concordance between multiplex PCR and culture was 81.6% (133/163); 29 cases (17.8%) were PCR-positive but culture-negative. The overall concordance between direct microscopy (Gram stain) and culture was 86.5% (95% CI: 80.2–91.0%), and Cohen’s kappa (κ) coefficient was 0.720, demonstrating substantial agreement (p = 0.383 via McNemara’s test). Analysis of 112 identifications with available semi-quantitative PCR results revealed a statistically significant positive correlation between the molecular load and culture positivity (ρ = 0.517; p < 0.001), as well as direct smear visibility (ρ = 0.475; p < 0.001). A one-log increase in PCR load was associated with a 3.18-fold higher odds of culture positivity (95% CI: 2.03–4.97; p < 0.001) and a 2.55-fold higher odds of microscopic visualization (95% CI: 1.71–3.83; p < 0.001). For a molecular load of 107 copies/mL, positive cultures were obtained in 91.3% of specimens, whereas at 104 copies/mL, the culture positivity rate was only 18.8%. Conclusions: Multiplex PCR assays demonstrate high sensitivity and frequently detect polymicrobial profiles, complicating independent etiological interpretation. The semi-quantitative molecular load strongly correlates with microscopic visualization and culture confirmation; however, it should not serve as an isolated criterion for initiating antimicrobial therapy. The highest diagnostic utility is achieved through an integrated, 3-step interpretation model combining PCR results, Gram staining, and conventional culture with the patient’s current clinical status, thereby enabling effective diagnostic and antimicrobial stewardship.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates additional cancer detection and observed changes in surgical management associated with preoperative contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM). Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched through October 2026. Eligible reports evaluated preoperative CEM in adults with breast cancer. R.F. and C.M.K. assessed eligibility and extracted data; QUADAS-2 assessed diagnostic/staging studies. Only patient-level management-change outcomes were quantitatively pooled, using logit-scale random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung–Knapp 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Additional cancer detection and other outcomes were synthesized descriptively and narratively. Certainty was discussed qualitatively without formal GRADE ratings. PROSPERO: CRD420261551170. No external funding was received. Results: Thirteen studies were included. Four observational cohorts reported breast-surgery or localization changes in 149/713 patients; the pooled proportion was 21.8% (95% CI, 14.9–30.7%; I2 = 52.5%). Excluding a mixed neoadjuvant-treatment cohort yielded 22.5% (95% CI, 11.0–40.5%). An exploratory analysis of broader treatment changes yielded 22.1% (95% CI, 18.0–27.0%) across six cohorts and 892 patients. Additional-cancer detection varied across four lesion-level comparisons with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); no pooled paired comparative effect was estimated. Single-database coverage, only four primary cohorts, imprecision, and selection and verification concerns limited confidence. Conclusions: Preoperative CEM was associated with observed changes in breast surgery or localization in selected cohorts. The pooled estimate of 21.8% represents management-change frequency and does not establish clinical benefit or diagnostic equivalence to MRI. Prospective comparative evidence is needed to determine whether these changes improve patient outcomes.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is rare in preschool children, and evidence for catheter-directed reperfusion predominantly concerns adolescents. Inferior vena cava (IVC) filter traversal is documented in adults but not in pediatric patients undergoing pulmonary reperfusion. Case Presentation: A normotensive 4-year-old girl was transferred after approximately 3 weeks of unsuccessful antibiotic treatment for presumed pneumonia. Doppler ultrasonography and CT venography identified occlusive left iliac and femoropopliteal deep venous thrombosis (DVT); computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE. She had elevated troponin levels and mild pulmonary hypertension. Reduced acute-phase protein S activity despite normal antigen levels raised the suspicion of inherited thrombophilia. Bilateral single-access trans-filter catheter-directed thrombolysis (SATF-CDT) was performed through a single femoral venous access, with both catheters traversing a pre-placed retrievable IVC filter. Following mechanical fragmentation, alteplase (10 mg) was administered by bilateral pulse spray and infused into each pulmonary artery. Selective angiography demonstrated near-total left and partial right main pulmonary artery occlusion. Completion angiography confirmed restored bilateral distal perfusion without a significant residual thrombus. Oxygen support was discontinued, troponin levels normalized, and pulmonary hypertension was no longer observed. No bleeding or immediate procedural complications occurred. Uneventful filter retrieval followed at 5 weeks; she remained well on enoxaparin without bleeding. Conclusions: SATF-CDT appears feasible in preschool children and may reduce venous access sites and procedural radiation. PE should be considered when presumed pneumonia persists; acute-phase thrombophilia findings require cautious interpretation.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Early identification of patients progressing toward brain death may reduce missed organ donation opportunities. We aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable natural language processing (NLP) model using admission brain computed tomography (CT) reports. Methods: This single-centre retrospective study included 161 adults admitted between 2011 and 2024, of whom 94 subsequently fulfilled brain death criteria and 67 did not. Predictors were derived exclusively from admission CT reports using rule-based preprocessing and term frequency–inverse document frequency word-level 1–3-gram features, without a curated vocabulary. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and Support Vector Machine models were evaluated using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation with 20 repetitions. Vectorisation, calibration and threshold selection were restricted to training partitions. A sensitivity target of at least 95% guided threshold selection. Confidence intervals were estimated using patient-cluster bootstrap resampling, and interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results: Logistic Regression achieved the highest mean ROC-AUC of 0.812 (95% CI 0.741–0.878), with a sensitivity of 94.1% and a specificity of 42.6%. Differences between models were relatively small, and the sensitivity target was not consistently achieved during validation. SHAP identified radiological expressions associated with severe neurological injury, alongside linguistic and report-related terms. Exploratory temporal analyses and documentary negative controls suggested potential confounding related to reporting practices and case selection. Conclusions: Admission CT reports may provide useful information for automated identification of patients at risk of subsequent brain death. However, limited specificity, temporal confounding and the absence of external validation preclude conclusions regarding clinical utility. Prospective multicentre studies are needed to establish generalisability and evaluate the potential contribution of NLP-assisted screening to donor-recognition pathways.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Breast cancer diagnosis from histopathological images must include accurate categorization, reliable uncertainty assessment, comprehensible evidence, and clinically significant reporting. Although deep learning-based histopathological classification has made significant progress, current methods often rely on single-model representations and do not provide sufficient approaches to manage prediction error and incorporate complementary morphological information across geographic scales. Furthermore, categorization, explainability, and clinical reporting are treated as separate tasks, creating a gap between image-level prediction and workflow-based clinical decision support. Methods: In this study, we propose a Task-Delegation Multi-Agent System (MAS) incorporating a Generalist Perception Agent (GPA), a Specialist Perception Agent (SPA), and a Clinical Reasoning Agent (CRA) to address these limitations. The GPA (BreastCareNet-G) handles routine cases using multi-scale CNN feature fusion, while the SPA (BreastCareNet-S) acts as a ViT-based consultant for complex morphological patterns. Instead of simple linear routing, we introduce a confidence-driven delegation protocol (0.85 threshold) where the GPA autonomously escalates ambiguous cases to the SPA. In scenarios of persistent evidence conflict, where both perception agents fail to meet the confidence threshold, the CRA (an LLM-based agent) intervenes to analyze the discrepancy, generate a structured diagnostic summary, and mandate an immediate human-in-the-loop review. Results: An analysis of the publicly available BreaKHis dataset demonstrated that the GPA autonomously accepted 2365 cases with a 99.79% accuracy. Based on raw forced-classification logits, the combined system correctly predicted 2368/2373 cases. For the 8 escalated cases, the SPA functioned as an unvalidated reporting adjunct, generating secondary ViT-based metadata for the CRA rather than extending automated clinical sensitivity. Conclusions: The proposed MAS framework effectively orchestrates multi-scale feature extraction, confidence-guided delegation, explainable AI, and LLM-assisted conflict resolution into a unified diagnostic workflow, serving as a robust technical proof of concept for enhancing the dependability and clinical safety of AI-assisted breast histopathology analysis.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Struma ovarii is a rare monodermal ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of mature thyroid tissue. Malignant transformation is uncommon, with papillary thyroid carcinoma representing the most frequent histological type. Owing to its rarity, malignant struma ovarii may present considerable diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when different morphological patterns coexist within the same tumor. Case Presentation: A 63-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with intermittent abdominal pain and a palpable paraumbilical mass. Imaging revealed a complex right adnexal lesion with cystic and solid components. Right salpingo-oophorectomy was performed. Histological examination demonstrated a mature teratoma with struma ovarii showing malignant transformation. The malignant component exhibited a biphasic pattern, comprising approximately 30% classical papillary thyroid carcinoma and 70% invasive follicular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma, with characteristic papillary-type nuclear features. Immunohistochemical findings supported thyroid differentiation. Conclusions: Papillary thyroid carcinoma arising in struma ovarii is an exceptionally rare ovarian neoplasm that may be difficult to recognize clinically and radiologically. The coexistence of classical papillary thyroid carcinoma and an invasive follicular variant within the same lesion further increases the diagnostic complexity. This case highlights the continuing challenges regarding classification, staging, optimal treatment, and long-term surveillance of malignant struma ovarii.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Molecular allergen diagnostics provide detailed information on IgE sensitization profiles, yet large-scale real-world data from Kazakhstan remain limited. This study aimed to characterize molecular food allergen sensitization patterns, age-related differences, and co-sensitization in patients undergoing multiplex allergy testing. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 8504 patients with food allergen sensitization whose ALEX2 results were obtained from the INVIVO laboratory network across Kazakhstan between January 2024 and December 2025. Sensitization was defined as specific IgE ≥ 0.3 kUA/L. The proportion of positive results for each food allergen component was calculated using the full analytical cohort (N = 8504) as the denominator. Age-related differences were assessed using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests with false discovery rate correction. Co-sensitization was evaluated through correlation analysis and hierarchical clustering. Results: The median age was 14 years (IQR, 7–33). The highest numbers of documented positive results were observed for Cuc m 2 (2336/8504, 27.47%) and the combined assay target Fra a 1 + 3 (1611/8504, 18.94%), followed by Mal d 3 (12.97%), Cor a 1.0401 (12.22%), and Zea m 14 (12.10%). The analyzed milk and egg components showed their highest observed positivity proportions in children aged 0–5 years, with significant overall differences across age groups (all BH-adjusted p < 0.001). Peanut, tree nut, and soybean components showed heterogeneous age-related patterns. Co-sensitization analysis identified clusters that included components from the same allergen source or protein family. Conclusions: Molecular food allergen sensitization in this Kazakhstan cohort demonstrated substantial component-specific heterogeneity and age-related differences. Structured co-sensitization patterns underscore the importance of interpreting multiplex IgE results within molecular and clinical contexts. These findings provide regional real-world evidence while emphasizing that sensitization does not establish clinically confirmed food allergy.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Malaria is widespread in tropical and subtropical regions and results in large numbers of deaths, disproportionately in the very young. Recent developments in vaccination have rekindled efforts towards better disease management, with eradication being conceivable. Diagnosis is the critical first step towards treatment and epidemiological monitoring. Current tests have various widely accepted limitations such as the requirement for highly skilled personnel, expensive instrumentation, inadequate sensitivity, and incompatibility with circulating variants. We report our efforts to develop an instrument-free diagnostic that can detect 100 or fewer target DNA copies per reaction and is well suited for use in either the field or clinic. Methods: Here, we develop a set of recombinase polymerase amplification and CRISPR/Cas12a detection assays that each provide sequence sensitivity and specificity. Results: We show detection and differentiation of P. falciparum from all other major human Plasmodium spp. down to tens of copies, with rapid detection of 100 P. falciparum target copies in a blood-containing matrix. Conclusions: We have developed a set of novel and sensitive diagnostic relations for Plasmodium spp. intended for integration into our previously developed handheld point-of-care diagnostic platform. The diagnostic is intended to be inexpensive, to interrupt continued transmission from those carrying low parasitemia burdens, and to detect malaria with deletions in genes encoding the proteins used in lateral-flow antigen diagnostics.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Pulmonary contusion (PC) is commonly seen in blunt chest trauma cases in the emergency department (ED). A PC is indicative of respiratory complications, necessitating early patient diagnosis and management. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) offers a quick bedside imaging modality to assess for injuries such as PC. This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of a simplified POCUS protocol in detecting PC compared to computed tomography (CT) in blunt chest trauma patients. Methods: We conducted a single-center prospective study from October 2021 to November 2025 at the University of California, Irvine Medical Center ED, with 90 patients analyzed. A convenience sample was utilized. Research associates conducted the screening process (e.g., 18–60 years of age; stable trauma status). An available medical student, emergency medicine (EM) resident, EM fellow, or EM attending performed the bedside POCUS procedure using the Mindray TE7ACE machine and was blinded to the clinical examination, CT results, and chest radiograph. A simplified lung ultrasound protocol was used to examine four lung fields—bilateral anterior and posterior—for the number of B-lines. POCUS findings were compared to chest CT results, which was the reference standard, and three or more B-lines in any lung field on POCUS were considered positive for PC in the setting of blunt trauma. Results: Ninety patients (mean age 32.9 years, SD 12.1) were analyzed, 37.8% of whom were female. Motor vehicle collisions were the most common trauma mechanism. Twenty-two patients had PC on CT. The prevalence of PC was 24.4%. In comparing POCUS to CT results, 18 true positives, 55 true negatives, 4 false negatives, and 13 false positives were identified. POCUS demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.8% (95% CI: 59.7–94.8%) and specificity of 80.9% (95% CI: 69.5–89.4%) in detecting PC. Its positive predictive value was 58.1% (95% CI: 39.1–75.5%), and its negative predictive value was 93.2% (95% CI: 83.5–98.1%). Conclusions: POCUS demonstrated moderately high sensitivity and specificity in detecting PC. While POCUS serves as a useful screening tool during the initial trauma assessment, findings do not establish a replacement of CT, and a positive POCUS result can prompt closer monitoring at the cost of monitoring those without PC, highlighting a trade-off between early detection and resource utilization.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Objectives: This study aimed to investigate renal volumetric changes in heart failure using fully automated three-dimensional (3D) CT volumetry and to examine their association with renal function and the progression of renal impairment. Methods: This retrospective study included 131 heart failure patients and 147 non-heart failure controls who underwent chest-abdominal CT. Fully automated 3D kidney segmentation was performed using deep learning-based image analysis software. Kidney volumes were measured and compared between groups. Patients with heart failure were further stratified by renal function (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] ≥ 30 vs. <30 mL/min/1.73 m2), and longitudinal changes were evaluated in those who underwent follow-up CT. Results: Heart failure patients had significantly lower total kidney volumes (median [interquartile range]: 224 [96] mL) compared to the control group (263 [84] mL, p < 0.0001). Among patients with eGFR < 30, the left kidney was numerically smaller than the right (86 [35] vs. 92 [28] mL), but not significantly so (p = 0.0564). Longitudinal follow-up demonstrated significant increases in kidney volume in increased cardiac width cases (n = 20), although congestion was not directly assessed, and kidney volume reduction in patients with a decreased cardiac width (n = 34), without establishing decongestion or renal atrophy. Conclusions: Automated 3D CT volumetry provides an objective assessment of renal involvement in heart failure. Left–right volume differences were exploratory and did not establish predictive value. Prospective studies are needed to determine their clinical significance.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) remains a leading cause of childhood morbidity and mortality worldwide, posing persistent diagnostic and management challenges. Correct, rapid diagnosis is essential, and point-of-care lung ultrasound (LUS) offers a bedside, non-radiating lung evaluation. Methods: This single-center retrospective observational study included 172 children hospitalized with CAP at the Emergency Clinical Hospital for Children “Louis Țurcanu”, Timișoara, Romania. LUS and laboratory testing were performed within 24 h of admission. Associations between LUS severity categories (0–3, 4–6, and 7–9), inflammatory markers, age, and hospital length of stay were analyzed using non-parametric tests and multivariable regression models. Results: Cough was the most frequent clinical sign (98.84%), followed by tachypnea (76.16%), fever, and abnormal breath sounds. LUS abnormalities were identified in 161/172 children (93.6%). CRP concentrations differed significantly across LUS severity categories (p < 0.001), whereas leukocyte count, neutrophil parameters, and CBC-derived inflammatory indices showed no significant association with LUS severity. In an age-adjusted ordinal logistic regression model, higher log-transformed CRP concentrations (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.18–1.81; p = 0.001) and older age (adjusted OR 1.15 per year, 95% CI 1.04–1.28; p = 0.006) were independently associated with higher LUS severity. In a multivariable negative binomial regression model, higher LUS severity and higher CRP concentrations were independently associated with longer hospital length of stay. Conclusions: In hospitalized children with CAP, greater LUS severity was associated with higher CRP concentrations and longer hospital stay, whereas CBC-derived inflammatory indices were not associated with LUS severity. Age and CRP were independently associated with higher LUS severity, while LUS severity and CRP were independently associated with hospitalization duration. These findings support an association between lung ultrasound severity and clinical disease burden but should be interpreted as observational rather than causal. Further prospective studies are required to confirm these results.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Hyponatremia is frequently observed in acute infections and may reflect systemic inflammation and physiological stress. However, its clinical relevance in acute cholangitis remains insufficiently defined. This study investigated the association between admission hyponatremia and Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18)-defined severity of acute cholangitis in patients with common bile duct (CBD) stones. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 2240 patients with imaging-confirmed CBD stones admitted from January 2021 to June 2025. Hyponatremia was defined as serum sodium < 135 mEq/L within 24 h of admission, before biliary intervention. Cholangitis was classified according to TG18. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, microbiological results, emergency ERCP, hospital stay, and discharge disposition were compared by sodium status. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with moderate-to-severe and severe cholangitis after adjustment for conventional markers. Results: Among 2240 patients, 941 had hyponatremia and 1299 did not. Hyponatremic patients more frequently had fever and jaundice, elevated inflammatory and cholestatic markers, and abnormalities in platelet count, prothrombin time, and creatinine. Hyponatremia was associated with higher odds of moderate cholangitis (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.33–1.88) and severe cholangitis (OR 2.72, 95% CI 2.03–3.65). In a separate multivariable analysis, hyponatremia remained independently associated with severe cholangitis (Grade III vs. all others; adjusted OR 1.84, 95% CI 1.35–2.51), but not with moderate-to-severe cholangitis (Grades II–III vs. all others). Patients with hyponatremia more frequently underwent emergency ERCP, had higher culture positivity among those tested, had slightly longer hospitalization, and more frequently experienced adverse discharge disposition. Conclusions: Admission hyponatremia was associated with greater TG18-defined acute cholangitis severity, particularly severe disease, in patients with CBD stones. Serum sodium may be a simple, inexpensive adjunctive marker for early severity assessment.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Engraftment syndrome (ES) is an early inflammatory complication after autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (auto-HSCT), and endothelial activation may contribute to its pathogenesis. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX), derived from routine laboratory parameters, is a practical candidate marker of endothelial-inflammatory stress, but the optimal peri-transplant timing of assessment remains unclear. We hypothesized that patients who subsequently develop ES would exhibit higher peri-transplant EASIX values before clinical onset. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 139 adult auto-HSCT recipients. ES was adjudicated using the Spitzer criteria plus a study-specific infection-exclusion rule: patients with positive blood cultures or procalcitonin > 1 ng/mL from 96 h before through 96 h after neutrophil engraftment were not classified as having ES. EASIX was calculated at conditioning start and daily from day 0 to +15. EASIX+7 was modeled on a log2 scale for the principal association analysis; ROC analysis was exploratory. Results: Thirty-nine patients (28.1%) developed ES. EASIX+7 was available in 104 patients and was higher in ES than non-ES patients (median, 5.92 vs. 4.25; p = 0.018). Each two-fold increase in EASIX+7 was associated with higher ES odds (OR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.05–2.43; p = 0.029), including after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted OR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.04–2.45; p = 0.033). Discrimination was modest (AUC, 0.652; 95% CI, 0.536–0.769). The exploratory cutoff of ≥5.0 yielded 67.9% sensitivity and 65.8% specificity. Conclusions: EASIX+7 was associated with subsequent ES occurrence but showed modest discrimination. It may warrant further evaluation as a practical risk-stratification marker rather than as a stand-alone predictive tool.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Routine preoperative laboratory testing is common in sinonasal inverted papilloma (SNIP), but its broader laboratory profile and population-level differences are poorly characterized. Methods: We assessed 52 fasting preoperative analytes in 284 adults with SNIP and described directional deviations and patient-level burden. Eight shared biochemical markers were compared between 202 SNIP patients aged 45–90 years and 10,457 cancer-history-negative participants from the 2015 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Age- and sex-adjusted models estimated geometric mean and adverse-direction prevalence ratios, with false-discovery-rate correction. Results: Across 14,768 measurements, 1318 deviations were observed (mean, 4.64 ± 2.80 per patient). Triglycerides had the highest within-cohort deviation rate (38.7%), but neither external comparison met the false-discovery-rate criterion. Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and uric acid (UA) were higher in SNIP (adjusted geometric mean ratios, 1.154 and 1.129, respectively), and elevated LDL-C and high UA were more prevalent (adjusted prevalence ratios, 2.461 and 2.134, respectively). Conclusions: External population comparisons prioritized LDL-C and UA over triglycerides as candidate markers for subsequent clinical validation; these observational results do not establish diagnostic utility or causality.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: The main objective of this study was to investigate the associations between maxillary and mandibular incisor inclinations, and sagittal and vertical skeletal parameters in Romanian adults using multivariable regression analysis adjusted for age and sex. Secondly, the aim was to determine differences in incisor inclination among skeletal Classes I, II, and III, providing population-specific data to complement existing international research. Methods: In this retrospective cephalometric study, 187 adult patients (aged 18 years and older; 49.7% female) were selected. Multiple linear regression models were built for Max1-FH (SNA, ANB, S-N/Go-Gn, Ar-Go-Me, age, sex) and IMPA (SNA, ANB, age, sex). Skeletal classes were compared with ANOVA or Kruskal–Wallis tests. Correlations were exploratory. Reliability was excellent (ICC ≥ 0.967). Results: Class II was the most frequent skeletal pattern (48.13%), followed by Class I (36.36%) and Class III (15.51%). In the multivariable models, Max1-FH was independently associated with SNA (B = 0.732, p < 0.001), ANB (B = −0.577, p = 0.001) and Ar-Go-Me (B = −0.279, p = 0.011) (R2 =0.323), whereas IMPA was independently associated with SNA (B = 0.638, p < 0.001) and ANB (B = 1.241, p < 0.001) (R2 = 0.273). Age and sex were not significant in either model. Max1-FH was higher in Class III (120.71° ± 7.24°) than in Class I (114.45° ± 7.81°, p = 0.002) and Class II (114.22° ± 8.70°, p < 0.001). IMPA was higher in Class II (median 97.00°) than in Class I (86.00°) and Class III (87.00°), with no difference between Classes I and III (p = 1.000). Conclusions: In this Romanian orthodontic adult sample, incisor inclinations were independently associated with sagittal skeletal parameters (SNA and ANB), and maxillary incisor inclination was also associated with the gonial angle (Ar-Go-Me), whereas age and sex showed no significant association. Incisor inclination differed among skeletal classes, with greater maxillary incisor proclination in Class III and greater mandibular incisor proclination in Class II.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Machine Learning (ML) models can estimate coronary heart disease risk from structured patient data, but they offer little guideline-based justification for their predictions. Explanations produced by large language models (LLMs) may also contain post hoc rationales when they are not tied to the model’s actual reasoning. We developed CARDIA-TR, a framework in which an ML model makes the diagnostic decision for suspected stable coronary heart disease and an LLM explains it using Turkish and international cardiology guidelines. Methods: Six classifiers were evaluated on the UCI Cleveland dataset (n = 303) with 10 × 5 repeated nested cross-validation, together with a leakage audit of a widely shared version of the dataset. Eight open-source LLMs answered 150 clinical questions using retrieval-augmented generation over 52 guideline documents. Their answers were assessed with automatic metrics, blinded physician ratings, and two LLM judges whose agreement with physician ratings was measured. For 303 patients, the LLMs explained ML decisions based on exact feature contributions and could flag guideline-discordant feature use. A physician scored 80 of these explanations. Results: Logistic regression performed best (ROC-AUC 0.911). Confirming earlier reports, 723 duplicate rows in a widely shared 1025-row version of the dataset explained reported accuracies of up to 100%. Lexical overlap with the sources did not reflect clinical accuracy. Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B received the highest judge and physician scores (physician 1.68 and 1.70 out of 2), but in the physician evaluation they did not differ significantly from Turkish-Gemma-9B. The physician rated all 80 faithful explanations as fully correct, including those for wrong ML predictions. The newer models detected guideline-discordant use of chest pain type caused by referral bias without false alarms (F1 0.986 and 0.935), also when the referral information was removed from the prompt. Conclusions: In this internally validated, referral-based cohort, an LLM explanation layer anchored to the ML model’s reasoning could justify decisions and audit their consistency with clinical guidelines. External validation is needed.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Falls have overtaken road-traffic accidents as the leading cause of traumatic brain injury (TBI), yet most forensic autopsy series describe a single fall mechanism or include fall-related deaths from any cause. We compared the autopsy injury pattern after falls from height and same-level falls among deaths from fall-related TBI, and explored whether the association with the mechanism varied with age. Methods: We reviewed available records from a Romanian institute of forensic medicine, where 8557 autopsies were performed in 2014–2024, and included deaths from TBI after accidental falls, excluding transport-related injuries and suicides. The primary outcome, skull fracture severity (none, simple or complex), was analysed with a partial proportional odds model adjusted for age and sex. Secondary injuries were analysed with modified Poisson and logistic regression, with false discovery rate correction, and reported as adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR). Results: Of 344 decedents (median age 66 years; 82.0% male), 129 had fallen from height and 215 had falls at the same level. A skull fracture was found in 115 of 129 (89.1%) versus 117 of 215 (54.4%) decedents (aPR 1.62, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.41–1.86), and a complex fracture in 97 of 129 (75.2%) versus 14 of 215 (6.5%) (aPR 11.4, 95% CI 6.8–19.1); fractures after same-level falls were mostly simple. The largest differences concerned basal skull fracture (66.7% vs. 6.0%; aPR 10.8), intraventricular haemorrhage (71.3% vs. 7.9%; aPR 8.88) and otorrhagia (55.0% vs. 9.3%; aPR 5.80), three injuries that clustered together after both mechanisms and persisted among deaths within one day of the fall. Brainstem, cerebellar and spinal injuries were also more frequent after falls from height. Subdural haematoma was the most frequent intracranial lesion in both groups (78.3% vs. 67.0%; aPR 1.17, 95% CI 1.03–1.34), and epicranial haematoma was equally frequent (58.1%). There was no evidence that age modified the association of the mechanism with complex or basal fractures; in exploratory analyses, the between-mechanism difference in subdural haematoma appeared smaller at older ages, but evidence for this interaction was inconclusive. Conclusions: In fatal fall-related TBI, a fall from height was associated less with whether the skull fractured than with how it fractured. The co-occurrence of a complex or basal skull fracture, intraventricular haemorrhage and otorrhagia was more prevalent after falls from height, but these population-level associations should not be used alone to infer the mechanism in an individual case; the absence of a fracture does not argue against a fatal same-level fall. Autopsy series recording fall height and antithrombotic medication could clarify the height gradient and the role of age.</jats:p>

Most notably, magnetic perturbations are intentionally applied in tokamaks to suppress edge localised modes (ELMs). However, despite growing confidence in the method, a complete understanding of the process involving all relevant mechanisms is yet to be gained. In this work, we present an integral kinetic plasma response model in the large-aspect-ratio limit capable of appropriately resolving finite Larmor radius effects of ions. Benchmarking against a prior differential model based on a finite Larmor expansion to second order demonstrates the necessity of the integral model due to unphysical modes in the solution of the former. Further, we investigate the isotope dependence of the linear plasma response in both approaches. <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In order to prepare for possible future operation of JT–60SA with tungsten plasma facing components, a H–mode scenario of JT–60SA at high power and high current is considered as reference in order to investigate the tungsten transport behavior and assess the amount of electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) which is predicted to be required in order to avoid central accumulation of tungsten. The modeling is performed with the ASTRA transport code in combination with the TGLF-SAT2 quasi–linear turbulent transport model and with neoclassical transport of impurities computed by the drift-kinetic solver NEO and the FACIT model. The impact of argon as additional seeded impurity is also considered, not only in the core behavior but also on the possibility of achieving tungsten screening in the pedestal region. The main result is that these H–mode conditions in JT–60SA achieve a so far largely unexplored domain of parameters, in which a reactor–like very low collisionality is combined with high rotation levels. In contrast to the usual domain of operation of present medium size tokamaks, where tungsten neoclassical transport is in the plateau to Pfirsch–Schlüter regime, in the predicted JT–60SA conditions toroidal rotation has a beneficial effect in increasing the strength of the temperature screening, enabling operation without any strong central tungsten accumulation and, in the most unfavorable conditions of high tungsten concentration and low rotation, requiring only 2 MW of central ECRH power to avoid locally negative electron heat fluxes in the center. Within the limited predictive capabilities of the present modeling approach for pedestal parameters, a sufficiently large and realistic domain of parameters in terms of argon concentration and plasma rotation, as well as of relative density and temperature logarithmic gradients, can also be expected to lead to the dominance of tungsten temperature screening in the JT–60SA pedestal.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Generating entangled photons from a laser-driven spin provides a promising resource for quantum communication, but their usefulness can depend on how the surrounding nuclear environment evolves during photon generation. We investigate a spin–photon interface driven by finite laser pulses while retaining nuclear-spin dynamics across successive emission cycles. Measurements on the intermediate photons produce conditional endpoint states, whose entanglement, Bell correlations, teleportation fidelity, and expected detection rates are evaluated. By comparing dynamically evolving, frozen-field, and reset nuclear environments, we find that simplified noise models can predict different operating windows for useful teleportation. In particular, the frozen-field approximation may overestimate performance under the conditions studied. Optical branching, imperfect feedforward, and nuclear-register size further constrain these windows. The results establish a task-oriented framework for evaluating photonic resources while highlighting the need for accurate environmental modeling and device-specific calibration.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background and Objectives: Blood pressure (BP) telemonitoring improves hypertension control, but Central-European evidence is scarce and the speed of reaching guideline targets is rarely quantified. We evaluated whether a mobile telemonitoring platform with remote pharmacotherapy titration achieves greater BP reduction and a higher proportion of patients at the 2024 ESC office BP target at 12 weeks than standard outpatient care and explored time-to-target and the distribution of care contacts. Methods: In this two-center, open-label, randomized (1:1) pilot trial, 100 adults aged 18–85 years with uncontrolled hypertension received telemonitoring (STmedical application with validated upper-arm cuff; n = 50) or standard care (n = 50) for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in the change in office systolic/diastolic BP (SBP/DBP); secondary endpoints were target attainment (<130/80 mmHg) at 12 weeks and resource use; time-to-target was exploratory. The pre-specified primary analysis was performed in completers; at the reviewers’ request, intention-to-treat analysis of all randomized participants (multiple imputation for missing 12-week values) was adopted as the primary analysis at revision, with completers as a sensitivity analysis. Results: A total of 45 (90%) telemonitoring and 43 (86%) standard-care participants completed the study. In the intention-to-treat analysis (multiple imputation, missing at random), the adjusted between-group difference in 12-week office SBP was 6.1 mmHg (95% CI 1.8 to 10.4) and in DBP 7.0 mmHg (95% CI 4.0 to 10.0); among completers the differences were 6.3 mmHg (2.0 to 10.7) and 7.2 mmHg (4.2 to 10.1). Office BP <130/80 mmHg at 12 weeks (non-responder imputation) was reached by 72% (36/50) versus 26% (13/50) of randomized participants (risk difference 46.0 percentage points, 95% CI 28.6 to 63.4; RR 2.77, 95% CI 1.68 to 4.56) and by 80% versus 30% of completers. Time-to-target, an exploratory outcome prone to detection bias because home readings were far more frequent with telemonitoring (about 13.1 versus 2.9 per patient-week), favored telemonitoring in the original analysis (Kaplan–Meier median 5 versus 12 weeks; adjusted HR 6.02, 95% CI 3.53 to 10.27); in the separately reported harmonized analysis, which assessed target status only in weeks with at least three home readings in both arms, the adjusted HR was 4.85 (95% CI 2.61 to 9.02) and the restricted mean time not at target was 4.7 weeks shorter (95% CI 3.3 to 6.1). Telemonitored patients had fewer in-person visits (0.6 versus 2.3) but more total clinical contacts (5.7 versus 2.6); 92% of medication adjustments were remote. No hypertensive crisis occurred; 12-week SBP <120 mmHg was observed in 10/45 (22%) versus 2/43 (5%) patients and symptomatic hypotension in 2 versus 0 patients (both in the telemonitoring arm, managed by remote down-titration). Retention at 12 weeks was 88%, and telemonitored patients transmitted on average about 13 readings per week. Conclusions: In this pilot trial, telemonitoring combined with intensive remote titration was associated with greater BP reduction and more patients at target at 12 weeks than standard care. Because the intervention arm also had more frequent measurements, clinical contacts and medication adjustments, the effect cannot be attributed to the application itself, the time-to-target comparison may be affected by detection bias, and no reduction in resource use can be inferred. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in a pre-registered, adequately powered multicenter trial.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Cervical cancer continues to pose a substantial global health burden, underscoring the need for accurate and early diagnostic tools. Although existing studies have demonstrated the feasibility of directly predicting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) scores from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs), the accuracy of these predictions remains limited. In this study, we investigated whether case-matched pairs of HER2 immunohistochemistry (IHC) WSIs and H&E WSIs can improve the HER2 score prediction. Methods: Case-matched pairs of H&E and HER2 IHC WSIs were independently encoded to generate separate sets of patch-level features. Then, within each patient-level cross-validation fold, a fold-specific HER2 IHC teacher was trained using only the IHC WSIs and labels from the four training folds and then frozen to guide a tumor-aware H&E student model through prediction distillation and multi-modal attentive contrastive learning between high- and low-attention patch groups. At the inference stage, the H&E student model predicted HER2 scores without any IHC input. Results: On the independent 126-case internal test set, under H&E-only inference, the proposed residual-fusion model trained on case-matched pairs of HER2 IHC and H&E WSIs achieved an accuracy of 0.6255, a macro-AUC of 0.6218, and a macro-F1 of 0.6103. By comparison, the model trained and evaluated using H&E-only WSIs achieved 0.5654, 0.5974, and 0.5465, respectively. In the separate IHC-assisted setting, when trained and evaluated on both H&E and IHC WSIs, the proposed residual-fusion model achieved an accuracy of 0.8080, a macro-AUC of 0.8685, and a macro-F1 of 0.7852. Although accuracy and macro-F1 were higher for the paired-training configuration under H&E-only inference, the macro-AUC remained modest. Conclusions: These findings suggest that paired IHC and H&E WSIs may provide useful training supervision for HER2 score prediction from H&E WSIs. Before clinical implementation can be considered, the model should be further evaluated in larger, independent, preferably multicenter external cohorts to assess its robustness and generalizability across institutions, scanners, staining protocols, and patient populations.</jats:p>

title: Development of weak signal methodology: Phase diagnostics of changes in management systems

affiliation.name: Autonomous Nonprofit Organization 'Digital Audit'

items.abstract:
<jats:p>Subject. Early diagnostics of structural changes in financial, economic, and managerial systems based on weak signal analysis.
Objectives. To develop a phase-based approach to assessing the sustainability of organizations, enabling the identification of pre-crisis states before they manifest in financial and market indicators.
Methods. A synthesis of methods of systems and morphological analysis, the provisions of nonlinear dynamics, and the concept of weak signals is used.
Results. It is shown that financial sustainability is determined by the configuration of internal and external ties, whereas traditional indicators reflect delayed effects of structural changes. It is substantiated that weak signals capture early shifts in the architecture of interactions and precede the deterioration of financial metrics. A phase model is proposed that interprets the development of
a system as a sequence of stable configurations, and the Fibonacci sequence as an analytical scale of structural thresholds and saturation levels. It is shown that structural dynamics can develop while the statistical stability of indicators is preserved. 
Conclusions and Relevance. The phase-based approach enables a shift from the ex post detection of deviations to the identification of structural preconditions for crisis, reduces the lag of managerial responses, and lays the foundation for anticipatory management. The results are applicable to tasks of financial sustainability diagnostics, risk management, analysis of corporate dynamics, and the development of decision support systems.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a numerical comparison of the temporal and spatial development of an electromagnetic (EM) field inside a metallic shielding enclosure with a rectangular technological aperture subjected to two parallel-polarized HPEM pulses possessing identical peak field strengths but substantially different temporal waveforms. The analysis was performed in CST Studio Suite using the time-domain solver for a PEC enclosure measuring 455 mm × 50 mm × 463 mm with a 30 mm × 80 mm aperture. A subnanosecond Gaussian pulse with a maximum electric field strength of 1 MV/m, a maximum magnetic field strength of 2.68 kA/m, and an FWHM of 0.0804 ns was compared with a trapezoidal nanosecond pulse possessing the same peak amplitudes and rise and fall times as those of the nanosecond Gaussian pulse, but an extended constant-amplitude plateau lasting 1.6 ns, and a total duration of approximately 1.96 ns. The simulation results confirm intuitive expectations that during the initial rising-edge phase, up to approximately 0.18 ns, both pulses produce the same field penetration mechanism through the aperture and lead to the formation of similar electric- and magnetic-field structures. Significant differences emerge only after the maximum amplitudes are reached, when the Gaussian subnanosecond pulse begins to decay, whereas the trapezoidal nanosecond pulse amplitude (plateau) remains constant. Despite its substantially longer interaction time, the trapezoidal nanosecond pulse does not result in a systematic increase in the EM field inside the enclosure interior. During the long plateau period, the enclosure interior divides into two field areas. The first area, concentered near the aperture, is static and does not affect most of the enclosure’s interior. In this large area, unaffected by the static field, only the EM waves move toward the extremes of the enclosure’s interior. This area is called the dynamic area. EM waves in the dynamic area are the result of the rise and fall periods of the trapezoidal nanosecond pulse (similar case as to the Gaussian subnanosecond pulse). This shows that a longer pulse with an amplitude plateau does not play an important role in the excitation of the enclosure interior. This means that the usefulness of a longer pulse for causing stronger EM interference is doubtful. This information has practical value for manipulating the EM field.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Shielding performance inferred from attenuation or nominal thickness can misrepresent the response of a finite semiconductor detector. This study uses Geant4 to map energy deposited in a silicon sensor of dimensions 20 mm × 20 mm × 0.5 mm behind polyethylene (PE) and PE–aluminium (PE–Al) shields under controlled photon, electron, and proton fields. Event-level scoring separates primary survival, residual entry energy, shield-generated secondaries, and finite shield coverage. The proton response was strongly non-monotonic near range-out: effective suppression occurred between 8–9 mm PE at 30 MeV and between 20–25 mm PE at 50 MeV, in agreement with NIST PSTAR projected ranges. For photons, short shield-to-sensor gaps increased silicon energy deposition, consistent with enhanced acceptance of shield-generated secondaries. At the final 100 mm gap, adding 0.5 mm Al to 25 mm PE improved the photon-response reduction by 3.083 ± 0.558 percentage points under the reference physics list; the uncertainty is a two-sided 95% sampling confidence-interval half-width and excludes physics-model uncertainty. An XCOM narrow-beam calculation gave 1.01 percentage points of additional uncollided primary-photon number removal, a different observable that cannot be subtracted from the detector-response change to quantify a secondary contribution. A finite-size test further showed that oblique protons could traverse an edge-clipped path in a nominally thick shield. Within the discrete candidate set, 25 mm PE was the lowest-mass configuration with positive mean response reduction in all four benchmark fields. These results define transport and geometry regimes that should be checked before a shielding design is advanced to mission-specific modelling or experimental qualification.</jats:p>

<jats:p>Subject. This article discusses the organizational and methodological approaches for diagnosing the economic safety state of nuclear industry construction organizations. 
Objectives. The study aims to develop methodological approaches for diagnosing the state of economic security, taking into account industry specifics in the field of nuclear power plant construction.
Methods. For the study, I used the methods of systems approach, theoretical analysis and classification, as well as structural analysis.
Results. The article reveals the limitations of traditional approaches for diagnosing the economic safety of the nuclear industry, and outlines five key features that determine the specifics of the nuclear power plants construction.
It also develops an author's system of indicators to offset the existing limitations in traditional approaches, proposes calculation formulas and thresholds.
Conclusions. The proposed author's indicators make it possible to take into account industry-specific features and improve the efficiency of diagnosing the state of economic security. The research results can be helpful for the economic safety departments of construction organizations in the nuclear industry.</jats:p>

title: Gamma-ray shielding performance of polystyrene composites reinforced with cadmium and bismuth oxides
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The development of lightweight, non-toxic, and flexible radiation shielding materials is critical for modern medical, aerospace, and industrial applications where conventional lead and concrete shields are impractical. In this study, polystyrene-based composites reinforced with cadmium oxide and bismuth oxide at weight fractions ranging from 5 to 25 wt% were fabricated via a solution casting technique. The macroscopic structural integrity of the composites was confirmed through bulk density measurements, indicating the absence of large-scale voids and ensuring the physical suitability of the samples for subsequent attenuation experiments. Gamma-ray attenuation measurements were conducted experimentally using a narrow-beam geometry and a sodium iodide doped with thallium scintillation detector across the energy range of 0.511–1.765 MeV. The experimental results were validated against theoretical calculations using the XCOM database, showing excellent agreement with relative deviations predominantly below 5%. The linear attenuation coefficient increased systematically with filler concentration, with bismuth oxide consistently outperforming cadmium oxide due to its higher atomic number of 83 versus 48, which enhances photoelectric absorption in the low-to-intermediate energy regime. At 0.662 MeV, the 25 wt% bismuth oxide/polystyrene composite achieved a linear attenuation coefficient value of 0.1239 cm⁻
                    <jats:sup>1</jats:sup>
                    , representing an 11.7% enhancement over the 25 wt% cadmium oxide/polystyrene composite. This highest concentration formulation demonstrated a half-value layer of 5.60 cm and a shielding efficiency of 11.65% at a fixed thickness of 1 cm at 0.662 MeV, marking a 26.7% reduction in required thickness and a 34% improvement in efficiency compared to pure polystyrene. Benchmarking against conventional materials revealed that the 25 wt% bismuth oxide/polystyrene composite has an areal density of 7.62 g/cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , making it 11.0% lighter than ordinary concrete while approaching the weight efficiency of lead, alongside offering superior flexibility and significantly lower toxicity compared to conventional lead and cadmium-based alternatives. These findings establish polystyrene–bismuth oxide composites as a promising, lead-free alternative for next-generation radiation shielding in weight-sensitive and environmentally conscious applications.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Saliva is an attractive non-invasive biofluid for systemic monitoring, but its complex composition can mask disease-specific signals. Salivary extracellular vesicles (EVs) have been proposed as an additional source of biomarkers of the metabolic dysregulation of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet whole saliva and salivary EVs have rarely been analyzed in parallel in the same individuals. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 22 normoglycemic controls and 42 patients with T2DM with acceptable (HbA1c ≤ 8%; n = 20) or poor (HbA1c > 8%; n = 22) glycemic control. Unstimulated whole saliva was differentially ultracentrifuged for EV separation. The obtained EV-enriched preparation was characterized by nanoparticle tracking analysis, transmission electron microscopy and EV-associated markers. Exploratory label-free proteomics was performed on donor pools from a subset matched for age and sex, and selected candidates were quantified by multiplex immunoassay in individual paired samples (n = 34) using linear models adjusted for age, sex and body mass index (BMI), with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Results: In the pooled discovery analysis, complement- and coagulation-related proteins showed higher relative abundance in both matrices from poorly controlled patients. After adjustment, EV concentration did not differ between groups, and complement C9 was the only analyte that remained elevated after multiplicity correction in both matrices in poorly controlled patients (BH-corrected p = 0.004) and, in whole saliva, also in patients with acceptable control (BH-corrected p = 0.049). C9 concentrations were strongly correlated between matrices (ρ = 0.84), and no group-by-matrix interaction was detected for any analyte. No difference was detected between patients with poor and acceptable control. Conclusions: Whole saliva and salivary EV-enriched preparations yielded concordant information, and whole saliva appears to be the more practical matrix. Salivary C9 should be regarded as a preliminary candidate biomarker associated with T2DM status, and requires confirmation in larger, independent cohorts balanced for age and BMI.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: This retrospective exploratory study described unadjusted differences in complete blood count (CBC) parameters according to smoking, alcohol consumption, sex, age, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based HPV status. Methods: The analytic sample included 624 patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and 479 hospital-based controls. Reference-midpoint-normalized red blood cell parameters differed by sex, while smoking, alcohol consumption, and age were associated with selected leukocyte and platelet differences. Results: In the small oropharyngeal subgroup (12 HPV-positive and 94 HPV-negative cases), selected CBC parameters also differed by PCR-based HPV status. Because the analyses were univariate, used nominal p-values without multiplicity correction, and did not control for correlated clinical and exposure variables, the findings are provisional and do not establish independent effects, causality, diagnostic accuracy, prediction, or prognosis. Conclusions: Future studies should prespecify adjustment for patient-related factors when evaluating CBC-derived markers in HNSCC.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>A sigma-cavity laser configuration, consisting of ring and linear sections, is known to provide stable single-frequency (SF) generation. However, using an Er-doped fiber laser as an example we demonstrate that in addition to typical stable SF generation self-sweeping can occur even with moderate isolation of ∼37 dB provided in the ring section by a standard circulator. We demonstrate that the generation regime—SF stabilization, self-sweeping, or multi-frequency operation—can be controlled by introducing additional losses in the laser cavity. Depending on the specific point of the cavity where the losses are introduced, the sweeping rate can either increase or decrease with attenuation variation. The observed regimes are explained in terms of an extremely weak counter-propagating wave forming gain dynamic population grating in the ring section of the cavity. The results provide new insights into mode dynamics in sigma-cavity fiber lasers. They can be of use both for the task of mode-hopping suppression required for stable SF operation and for the task of controlling the self-sweeping rate for applications requiring wavelength tuning.</jats:p>

title: Effect of diode laser (532 nm) and Helium – Neon laser (632.8 nm) on the Activity of White Blood Cell

items.abstract: <jats:p>It is widely recognized that low-level laser irradiation affects immune system cells in various ways, one of which is enhancing the phagocytic activity of the treated cells. This study has been established to shed light on the possible effect of laser irradiation on phagocytic activity of W.B.Cs. Fresh blood samples have been obtained from 50 healthy adults volunteers for phagocytosis assay. The activity of W.B.C for whole blood have been measured at (5, 15, 30, 60, 90 and 120) min before and after exposure to laser He-Ne laser (632.8nm), Diode laser (532nm) irradiation. The present study revealed a significant increase in the mean activity of phagocytosis after exposure to 632.8 nm and 532nm, this activity further increased by increasing exposure time. The laser irradiation by 532 nm has been much more efficient; 30 minutes irradiation with 532 nm reached comparable and produced even better effects on the improvement of blood activity than the 60 min irradiation with 632.8 nm at significant level (P<0.05). The W.B. Cs count has been significantly increased by using 632.8 nm and 532 nm irradiation compared with non-irradiated group. (P<0.05). In conclusion, the current study suggests that low level laser can increase the phagocytic activity of W.B. Cs, and this increase is proportional to increasing the exposure time.</jats:p>

title: A comparison of classical machine learning and vision language models for TB diagnostics
