items.abstract: <jats:p>Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge, and timely diagnosis is essential for effective treatment and disease control. Automated analysis of chest X-ray images using machine learning has shown strong potential for supporting clinical diagnostics. Previous studies using hyperparameter-optimized machine learning algorithms, including convolutional neural networks (CNN), support vector machines (SVM), and decision trees, have achieved high classification performance on TB chest X-ray datasets, with accuracies exceeding 98%. In this work, we extend these investigations by evaluating the performance of a fine-tuned vision–language model (VLM) for tuberculosis classification and comparing its performance with traditional machine learning approaches. The study uses a publicly available TB chest X-ray dataset and evaluates models using standard clinical performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, precision, F1-score, and specificity. Traditional optimized models such as SVM, CNN, and decision trees achieved accuracies of 99.58%, 99.50%, and 98.33%, respectively. The proposed VLM-based approach achieved a test accuracy of 99.67%, with precision, recall, and F1-score values of 0.9967. These results demonstrate that fine-tuned transformer-based VLM architectures can achieve performance comparable to, and slightly better than, optimized classical machine learning models for TB chest X-ray classification. The findings highlight the potential of VLMs for AI-assisted medical imaging diagnostics and future multimodal clinical decision-support systems.</jats:p>

title: Diagnostics of the sustainable development of industrial enterprises in the monitoring system of the regional economy

affiliation.name: Lugansk Vladimir Dahl State University

items.abstract:
<jats:p>Subject. Diagnostics of the sustainable development of industrial enterprises as the primary level of monitoring of the regional economy.
Objectives. To propose and test a two-block methodology for diagnosing the sustainable development of industrial enterprises, to substantiate its calculated parameters – the weights of indicators, threshold criteria for scoring and the scale of interpretation of the integral index, to determine the possibilities of applying aggregated results in regional industrial monitoring.
Methods. The research is based on system, process, resource, and risk-based approaches. The assessment was based on fixed documentary criteria, normalization, calculation of partial and integral indices, and sensitivity analysis. Equal weights of indicators and blocks are accepted in accordance with the principle of insufficient foundation.
Results. A methodology is proposed that combines eight organizational and eight economic indicators, partial, integral and aggregated indexes, and eight analytical contours. The zone of permissible deviation ±5% when converting indicators into points and a five-level equal-interval scale of interpretation of the integral index are substantiated. The methodology is applicable to assess the sustainable development of enterprises, their cross–industry comparison and identification of risk areas, and the diagnostic results are used to justify management decisions and targeted measures of regional industrial policy.
Conclusions. A joint review of organizational and economic indicators makes it possible to determine which factors contribute to the sustainability of each enterprise. Even with similar values of the integral index, enterprises differ in the composition and severity of the identified limitations. The aggregated index characterizes only the surveyed population and is not an assessment of the entire industrial complex of the region.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>During the operation of the tokamak device, the high heat load released by the core plasma instability events severely affects the structure and performance of tungsten-based divertor materials. For the expected Type I ELMs in future long-pulse steady-state fusion devices, the coaxial gun discharge plasma parameters are designed to simulate the characteristics of low-medium energy density. Under constant initial conditions (discharge frequency, gas-prefilled), the total accumulated heat flux is kept constant by varying the energy density and the number of pulses. By combining the plasma-material interaction process, the temperature evolution of tungsten (W) target under different heat loads and its damage effects are comparatively studied. The results show that when the total energy is fixed, the thermal deposition time scale and the instantaneous temperature gradient lead to different types of damage, including roughening, grain loss, blistering, crack networks, and cracking accompanied by melting. Low-energy-density multi-pulse impacts cause slow heat deposition and small temperature gradients, increasing surface roughness via cyclic thermal stress. High-energy-density impacts involving only a few pulses cause rapid heat deposition and steep temperature gradients, inducing high thermal stresses that lead to blistering and cracking. The energy density of an individual pulse determines the transition from surface to bulk damage. These results suggest that peak heat load control should take priority over cumulative heat flux limitation in the service design of W targets for fusion devices.</jats:p>
